providers.description: Bright Machines is a San Francisco-based software-defined manufacturing company founded in 2018 by Amar Hanspal and Lior Susan that builds a full-stack intelligent automation platform for electronics and AI-infrastructure assembly. Its Microfactory pairs modular Bright Robotic Cells with Brightware, a platform operating system that orchestrates hardware, runs a machine-vision "Smart Skills" perception stack, and provides manufacturing-execution services for work orders, material management and real-time production KPIs. Bright Data, the company's data layer, unifies component, process and enterprise-system data through secure APIs and auditable data flows, and Bright Designer turns product CAD into assembly-ready digital twins using NVIDIA Omniverse on Microsoft Azure. The company has raised roughly $279M from Eclipse, BlackRock, NVIDIA, Microsoft, Jabil and others. All platform and data interfaces are delivered to customers under commercial engagement; Bright Machines publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs or machine-readable API contracts.

providers.name: Lightelligence
providers.description: Lightelligence (legal entity Shanghai Xizhi Technology Co., Ltd. / 曦智科技, founded 2017 as an MIT spin-out) builds optoelectronic hybrid computing hardware — photonic accelerators and optical interconnect fabric for AI and high-performance computing. Its product line is physical: the PACE 2 optoelectronic accelerated computing card (a PCIe Gen4 x16 accelerator built around a 128x128 optical matrix multiplier), the Gazelle optical computing evaluation board, the Photowave CXL optical interconnect, and the Lightsphere X distributed optical circuit switch, supported by the company's oMAC, oNOC and oNET optical core, network-on-chip and inter-chip network technologies. The software surface is a device-side stack — ONNX, OpenCL, PyTorch and TVM support plus a Python SDK (lt_sdk) that compiled and ran models on the optical processing unit — not a web API. As of this profile the company publishes no public web API, no OpenAPI/AsyncAPI/GraphQL contract, and no developer portal; the lightelligence-sdk package and its Read the Docs reference have both been withdrawn. Its remaining public developer-facing surface is a GitHub organization of chip design and verification tooling (Bazel Verilog build rules, RTL/UVM linters, the yis interface-spec generator) and an Optical Computing Developer Community of research cases and papers.

providers.name: proteanTecs
providers.description: proteanTecs is an Israeli deep data analytics company for advanced electronics. It embeds on-chip monitoring Agents (UCT, margin, path margin, I/O and power monitors) into semiconductor designs and pairs them with cloud and edge machine-learning applications that report health, performance, reliability and quality of chips and systems from design through production test into field operation. Solutions cover power and performance optimization, RAS, functional safety and diagnostics, chip production, system production and advanced packaging, and are consumed by semiconductor, data center, AI/HPC, automotive, telecom and mobile customers. The company markets APIs and data connectors for integrating its analytics with ATE testers and third-party analytics tools, but publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Verve Motion
providers.description: Verve Motion is a wearable robotics company spun out of the Harvard Biodesign Lab that builds SafeLift, a soft powered exosuit for industrial workers who lift repetitively. Inertial sensors woven into the suit detect lifting motion and trigger assistive force that the company says takes up to 40% of the strain off a worker's back, while Verve Logic — its cloud platform — collects the resulting movement data and reports ergonomic risk, unsafe-posture trends and exosuit utilization to safety managers. SafeLift is sold as a subscription bundling the exosuit, the Verve Logic data portal and Verve Care support, and is distributed in part through partners such as HexArmor. Verve Motion publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable specification; the Verve Logic portal at logic.vervemotion.com is a customer-only single-page application that disallows crawling in robots.txt.

providers.name: Botrista
providers.description: Botrista, Inc. is a San Francisco based beverage-automation company founded in 2017 that builds the DrinkBot robotic beverage dispenser and the CloudBar cloud platform behind it. The DrinkBot automates craft beverages — infused teas, flavored lemonades, iced coffees and mocktails — dispensing a drink in roughly twenty seconds from a touchscreen order, and every unit is internet connected so it pulls recipes, reports consumption, tracks ingredient levels and pushes maintenance alerts back to Botrista. CloudBar is the operator-facing web application used by restaurant, campus dining, convenience and theme-park operators to manage recipes, inventory replenishment and sales/menu performance analytics across a fleet of machines, alongside a separate Botrista Data Portal. Botrista sells beverage automation as a service rather than as a developer platform: as of this profiling pass it publishes no public developer portal, no API reference and no machine-readable API contract, and POS integrations are handled case-by-case through its commercial team.

providers.name: Ferro Corporation
providers.description: Ferro Corporation is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Ferro Corporation API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Modular Robotics
providers.description: Modular Robotics is a Boulder, Colorado hardware and educational-robotics company best known for Cubelets, magnetic modular robot construction blocks organized into SENSE, THINK, and ACT categories, and the MOSS building system. It also produces the Dexter Industries STEM product line, including the GoPiGo Raspberry Pi robot, BrickPi (LEGO Mindstorms plus Raspberry Pi), GrovePi, and the micro:bit GiggleBot. The company sells physical robotics kits and companion apps such as the browser-based Cubelets Console with Blockly and C coding rather than a public HTTP API; programmatic access is provided through first-party open-source Python driver libraries published on PyPI and maintained under the official DexterInd GitHub organization.

providers.name: Quaise Energy
providers.description: Quaise Energy is a deep-geothermal energy company and MIT spinout, founded in 2018 by Carlos Araque and Matthew Houde out of a decade of millimeter-wave research by Paul Woskov at the MIT Plasma Science and Fusion Center. Quaise is developing millimeter-wave (MMW) drilling — using a gyrotron to vaporize rather than grind rock — to reach supercritical conditions several kilometers down, where temperatures approach 500 degrees C, and to convert existing fossil-fuel power stations to superhot geothermal baseload. The company drilled 100 meters with the technique at its Central Texas field site in 2025. Quaise is an energy and hardware company: it publishes no developer program, no public API, and no machine-readable API contract. Its only public web application is a levelized-cost-of-energy (LCOE) calculator whose full functionality sits behind an AWS Cognito login.

providers.name: Sanctuary AI
providers.description: Sanctuary AI is a Vancouver, British Columbia humanoid robotics company on a mission to create and deploy industrial-grade general-purpose humanoid robots to help address growing labor challenges. Its flagship product is Phoenix, a bipedal humanoid robot designed for dull, dirty, and dangerous work in automotive, manufacturing, and logistics environments. Phoenix is driven by Carbon, Sanctuary AI's proprietary AI control system that mimics human cognitive subsystems — memory, sight, sound, and touch — to translate natural-language tasks into dexterous physical actions. The company is vertically integrated, designing everything from motors and actuators through to generative AI algorithms in-house. Co-founded by James Wells (CEO) and Olivia Norton (CTO/CPO), Sanctuary AI has a private GitHub organization with no public repositories, no developer portal, no public API, no SDK, and no published OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specifications. The commercial model is hardware sales and enterprise deployments; Carbon is a proprietary on-board system and there is no public developer surface.

providers.name: EyeLights
providers.description: EyeLights is a French deep-tech company building augmented reality head-up display (HUD) technology for riders and pilots. Its products project GPS navigation, speed, intercom, radar and call information into the rider's line of sight: EyeRide, a universal HUD accessory compatible with any motorcycle helmet; the GT-AIR 3 Smart, an integrated head-up display visor built into a SHOEI helmet; the APEX HUD glasses for general aviation; and Pulse Ultra, a universal Bluetooth intercom. The company sells direct-to-consumer through a Shopify storefront at eye-lights.com and runs customer support on Odoo. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio lead; EyeLights publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time, so this record captures its consumer web, identity, and security posture rather than an API contract.

providers.name: KLA
providers.description: KLA Corporation (formerly KLA-Tencor) is a leader in process control and process-enabling solutions for manufacturing wafers and reticles, integrated circuits, packaging, printed circuit boards and flat panel displays. KLA delivers advanced inspection tools, metrology systems, and computational analytics for the semiconductor industry. KLA does not publish a public developer portal or open API program; customer-facing software and tool APIs are provided to KLA customers under contract and are not publicly available.

providers.name: Segway-Ninebot
providers.description: Segway-Ninebot is a global personal-transportation and robotics company, formed when Ninebot acquired Segway in 2015. It designs and manufactures electric kickscooters (the world's top-selling e-kickscooter brand, 13M+ units sold across 100+ countries), self-balancing personal transporters, e-bikes, and — through its Robotics division — RMP mobile-robot chassis and delivery/service robots (Nova Carter, NVIDIA Isaac-powered developer kits). Backed by HongShan. Its public developer surface is limited to Segway Robotics' open-source ROS / NVIDIA Isaac integration packages on GitHub; no first-party REST or OpenAPI product API is currently published.

providers.name: Ai Fabrik
providers.description: AI Fabrik is an infrastructure company building an edge inference delivery network for high-performance AI tokens. Incubated within Gruve and led by founder Tarun Raisoni alongside Swati Deshpande and Tanuj Mohan, the company has deconstructed the traditional data center model and rebuilt every layer for real-time AI, delivering distributed inference close to users and cloud providers with sub-20ms latency, cost efficiency, and built-in compliance. AI Fabrik is deploying five initial production sites with 6,000+ B300 GPUs launching in 2026, backed by Mayfield, Xora (Temasek), Acclimate Ventures, and Cisco Investments.

providers.name: Athos
providers.description: Athos is a sports performance technology company founded in 2012 and based in Redwood City, California, that builds athletic apparel with embedded surface electromyography (EMG) sensors. Its garments and snap-on Athos Core module capture muscle activity, effort, and motion data, streaming it over Bluetooth to a mobile app and coaching dashboard so athletes, trainers, and sports scientists can measure muscular exertion, fatigue, and return-to-play readiness in real time. Athos is a consumer and team hardware brand with no publicly documented developer API; this profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and enriched for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: CelLink
providers.description: CelLink (CelLink Technologies / CelLink Corporation) manufactures large-format, high-conductance flexible circuits that consolidate power, data, and sensing into thin, lightweight layers, replacing traditional wire harnesses and busbars. Its product lines are Battery Pack Interconnect, Flex Harness, and Data Center power delivery, serving automotive, aerospace, industrial, data center, and grid-storage electrification markets. Founded by CEO Kevin Coakley and VP Engineering Malcolm Brown, the company is headquartered in San Carlos, California, with sites in Georgetown, Texas; Wixom, Michigan; Hamburg, Germany; and Shanghai, China. CelLink circuits have been in electric-vehicle production since 2020. CelLink is a hardware manufacturer and publishes no public developer portal, API, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Diraq
providers.description: Diraq is a quantum computing company headquartered in Sydney, Australia, with offices in Palo Alto, California and Boston, Massachusetts. Spun out of UNSW Sydney in 2022 by Professor Andrew Dzurak, Diraq builds quantum processors from silicon spin qubits — quantum information encoded in the spin of single electrons held in quantum dots formed inside structures derived from conventional CMOS transistors, so the qubits can be fabricated on standard semiconductor foundry lines. The company works with imec, NVIDIA and Quantum Machines, has advanced through DARPA's utility-scale quantum computing initiative, and targets a first commercial processor toward the end of the decade. Diraq is a pre-commercial hardware and research organization: as of this profile it publishes no developer program, public API, SDK, or machine-readable contract of any kind, and its stated commercial pathway — cloud access to its processors — is still on the roadmap rather than in market.

providers.name: Gradiant
providers.description: Gradiant is a global water and wastewater infrastructure company founded in 2013 out of MIT and headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts, that designs, builds and operates end-to-end industrial water systems from intake to discharge. It positions itself as "the Water Layer of the AI Economy", supplying ultrapure water, process water, wastewater recycling, minimal- and zero-liquid-discharge and resource-recovery systems to semiconductor fabs, AI data centers, energy producers and applied industries including pharmaceuticals, mining, food and beverage, refining and chemicals, textiles and renewables. Its proprietary technology portfolio includes Counterflow Reverse Osmosis (CFRO), Semi-Batch Reverse Osmosis (SBRO), Carrier Gas Extraction (CGE), Selective Contaminant Extraction (SCE), Free Radical Oxidation (FRO), Bio Infinity, the ForeverGone PFAS destruction process, the HyperSolved data-center cooling-water platform, the CURE Chemicals specialty-chemicals line and SmartOps AI, a machine-learning platform for optimizing and predicting plant operations. Gradiant raised a Series E at a $2 billion valuation in May 2026. It is an industrial equipment, chemicals and build-own-operate services company: it publishes no public developer portal, no developer API, no SDK and no machine-readable API contract, and SmartOps AI is delivered as a customer-facing operations platform rather than as a public API.

providers.name: Jays
providers.description: JAYS is a Swedish consumer audio brand founded in 2006 by Jens and Johan, headquartered in Sweden and owned by the Northbaze Group AB. It designs and sells wireless and wired headphones, true-wireless earbuds, Bluetooth and multiroom speakers, and audio accessories, sold direct-to-consumer through a Shopify storefront at jaysheadphones.com. JAYS publishes no first-party developer API; its only machine-accessible surface is the Shopify-provided agent-commerce layer: a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profile with a hosted MCP shopping endpoint, Customer Account OpenID Connect / OAuth discovery documents, and an llms.txt. This profile was surfaced as a Creandum portfolio/commitment lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: NanoLumens
providers.description: NanoLumens is an American designer and manufacturer of direct-view LED (dvLED) displays and video walls, headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia and founded in 2006 by Rick Cope. It builds fixed and flexible indoor and outdoor displays in custom sizes, shapes and curvatures across the Engage Pro, Engage, NXT, Nixel, NanoPanel 55, Captivate, Performance, CLRVision, CLRVU and NanoBanner product lines, together with Aurora video processing and the NanoSuite display-management software. Its displays are deployed in retail, casinos, higher education, sports and arenas, control rooms, hospitality, themed entertainment, government, corporate and transportation environments. The software side of the business — the AWARE platform and NanoSuite, powered by the ISAAC ecosystem — markets a JSON REST API and webhook-based alerting for remote diagnostics, content scheduling and display-fleet monitoring, but that API is delivered to display owners through an authenticated tenant and has no public developer portal, API reference or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Polymateria
providers.description: Polymateria Ltd is a British materials-science company, based at the Imperial College I-HUB on the White City Campus in London, that develops Biotransformation — a masterbatch additive blended into polyethylene and polypropylene at roughly 2% by weight so that plastic which escapes a waste stream weathers into a bioavailable wax and fully biodegrades in the open environment without leaving microplastics behind. The company co-authored BSI PAS 9017, the first standard for measuring the biodegradability of polyolefins, is a World Economic Forum Technology Pioneer and a Terra Carta signatory, and sells to converters, brand owners and packaging manufacturers rather than to developers. Its product is a chemical additive, not software: the public website is a WordPress marketing and media site, and the only credentialed surface it operates is a customer portal that serves third-party test datasets as documents. No developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable API contract of any kind was found in this pass.

providers.name: Saphlux
providers.description: Saphlux is a quantum dot Micro-LED (QD-MLED) display technology company founded in 2014 out of Yale University and headquartered in San Diego, California, with additional operations in China and Japan. It commercialized semi-polar (20-21) GaN-on-sapphire epitaxial wafers to address efficiency droop and the green gap in nitride emitters, and now mass-produces NPQD quantum-dot Micro-LED devices. Its product lineup spans QD-COB and QD-COB Pro Series panels for large-format commercial and home-theater displays and the T-Series monolithic full-color micro-displays for all-day wearable AR eyewear and AI smart glasses. Saphlux is a semiconductor materials and display-module manufacturer that sells hardware to OEMs and display integrators; it publishes no public developer program, API, or SDK.

providers.name: TRIDITIVE
providers.description: TRIDITIVE is an automated additive manufacturing company founded in 2016 and headquartered in Meres, Asturias, Spain, with offices in Hartford, Connecticut and London. It builds the AMCELL family of automated industrial 3D printing machines (Amcell 1300, 4300, 8300, Bulkam), the Traced traceability system, and the EVAM Software platform for additive manufacturing workflow management, digital warehousing, and on-demand production of polymer and metal parts. A Techstars portfolio company, TRIDITIVE publishes no public API, developer portal, or client SDKs as of July 2026.

providers.name: Atom Power
providers.description: Atom Power, Inc. is a Charlotte, North Carolina electrical technology company founded in 2014 that invented the Atom Switch, the world's first commercial UL-listed digital solid-state circuit breaker. The company builds SiC (silicon carbide) power modules, solid-state switchgear and panel-level Level 2 electric-vehicle charging hardware for commercial, industrial, data-center and grid-edge deployments, paired with cloud software for energy management, load balancing and charger operations. Atom Power previously ran an "Atom Cloud" developer portal on Azure API Management at developers.atompower.com with a gateway at api.atompower.com; both hostnames are now dangling CNAMEs to deleted Azure API Management instances, so no public API contract is currently reachable.

providers.name: Empower Semiconductor
providers.description: Empower Semiconductor is a fabless power-semiconductor company founded in 2014 and headquartered in San Jose, California, with an R&D office in Munich. It designs integrated voltage regulators (IVRs), silicon capacitors (ECAP) and vertical power-delivery platforms for AI, high-performance computing and embedded systems, built on its FinFast architecture combining FinFET-based design, advanced packaging, advanced magnetics and integrated silicon capacitors. Its Crescendo platform targets kilowatt-class vertical power delivery for AI and HPC processors and its Forte family delivers multi-domain integrated regulation up to 25W. Analog Devices completed its acquisition of Empower Semiconductor on 7 July 2026. Empower ships silicon, not software: it publishes no developer portal, no public API, and no machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Iontra
providers.description: Iontra Inc. is a Denver, Colorado battery technology company that develops proprietary Charge-Control technology for rechargeable lithium batteries. Founded in 2013 and publicly launched in 2022, Iontra applies electrodynamic sensing and signal processing during charging to suppress lithium plating, dendrite growth and SEI-layer expansion, claiming up to 4x cycle life, 2x faster charging, improved cold-weather charging and better safety without changing cell chemistry. The technology is chemistry agnostic across Li-ion, Li-metal, Li-S, solid-state and Na-ion cells, and is delivered to OEMs as custom charging algorithm "recipes" flashed onto an application-specific microcontroller, or as a software-only library. Iontra closed a $45M Series C led by Volta Energy Technologies to launch an integrated RISC-V charge-control and fuel-gauge MCU. Iontra is an embedded/silicon company: it publishes no public web API, no OpenAPI, and no public SDK packages — its SDK is firmware delivered to OEM customers through a login-gated Document Portal under commercial engagement.

providers.name: MayMaan Research
providers.description: MayMaan Research is a clean-energy engineering company that redesigns the internal combustion engine around its patented AquaStroke platform, a piston engine that runs on a blend of roughly 70% water and 30% bio-alcohol (ethanol or methanol) instead of gasoline or diesel. The company builds modular generator sets and powertrains that scale from a 35 kW unit (A35) through the AV2 to multi-megawatt installations, and it positions them as drop-in replacements for diesel gensets in power generation, EV charging infrastructure, data centers, telecommunications, marine, construction, agriculture, defense and off-grid deployments, with near-zero NOx, SOx, CO2 and particulate output. MayMaan is headquartered in Hollywood, Florida with a European office in Paris, holds engine and fuel-system patents internationally, and raised a $30 million Series A led by WAVE Equity Partners. It is a hardware manufacturer: as of this profile it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable interface of any kind.

providers.name: Phasecraft
providers.description: Phasecraft is a quantum algorithms company building software that combines classical and quantum computing to solve real-world problems in materials discovery, advanced biochemistry, and optimization. Its algorithms are engineered to run efficiently across multiple quantum hardware platforms, and its published results include scalable approaches to the Fermi-Hubbard model and QAOA-based optimization. Founded by Profs. Ashley Montanaro (CEO) and Toby Cubitt (CTO), the company operates from London, Bristol, and Washington DC, and is backed by Playground Global. Phasecraft exposes no public developer API; its programmatic surface is limited to open research code on GitHub and two interactive web tools (a materials database and an optimization graph library).

providers.name: Photoneo
providers.description: Photoneo is a Slovak (Bratislava, founded 2013) machine-vision company and a global pioneer of high-resolution structured-light 3D measurement. Its flagship products are the PhoXi 3D Scanner family and the MotionCam-3D, a parallel structured-light camera that captures moving scenes in real-time 3D, together with AI-enabled software such as Bin Picking Studio, Locator, and Palletizing for robotic automation. Rather than a hosted web/REST API, Photoneo exposes a developer surface through the PhoXi Control software and its official C++, C#, and Python device APIs, GenICam/GigE Vision standard connectivity, TCP/IP robot interfaces (UR, ABB, FANUC, Staubli, Mitsubishi, Kawasaki, Yaskawa), and a set of BSD-licensed example repositories on GitHub. Documentation lives in the Photoneo Knowledge Base (docs.photoneo.com) and the 3D scanning wiki. Photoneo (now part of the Brightpick Group) was acquired by Zebra Technologies.

providers.name: actnano
providers.description: actnano, Inc. is a Massachusetts-based advanced materials company that develops and manufactures PFAS-free protective nanocoatings for electronics. Its flagship Advanced nanoGUARD technology is a gel-state, 100% fluorine-free conformal coating applied to printed circuit board assemblies, connectors, antennas, LEDs and high-heat-generating components, delivering up to IPx8 moisture and condensation protection without trapping heat or degrading signal integrity. Founded in 2012 and headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, with a Munich center of excellence and operations in Mexico and Japan, actnano serves mobility and automotive electronics, consumer electronics, AI and data-center infrastructure, solar, industrial electronics, medical devices and optical anti-fog applications. The company states REACH and RoHS compliance and ISO 9001:2015 certification, and is backed by BMW i Ventures, Porsche Ventures and Emerald Technology Ventures. actnano is a materials manufacturer: it publishes no public developer program, API, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Chelsio Communications
providers.description: Chelsio Communications designs and sells high-performance Ethernet network adapters and ASICs — the Terminator (T4/T5/T6/T7) Unified Wire family — for virtualized enterprise datacenters, hyperscale public and private clouds, cluster computing, GPU-accelerated computing and high-frequency trading. Its 1/10/25/40/50/100GbE adapters fully offload TCP, iSCSI, FCoE, iWARP RDMA and NVMe-oF onto a single chip with single firmware, and the sixth-generation T6 ASIC adds integrated cryptography offload for IPsec/TLS/SSL/DTLS. Chelsio distributes Unified Wire driver packages for Linux, Windows, FreeBSD and VMware ESXi plus the Unified Wire Manager management software as downloads from its service portal; it publishes no public developer program, REST API or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Fortune Brands Innovations
providers.description: Fortune Brands Innovations is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Fortune Brands Innovations API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Whill
providers.description: WHILL, Inc. designs and manufactures enhanced personal mobility solutions — electric power chairs and mobility scooters, including the Model C2, Model F, the Modo Breeze ultralight foldable wheelchair, and the Model R three- and four-wheel scooters — and operates an autonomous personal mobility service that has completed over 700,000 rides worldwide across airports and other venues. WHILL was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this writing it is a consumer hardware and mobility-service company and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile is maintained as a company record and will be enriched if WHILL launches a developer program.

providers.name: Unspun
providers.description: Unspun is a fashion-technology company building Vega, the world's first 3D weaving machines, which transform yarn directly into finished woven garments in about twenty minutes for automated, localized, on-demand apparel manufacturing. Founded by Beth Esponnette, Walden Lam, and Kevin Martin and operating from Oakland, California and Hong Kong, the company pairs its weaving hardware with software for custom-fit patternmaking and design automation, working with manufacturers and brands to eliminate overproduction, with a mission of reducing global human carbon emissions by one percent. Unspun is backed by DCVC and does not currently publish a public API or developer program.

providers.name: Apeel
providers.description: Apeel (Apeel Sciences) is a food technology company founded in 2012 and headquartered in Goleta, California. It produces a plant-derived, edible coating, made from lipids and glycerolipids found in the peels, seeds and pulp of produce, that is applied to fresh fruit and vegetables at packing houses to slow water loss and oxidation, extending shelf life and reducing food waste across the supply chain. Apeel-treated produce is sold through grocery retailers in multiple countries. In 2021 Apeel acquired ImpactVision and added hyperspectral imaging to its supplier installations to grade interior quality, ripeness and freshness. Apeel is a materials-science and supply-chain operator: as of this profile it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, machine-readable API contract, or self-serve developer sign-up.

providers.name: Lightberry
providers.description: Lightberry is a San Francisco robotics software company (Y Combinator Fall 2025) that builds conversational AI "personality" software for humanoid and quadruped robots. Its platform lets a robot listen, speak, see its surroundings, and act on natural-language instruction without the owner writing any code, emphasizing emotional intelligence, contextual awareness, and autonomy rather than a simple speech-to-text voice pipeline. Lightberry ships pre-installed on robots sold through its partnership with Unitree, and the company runs a manufacturer-compatibility program with robot makers including Fourier, Booster Robotics, and High Torque. Its published documentation today covers device setup (power-on, WiFi provisioning, starting a conversation) plus an MCP architecture note describing a Model Context Protocol server that routes tool calls to individual Lightberry devices, which each expose a REST endpoint. There is no public developer portal, API reference, SDK, or OpenAPI definition at this time.

providers.name: Rabbit
providers.description: Rabbit Inc. is a consumer technology company building AI-powered devices, best known for the Rabbit R1, a $199 handheld AI companion with industrial design by Teenage Engineering. The R1 runs rabbitOS and centers on a Large Action Model (LAM) that automates tasks across operating systems and applications (DLAM), alongside features like the Magic Camera, voice recording with transcription, and vibe-coded "creations." Rabbit is a portfolio company of a16z. As of this profile, Rabbit is a consumer hardware and device company with no publicly documented developer API, SDK, or developer portal; its public surface is a marketing site, support center, blog, and newsroom.

providers.name: SquareTrade (Allstate)
providers.description: SquareTrade, an Allstate company, provides consumer product protection plans and extended warranties for smartphones, electronics, appliances, furniture, and other goods, marketed in North America as Allstate Protection Plans. It serves more than 140 million customers through partnerships with major retailers and mobile carriers across the US, Europe, Japan, and Australia, handling plan registration, claims filing, same-day repairs, and in-home service. SquareTrade was surfaced as a portfolio company of bain-capital-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation; its digital surface is consumer- and partner-facing (plan portal, claims, partnerships).

bands.label: Minimal
bands.blurb: Index entry only; little beyond a description and a link.

providers.name: MagnusMetal
providers.description: Magnus Metal (MagnusMetal Ltd.) is an Israeli advanced-manufacturing company bringing metal casting into the Industry 4.0 era with its patent-pending Digital Casting System. Founded in 2017 and headquartered at the Revadim Industrial Park in Kibbutz Revadim, Israel, the company builds machines that combine additive-manufacturing and casting principles: a slicer designs a ceramic mold layer by layer and solid alloy is deposited into each layer, so parts are produced from widely available solid metals rather than powders and with no hard tooling. The company markets the process for powertrains, engines, industrial machinery and structural components, claiming removal of 6-18 weeks of tooling lead time, up to 70% raw-material savings and roughly 50% lower energy use. Magnus Metal is a hardware and materials manufacturer - it sells castings and casting systems, not software - and publishes no public developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: Motorola
providers.description: Motorola (motorola.com) is the consumer mobile-device brand operated by Motorola Mobility, a Lenovo company, producing Android smartphones (moto g, moto edge, and razr foldable lines), tablets, and accessories sold worldwide. It was originally added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio stub. On review, the consumer brand publishes no open public REST/HTTP API developer portal: the historical developer.motorola.com Moto Mods hardware SDK (for the modular Moto Z) is no longer reachable, and no OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, or well-known discovery surface was found. Enterprise and public-safety APIs are offered separately by Motorola Solutions, Inc. (docs.motorolasolutions.com), a distinct company, under a gated partner Application Developer Program.

providers.name: Pragmatic
providers.description: Pragmatic Semiconductor Limited is a UK semiconductor manufacturer that designs and produces FlexICs - ultra-thin, physically flexible integrated circuits built on thin-film transistor (TFT) technology rather than conventional crystalline silicon. Founded in 2010 by Richard Price and Scott White and headquartered at Cambridge Science Park with manufacturing at Pragmatic Park in Sedgefield, County Durham, the company operates the Pragmatic FlexIC Foundry, a service that takes third-party custom flexible IC designs from tape-out to delivery in roughly six weeks. Product lines include the FlexIC Platform Gen 3 mixed-signal flexible ASIC design flow, Pragmatic NFC Connect and Pragmatic NFC Protect. The company raised a $231M Series D in 2023. Its only network-reachable API surface is the undocumented, authentication-gated backend of its customer portal; it publishes no developer program, no machine-readable contract and no public API reference.

providers.name: Terra CO2
providers.description: Terra CO2 Technology is a Golden, Colorado climate-technology and building-materials manufacturer that produces low-carbon replacements for Portland cement. Its commercial product, OPUS SCM, is a supplementary cementitious material that replaces up to 50% of the Portland cement in a concrete mix as a drop-in substitute for legacy SCMs such as fly ash, cutting CO2 by roughly 70% and NOx by roughly 90% per ton replaced, and it is produced from abundant silicate feedstocks rather than coal-plant by-products. A second product, OPUS ZERO, targets a full zero-carbon cement replacement and is in concrete trials. The company runs a pilot and materials R&D facility in Golden and is building a 240,000-ton-per-year commercial plant in Cleburne, Texas, backed by more than $250M raised from climate and construction investors including Cemex Ventures. Terra CO2 sells physical material into the construction supply chain; it publishes no developer program, no public API, and no machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: 1QBit
providers.description: 1QB Information Technologies Inc. (1QBit) is a quantum computing software company founded in 2012 and headquartered in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada. It builds hardware-agnostic algorithms and software for optimization, simulation, and machine learning that run across quantum, quantum-inspired, and classical high-performance computing hardware, with work spanning computational finance, life sciences and quantum chemistry, materials, and telecommunications. 1QBit has hardware and platform partnerships with D-Wave, Fujitsu, IBM, and Microsoft Azure Quantum, and participates in DARPA's Quantum Benchmarking Initiative (QBI) on automated design tools for utility-scale quantum computation. The company markets a 1Qloud optimization platform whose own marketing page cites Python SDK, gRPC, and REST API interfaces, but as of August 2026 1QBit publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable API contract — the former portal.1qbit.com host no longer resolves and access is arranged through industry partnerships. Its only public developer surface is a small GitHub organization of research code plus two first-party Python libraries on PyPI.

providers.name: ConnectDER
providers.description: ConnectDER is a Philadelphia-based clean energy hardware company and the leading US manufacturer of meter socket adapters (MSAs, also called meter collars) for the residential market. Founded in 2011 as Infinite Invention LLC after a DOE SunShot Incubator grant, it builds plug-and-play devices that install at the utility meter socket to interconnect distributed energy resources — rooftop solar, battery storage and EV charging — without panel upgrades, line-side taps or circuit relocations. Its product line is the IslandDER MSA (a microgrid interconnect device for solar-plus-battery and whole-home backup, integrated by SolarEdge, FranklinWH, Lunar Energy, EcoFlow and Fox ESS), the Solar MSA and the EV MSA. ConnectDER helped author UL 414 Supplements A, B and C, the standards governing meter socket adapters, and has surpassed 40,000 devices installed across US utility territories including PG&E, SCE and SDG&E. ConnectDER publishes no public developer API, SDK or machine-readable API contract; its devices communicate with partner battery systems over discrete hardwired sensing, control and status signals rather than a network interface. It does publish an llms.txt at its web root.

providers.name: Hadrian
providers.description: Hadrian (Hadrian Automation) is a Los Angeles-area precision-manufacturing company founded in 2020 by Chris Power, building software-driven, AI-powered factories that produce high-tolerance machined components for the aerospace and defense industrial base — including parts for rockets, satellites, jets, drones, and missiles. The company's core software stack is Opus, described as a full-stack, AI-powered Factory Autonomy platform that interprets legacy engineering designs, automates CNC machining, inspection, tool-path optimization, adaptive programming, scheduling, and quality assurance, and enables new operators to be productive in 30 days or less. Hadrian operates multiple factories — Factory 2 (F2) and Factory X (FX) in Torrance, California, and Factory 3 (F3) in Mesa, Arizona — and offers three commercial models: precision component manufacturing, Manufacturing-as-a-Service (dedicated automation cells for a single customer), and Factories-as-a-Service (turnkey factory design and operation). Customers and partners include major aerospace and defense primes such as Lockheed Martin. Hadrian has also launched an additive manufacturing division to expand U.S. defense production capacity. The Opus platform is internal-only — Hadrian sells finished precision parts and factory capacity, not software access — and there is no public developer API, SDK, GitHub organization, or open-source release for Opus or any Hadrian system.

providers.name: Neurophos
providers.description: Neurophos is an Austin, Texas semiconductor company, spun out of Duke University in 2020, building photonic AI inference silicon. Its Optical Processing Unit (OPU) integrates over a million micron-scale dynamic optical metasurface modulators — technology descended from metamaterials research — onto a single chip, performing the matrix multiplications behind AI inference in light rather than electrons. The company markets the T100 OPU as a drop-in data-center alternative to GPUs, publishing chip and server configurations rated at 235 TOPS/W with HBM-backed memory, and lists Triton and JAX as supported software frameworks. Neurophos raised a $110M Series A in January 2026 led by Gates Frontier with M12, Carbon Direct, Aramco Ventures and Bosch Ventures. It sells hardware, not software services: there is no developer program, no public API and no SDK. The only machine-readable surfaces at its domain are an llms.txt and the Wix-platform site MCP endpoint that llms.txt advertises.

providers.name: Photonic
providers.description: Photonic Inc. is a Vancouver, British Columbia deep-tech company founded in 2016 by Dr. Stephanie Simmons and led by CEO Dr. Paul Terry, building distributed, fault-tolerant quantum computing and quantum networking on silicon T centre spin-photon qubits. Its "Entanglement First" architecture couples qubits that compute, store and emit telecom-band photons natively, so individual modules can be entangled over ordinary telecom fibre rather than scaled inside a single dilution refrigerator, and its SHYPS QLDPC error-correction codes cut the physical-qubit overhead of fault tolerance. Backed by Microsoft, British Columbia Investment Management Corp, RBC and TELUS, selected for Stage B of DARPA's Quantum Benchmarking Initiative, and intending to deliver quantum computing through Azure and private systems. As of this profile Photonic is pre-commercial from an integration standpoint: it publishes no API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: Speedata
providers.description: Speedata is a Tel Aviv-based semiconductor company that builds the APU (Analytics Processing Unit), a processor purpose-built for accelerating Apache Spark SQL, batch ETL and AI data-preparation workloads rather than graphics or model training. The APU ships as the C200 PCIe Gen5 accelerator card powered by the company's Callisto ASIC, paired with a software layer called Dash that plugs into the Spark Catalyst optimizer and offloads compute-intensive stages to the card with no application code changes. Founded in 2019 by researchers in multi-threaded coarse-grained reconfigurable architecture, the company raised a $44M Series B in June 2025 (total funding ~$114M) from Walden Catalyst Ventures, 83North and Koch Disruptive. Speedata publishes no public web API, developer portal or machine-readable API contract; its programmatic surface is a Spark plugin JAR distributed under an early-access program, plus a free browser/CLI Workload Analyzer for estimating acceleration on a customer's own Spark workloads.

providers.name: Xperi
providers.description: Xperi Inc. (NYSE: XPER) is an entertainment technology company whose licensed technologies power audio, video, and media discovery experiences across connected cars, consumer electronics, pay-TV, and streaming media platforms. Its brands include DTS immersive audio, HD Radio digital broadcast radio, IMAX Enhanced certification, and the TiVo video platform. Xperi ships its technologies to automakers, device makers, and video providers through commercial licensing and integration programs rather than a public developer API; no public developer portal or API documentation was found, though its TiVo engineering organization maintains an open-source presence on GitHub.

providers.name: Aiko Solar
providers.description: Aiko Solar (Zhejiang Aiko Solar Energy Co.) is a solar photovoltaic manufacturer specializing in high-efficiency solar cells and modules, best known for its ABC (All Back Contact) module technology for residential, commercial, industrial, and utility-scale applications. A BloombergNEF Tier 1 manufacturer, the company reports 200 GW+ accumulative cell and module shipments and mass-production cell efficiency around 25%. This is a hardware manufacturer with no public developer or API surface; the profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: Cashify
providers.description: Cashify is an Indian re-commerce platform for buying, selling, and repairing used and refurbished consumer electronics — smartphones, laptops, tablets, and other gadgets. Founded in 2013 and headquartered in Gurugram, the company provides instant online price quotes, free doorstep pickup with on-the-spot payment for devices sold to it, and sells certified refurbished devices backed by warranty. Alongside its consumer website and mobile apps, Cashify operates a network of physical retail stores across India, runs device repair services, and offers a partner program for retailers. It is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners among other investors. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a company lead and has been enriched with identity and domain-security artifacts.

providers.name: Chemify
providers.description: Chemify is a Glasgow-based programmable-chemistry company, spun out of the University of Glasgow in 2022 by chemist Lee Cronin, that digitizes the creation of molecules through what it calls "Chemputation." The platform fuses AI/ML-driven molecular design, a universal chemical programming language, and robotic synthesis so pharmaceutical, biotech, and industrial partners can move from a novel concept to a makeable compound end to end. In 2025 Chemify opened its first Chemifarm, a fully automated chemistry facility in Glasgow's Maryhill district that pairs its molecular-design engine with industrial-scale robotic synthesis, and closed a $50M Series B co-led by Wing Venture Capital and Insight Partners, with backing from DCVC. Chemify does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation, or SDKs; engagement runs through its partner program.

providers.name: Chipstack
providers.description: Chipstack is an AI-driven semiconductor verification company that uses agentic AI to automate chip design verification, one of the most time-consuming stages of building a complex chip (often 60% or more of total development effort). Its product suite is a set of specialized AI agents — a Mental Model AI Agent, a Formal AI Agent, a Unit Simulation AI Agent, and a UVM AI Agent — that read design intent and generate, run, and reason about verification tasks to shift that work earlier in the design cycle and cut the time and resources it takes to tape out. Founded and based across Seattle, WA and San Jose, CA, and backed by Khosla Ventures, Chipstack is an enterprise, demo-request product rather than a public developer platform: as of this profile it publishes no public API, developer documentation, SDK, or developer portal. In 2026 the company announced it is joining Cadence. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for discovery and monitoring.

providers.name: E-Peas
providers.description: e-peas is a Belgian fabless semiconductor company founded in 2014 in Louvain-la-Neuve that designs power management integrated circuits (PMICs) for energy harvesting, enabling battery-free and battery-assisted IoT devices to power themselves from ambient energy. Its flagship Ambient Energy Manager (AEM) family harvests from photovoltaic (light), thermal, vibration/piezoelectric, radio-frequency, and hybrid multi-source inputs, and the company also develops ultra-low-power microcontrollers for autonomous data acquisition. e-peas positions itself as a pioneer of the "Ambient IoT" concept serving smart buildings, industrial IoT, consumer electronics, and wearables, with an ecosystem of 30+ partners including Panasonic, TDK, Vishay, and Silicon Labs. This is a hardware/silicon company that does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or API documentation.

providers.name: Ergatta
providers.description: Ergatta is a connected-fitness company that makes game-based home rowing machines, pairing WaterRower-derived water-resistance hardware handcrafted in Rhode Island with a gamified software platform of interactive challenges (Endeavor, Meteor, Wavelength), live and on-demand races, scenic rows, coached classes, and custom workouts. Ergatta sells the Luxe and Lite rowers plus upgrade kits for existing WaterRower and Concept2 machines, delivered through a Shopify-hosted direct-to-consumer storefront with a membership subscription. Ergatta does not publish a public developer API; this API Evangelist profile captures its public web surface and identity for network discovery.

providers.name: Jiobit
providers.description: Jiobit is a real-time GPS tracking device company owned by Life360, based in San Mateo, California. Its lightweight (18g) wearable tracker is designed for kids, pets, seniors, and adults, combining LPWA CatM1 cellular, GPS, WiFi, and BLE for location accuracy of 1-50 feet, up to 30 days of battery life, geofence and SOS/911 emergency alerts, and tamper-proof, government-level encryption. Jiobit is a consumer hardware and mobile-app product sold direct-to-consumer with a monthly connectivity subscription; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company discovery and monitoring.

providers.name: Kandou
providers.description: Kandou (Kandou AI) is a fabless semiconductor company founded in 2011 by Amin Shokrollahi and headquartered in Lausanne, Switzerland. It designs high-speed, energy-efficient chip-to-chip interconnect technology built on its proprietary Copper MIMO / Chord Signaling architecture, which turns noise in copper channels into usable bandwidth for massively scalable AI systems. Products include the Glasswing chiplet interconnect IP, the Regli PCIe retimer, the Matterhorn USB4 retimer, the Zetti PCIe switch, and AI Fabric memory/networking platforms. Chord signaling has been adopted into JEDEC and OIF industry specifications. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners across multiple rounds, Kandou raised a $225M round in March 2026 led by Maverick Silicon with strategic participation from SoftBank, Synopsys, Cadence, and Alchip. This is a hardware/semiconductor IP company with no public REST/GraphQL API, SDK, or developer platform surface.

providers.name: Marshall
providers.description: Marshall is a Swedish-British consumer audio brand, part of Marshall Group AB, known for its iconic guitar amplifiers and a modern line of Bluetooth speakers, wireless headphones, and earbuds. Built on more than 60 years of live-music heritage, Marshall sells direct-to-consumer through marshall.com across amps, home and portable speakers, and personal audio. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a consumer portfolio company of HongShan. Marshall publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation at this time; this profile captures its public web identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Mesodyne
providers.description: Mesodyne is an MIT-founded engineering and manufacturing company (established 2018) that builds the LightCell, a patented thermophotovoltaic power generator which converts liquid and gaseous fuels — gasoline, diesel, propane, jet fuel, and hydrogen — directly into silent electricity with more than ten times the energy density of batteries. Designed for military, tactical, drone, and off-grid use, it operates day or night across extreme environments with low heat and emissions signatures and no routine maintenance. Mesodyne publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile captures the company identity and its domain-security posture.

providers.name: Movandi
providers.description: Movandi is an RF semiconductor company founded by former Broadcom executives (CEO Maryam Rofougaran and CTO Reza Rofougaran) that designs 5G mmWave chipsets, RF front ends, phased-array antenna modules, 5G smart repeaters, and beamforming software for terrestrial and non-terrestrial networks. Based in Irvine, California and backed by Sierra Ventures, the company holds 130+ patents covering millimeter wave semiconductor, system, and software technologies spanning 5G, fixed wireless, and satellite connectivity. Movandi is a hardware/semiconductor vendor and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal surface.

providers.name: Nanotronics
providers.description: Nanotronics (rebranded to CubeFabs in 2025) builds AI-driven inspection, process-control, and automation systems for advanced industrial manufacturing, with a focus on semiconductors, data centers, EV/automotive, and aerospace/defense. Its "AI factory" platform combines optical imaging, machine learning, and robotics to improve manufacturing precision, yields, and cost efficiency for customers including Hologic, Broadcom, Coherent, and Standard BioTools. Surfaced as a founders-fund portfolio company; no public developer/API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Omnitron Sensors
providers.description: Omnitron Sensors designs advanced MEMS (micro electro mechanical systems) sensors using innovative 3D manufacturing techniques, aiming to deliver high-performance, low-cost sensing with major gains in precision and reliability. Its technology targets AI data centers, autonomous systems and vehicles, environmental and climate monitoring, and extended reality (XR) devices. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network, the company is a hardware/semiconductor business with no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: One Five
providers.description: One Five (styled one.five) is a sustainable packaging technology company based in Holm, Germany that pairs an AI-driven decision platform, Quartermaster, with ready-to-use recyclable and compostable packaging products. The Quartermaster platform embeds product-market-fit and material analysis into packaging development to accelerate material scouting and packing trials, helping consumer brands cut R&D spend, improve customer acquisition efficiency, and meet emerging packaging regulations while reducing environmental impact. One Five ships flexible sustainable packaging for categories such as dishwasher tablets and gummies through partners including Bluemorph and Glassleaf, and is backed by Speedinvest. The company offers no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Quantum Circuits
providers.description: Quantum Circuits, Inc. is a quantum computing hardware company (a Yale University spinout) building superconducting quantum systems with built-in error detection. Its dual-rail cavity qubits pair Quantum Error Detection (QED), Real-Time Control Flow (RTCF), and Error Detection Handling (EDH), and its Aqumen Seeker QPU (introduced November 2024) targets stable, repeatable, fault-tolerant quantum computation. The company engages early users through a Strategic Quantum Release (SQR) program that includes a simulator and access to Aqumen Seeker systems, rather than a public self-serve API. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Reach
providers.description: Reach Power (Reach Labs) is a Y Combinator-backed (S2015) wireless power company building long-range wireless energy distribution networks, aiming to "do for power what Wi-Fi did for data." Its patented, AI-driven power-beaming systems use adaptive metamaterial antennas to steer electromagnetic waves and deliver electricity through the air to multiple devices simultaneously, scaling from microwatts to kilowatts across both mobile and stationary transmitters. Reach serves defense and intelligence, manufacturing and logistics, and public safety markets, powering autonomous vehicles, industrial robotics, sensors, and drones. Partners and customers include the U.S. Department of Defense, NASA, DARPA, the U.S. Army and Air Force, Aisin/Toyota, and Panasonic. The company is headquartered in San Francisco. As of this profile, Reach publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this is a hardware and energy-infrastructure company rather than an API platform.

providers.name: Sakuu
providers.description: Sakuu Corporation is a Silicon Valley advanced-manufacturing company that builds commercial-scale printing equipment for the battery and supercapacitor industries. Founded in 2016 as KeraCel and renamed Sakuu in 2021, it develops the Kavian platform — a dry-process electrode printing system that produces cathodes and anodes without solvents or drying ovens, covering NCA, NCM, LFP, LTO, graphite and silicon-graphite chemistries as well as sodium-ion, aluminum-ion and solid-state formulations. Kavian was named a TIME Best Invention of 2024 and a Fast Company World Changing Idea of 2025, and the Kavian 2000 platform is sold to battery makers serving AI data centers, energy storage, two- and three-wheel mobility, aerospace and industrial electrification. Sakuu sells capital equipment and process technology; it does not operate a software product, a developer program, or any public API.

providers.name: SmartMore
providers.description: SmartMore Corporation (思谋科技) is a Hong Kong- and Shenzhen-headquartered industrial AI and machine vision company founded in 2019, building products and solutions for smart manufacturing and digital innovation. Its flagship SMore ViMo platform bundles ViMo Cloud, ViMo Deeplearning and ViMo Studio into a low-code industrial vision stack covering data management, model training, visual solution design and production-line deployment, and is sold alongside first-party hardware — industrial smart cameras, barcode readers (VS600/VS800P/VS1000/VS2000), vision sensors (VN2000/VN4000) and lenses — through the SmartMoreInside sub-brand. The company also markets digital platforms (Light3D, Data, Gauge, AIoT) and industrial large models (IndustryGPT, SMore LrMo). SmartMore states it has filed 400+ global patent applications with 200+ granted, served 200+ enterprise customers, and reached unicorn status on a Series B that exceeded USD 200 million in 2021, with R&D and business centers in Hong Kong, Shenzhen, Shanghai, Suzhou, Tokyo, Beijing, Hangzhou and Singapore. As of this pass the company publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable contract; ViMo model export to an SDK is described in marketing copy but is delivered with the licensed product rather than documented publicly.

providers.name: Tensordyne
providers.description: Tensordyne (formerly Recogni) builds next-generation AI inference systems from the foundation up — a proprietary logarithmic-math architecture cast into custom 3nm silicon, compute hardware, scale-up interconnect, and system software. Its flagship Napier platform targets the fastest, lowest-cost, most energy-efficient generative AI inference for hyperscaler and neocloud data centers, delivering 608 PFLOPS dense compute per rack in an air-cooled 30 kW pod and supporting MoE models, agentic workloads, and 4K video generation. The stack integrates with PyTorch, Triton, vLLM, and Kubernetes; a developer SDK is announced as coming soon. Backed by Mayfield, Bosch Ventures, Toyota Ventures, GreatPoint Ventures, and Plug and Play, the company has raised more than $211M and operates from Sunnyvale, California and Munich, Germany.

providers.name: versatile.ai
providers.description: Versatile is a construction-technology company building AI-powered crane intelligence for jobsites, primarily serving steel erectors and general contractors. Its CraneView hardware device attaches to a crane's hook block and passively captures operational data, which the Control Center software turns into real-time insight on pace, progress, productivity, and delays without asking crews to change how they work. The company is backed by Insight Partners. As of this profile Versatile publishes no public API, SDK, or developer platform; this record captures its identity, published web properties, and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Vita Inclinata
providers.description: Vita Inclinata Technologies is a Colorado-based hardware company that builds physics-based load stabilization systems for helicopter hoists and construction cranes, eliminating the dangerous spin and sway of suspended loads. Its ecosystem spans Vita Aerospace (helicopter and rescue hoist stabilization), Vita Industrial (crane and construction load control), Air Rescue Systems (hoist training and products), and the Vita Rescue System used in military MEDEVAC operations. The company is Techstars-backed. It was surfaced as a portfolio-company lead and added to the API Evangelist network; as a physical-hardware manufacturer it currently publishes no public developer API, SDK, or technical integration surface.

providers.name: W. R. Grace
providers.description: W. R. Grace & Co. is a global producer of specialty chemicals and specialty materials, providing catalysts and process technologies to refining, petrochemical, and other manufacturers. Grace operates in two segments: Catalysts Technologies (fluid catalytic cracking catalysts, additives, and process technologies) and Materials Technologies (silica-based engineered materials for pharmaceutical, food, coatings, and industrial applications). Grace's Fine Chemical Manufacturing Services division provides active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) development and manufacturing for the pharmaceutical industry. W. R. Grace does not offer a public developer API for software integration.

providers.name: Fuchsia
providers.description: Fuchsia is an AI-native hardware certification and compliance platform ("Vanta for hardware") that helps hardware teams get products to market faster by streamlining regulatory testing and certification. The platform maps the applicable standards for a product (FCC, CE, UL, FDA 510(k), ISO, RF & EMC, environmental, and functional-safety categories), auto-generates the lab-ready technical documentation and test plans required for certification, connects teams with qualified testing labs specialized in their product category, and tracks compliance progress to surface blockers early. Fuchsia uses AI agents to manage the compliance workflow end to end — from design through testing and certification — including direct communication with testing labs, aiming to democratize regulatory compliance that has traditionally favored larger companies with dedicated compliance teams. Founded in 2025 and part of the Y Combinator Spring 2026 batch, Fuchsia is based in the San Francisco Bay Area and targets robotics, medical-device, IoT, and consumer-hardware builders. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company; as of this enrichment pass Fuchsia publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Hark
providers.description: Hark is an artificial intelligence lab founded in 2025 by Brett Adcock (founder of Figure AI and Archer Aviation) and headquartered in San Jose, California, building what it calls "the most advanced personal intelligence in the world" — proprietary agentic, multimodal foundation models paired with purpose-built, AI-native consumer hardware intended to act as a universal interface between a person and their digital life, with speech, text, vision and persistent personal memory. The company emerged from roughly eight months of stealth in March 2026 and announced a Series A of more than $700 million at a $6 billion post-money valuation in May 2026, led by Parkway Venture Capital with participation from NVIDIA, AMD Ventures, Intel Capital, Qualcomm Ventures, Salesforce Ventures, ARK Invest, Brookfield, Greycroft, Align Ventures, Prime Movers Lab and Tamarack Global. As of August 2026 Hark is pre-product: the platform is in closed beta behind a request-access form, and the company publishes no developer portal, no developer documentation, no public API, no SDKs and no machine-readable contract of any kind on its own hosts. hark.com is a four-page marketing site (home, careers, privacy policy, and a single announcement article).

providers.name: Levita Magnetics
providers.description: Levita Magnetics is a Mountain View, California medical device company, founded by minimally invasive surgeon Dr. Alberto Rodriguez-Navarro and co-founded by Nicolas Luksic, with an additional office in Santiago, Chile. It develops Magnetic Surgery — the Levita Magnetic Surgical System, in which an external magnet placed on the patient's skin controls a shaftless detachable retractor to enable reduced-port laparoscopic procedures — and the MARS (Magnetic-Assisted Robotic Surgery) platform launched in 2023, an FDA-cleared surgical robotic system used in abdominal and, more recently, pediatric procedures. The MARS platform is built on RTI Connext (the DDS real-time connectivity standard) internally, and Levita has demonstrated AI-guided autonomous camera control during surgery. Levita ships regulated surgical hardware and its embedded control software to hospitals; it operates no public developer program, publishes no API documentation, and exposes no machine-readable API contract on any host it controls.

providers.name: Puzzle Medical Devices
providers.description: Puzzle Medical Devices Inc. is a Montreal, Quebec based clinical-stage medical device company founded in 2018 by Jade Doucet-Martineau, Gabriel Georges and Francois Trudeau. It develops ModulHeart, a modular percutaneous mechanical circulatory support pump for patients with advanced heart failure, anchored in the descending aorta to reduce cardiac afterload and improve renal perfusion. ModulHeart holds FDA Breakthrough Device Designation and has completed a first-in-human study. The company is a hardware manufacturer, not a software vendor - it publishes no developer program, API reference, SDK or machine-readable contract. Its only agent-reachable surface is a Model Context Protocol endpoint provisioned automatically by Wix, its website host, which serves public site content rather than any product capability.

providers.name: 24M
providers.description: 24M Technologies is a battery technology company founded in 2010 out of MIT laboratories and headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts. Rather than manufacturing cells at scale itself, 24M licenses its battery materials, cell architecture and SemiSolid manufacturing platform to energy-storage system integrators, EV battery manufacturers and OEMs worldwide. Its product portfolio spans the Eternalyte electrolyte (ultra-fast charging and low-temperature performance), the Impervio separator (thermal-runaway prevention), the LiForever electrode, the 24M ETOP electrode-to-pack architecture, and 24M production equipment. Partners and corporate investors have included Volkswagen Group, Kyocera, Itochu and FREYR Battery. 24M is a hardware, materials and manufacturing company; it publishes no public developer API, SDK or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: CHIPS Alliance
providers.description: CHIPS Alliance is a Linux Foundation project (founded in 2019) that develops open-source hardware (silicon) and tools, including CPUs, SoC subsystems, peripherals, IP blocks, and FPGA tooling. The Alliance fosters collaboration among 50+ member organizations across industry (AMD, Antmicro, Google, Microsoft, SiFive, Intel, Nvidia, Cisco, Synopsys, Microchip, SanDisk and others) and academia (Berkeley, Stanford, MIT, and more) to lower the cost of hardware design, accelerate innovation in silicon, and provide an open and accessible alternative to proprietary EDA flows. CHIPS Alliance hosts more than a dozen technical projects including Chisel (Hardware Construction Language), F4PGA, Caliptra (Root of Trust), VeeR (RISC-V cores), Surelog/UHDM (SystemVerilog parsing), and the FPGA Interchange format. The Alliance does not publish a centralized REST API; technical assets are distributed via GitHub repositories under github.com/chipsalliance and member-driven mailing lists.

providers.name: Forge Nano
providers.description: Forge Nano is a materials-technology manufacturer headquartered in Thornton, Colorado that commercializes particle and wafer Atomic Layer Deposition (ALD) under its Atomic Armor platform and patented ALDx architecture. The company applies atomic-scale nanocoatings to powders, electrodes and semiconductor wafers to improve energy density, cycle life, thermal stability and yield, and sells three lines of business: US-sourced lithium-ion cells from its Morrisville, North Carolina gigafactory, commercial semiconductor wafer-fabrication equipment including the TEPHRA cluster tool for 200mm wafers, and Powder ALD coating systems for batteries, catalysts and composites. Its markets are semiconductors, energy storage, defense and aerospace, AI hardware and quantum devices. Forge Nano is a hardware and advanced-materials company: as of this profiling pass it publishes no public developer portal, API, SDK or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: JMEM
providers.description: JMEM (Jmem Tek) is an upstream semiconductor company specializing in Application-Specific Integrated Circuit (ASIC) solutions for quantum-resilient cybersecurity. The company designs hardware security intellectual property and provides IC design services, offering products such as JRoot, JPUF, JCrypt, and JShield, along with Zanker, described as the world's first PUF-based post-quantum cryptography (PQC) chip. Its NIST-aligned, quantum-safe encryption and hardware-anchored identity authentication protect chips against counterfeiting and unauthorized modification across UAV, automotive, surveillance, and fintech applications. JMEM is a portfolio company of 500 Global, added to the API Evangelist network and enriched from its public web presence; it publishes no public API or developer surface at this time.

providers.name: Lumilens
providers.description: Lumilens is a San Jose, California photonics company building optical interconnect silicon for AI data centers. Founded in 2024 by Ankur Singla (previously Contrail Systems and Volterra) with Ted Schmidt, Samuel Liu, Ritesh Kapahi and Dave Friedman, it designs co-packaged optics (CPO) and near-packaged optics (NPO) devices that let hyperscalers replace copper interconnect with fiber at 800Gb/s, 1.6Tb/s and beyond, attacking the connectivity bottleneck that now limits GPU cluster scaling more than compute does. The company emerged from stealth in August 2026 with more than $900M raised — including a $700M Series C at a $5.51B valuation led by Atreides Management, Bain Capital Ventures, Meritech, Seligman Ventures and Spark Capital — and says it is already shipping production optical interconnect into hyperscale AI data centers under a multi-billion-dollar customer agreement. Its product is physical silicon sold direct to a small set of very large buyers; as of this profile it publishes no developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable contract of any kind, and lumilens.com is still an interim recruiting and news site.

providers.name: Upscale AI
providers.description: Upscale AI is a pure-play AI networking infrastructure company headquartered in Santa Clara, California, founded by industry veterans from Palo Alto Networks, Marvell, Cisco, and Google and led by CEO Barun Kar. The company builds a full-stack, open-standards AI fabric spanning silicon, systems, and software — its SkyHammer scale-up ASIC architecture and NVIDIA Spectrum-X/SONiC-based scale-out Ethernet systems connect accelerators, memory, and storage for large-scale AI training and inference. Backed by Mayfield among others (Premji Invest, NVIDIA, Salesforce Ventures, Temasek, Tiger Global), it has raised $500M total at a $2B valuation. The company publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable interface surface beyond a Webflow-served llms.txt; it sells networking hardware and software evaluated by hyperscalers and neoclouds.

providers.name: VSORA
providers.description: VSORA is a French fabless semiconductor company headquartered in Meudon-La-Foret, France, that designs high-performance AI inference chips. Its Jotunn 8 data-center inference chip (3200 Tflops fp8, 288 GB HBM, built on TSMC 5nm) targets cost- and energy-efficient large-scale AI inference, and its Tyr family (Tyr 2, Tyr 4) targets edge AI and on-device processing. VSORA is a Partech portfolio company and publishes no public web API or developer portal as of July 2026.

providers.name: 1X Technologies
providers.description: 1X Technologies (formerly Halodi Robotics) is a Norwegian-American humanoid robotics company building general-purpose bipedal robots designed to live and work alongside people. Founded in 2014 in Norway by Bernt Øyvind Børnich, the company is now headquartered in Palo Alto, California with R&D and manufacturing presence in Moss, Norway and a new vertically integrated NEO factory in Hayward, California. 1X is backed by the OpenAI Startup Fund, EQT Ventures, Tiger Global, Samsung NEXT, and others through Series A2 ($23.5M, 2023), Series B ($100M, 2024), and a $1B raise reported in 2025. Its commercial robots are EVE — a wheeled upper-humanoid deployed in industrial and security settings since 2022 — and NEO, a bipedal home humanoid that began pre-orders October 28, 2025 at $20,000 (or $499/month) with consumer deliveries in 2026. 1X also acquired Kind Humanoid (Jan 2025) and announced a partnership to deploy up to 10,000 NEO robots into EQT portfolio company factories and warehouses between 2026 and 2030. Unlike most humanoid robotics vendors, 1X publishes meaningful open-source artifacts: the EVE ROS2 API (custom WholeBodyTrajectory and DrivingCommand message types) and the halodi-messages package on GitHub under Apache-2.0, plus the 1X World Model Challenge with 100+ hours of vector-quantized EVE observations and GENIE baseline models released on Hugging Face. There is no public REST/HTTP developer API or hosted developer portal — the developer surface is ROS2 messages, robot models in URDF, and the world-model dataset/model artifacts.

providers.name: Intuition Robotics
providers.description: Intuition Robotics is a Tel Aviv-based AI company (with offices in the United States, Japan, and Greece) building social companion technology for older adults. Its flagship product, ElliQ, is an AI care companion robot that proactively engages users through natural conversation, body language, lights, and sound, powered by a proprietary "Relationship Orchestrator" cognitive-AI platform and multiple large language models to support health, wellness, cognitive engagement, and reducing loneliness. Intuition Robotics publishes no first-party developer API, SDK, or developer portal; the ElliQ product store (elliq.com, on Shopify) does expose an agent-commerce surface via the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP), including a published llms.txt and a UCP shopping MCP endpoint for agent-driven catalog search and checkout. Backed by Bloomberg Beta among other investors.

providers.name: Skyworks Solutions
providers.description: Skyworks Solutions, Inc. is an American semiconductor company headquartered in Irvine, California that designs, develops, and markets proprietary semiconductor products for wireless communications, automotive, broadband, connected home, industrial, defense, and consumer electronics applications. Skyworks is a leading provider of analog and mixed-signal semiconductors, with dominant market share in 5G RF front-end modules (35% market share). Products span amplifiers, filters, front-end modules, isolators, switches, and power management ICs serving mobile, automotive, IoT, and infrastructure markets. The company does not publish a public developer API but provides datasheets, evaluation tools, and design resources for hardware engineers.

providers.name: Unitree Robotics
providers.description: Unitree Robotics is a Hangzhou, China-based high-performance robot manufacturer founded in 2016 by Wang Xingxing. The company is a global pioneer in the commercial quadruped (robot dog) market and has expanded into bipedal humanoid robots. Its product line includes the Go1, Go2, and Go2-W quadrupeds for consumers, education, and research; the industrial-grade B1 and B2 quadrupeds for inspection, patrol, and logistics; the H1 full-size humanoid; the G1 humanoid for research and developer experimentation; the R1 humanoid; and the Z1 robotic arm. Unitree also produces in-house components including the L1/L2 LiDAR, hand-grade actuators, and dexterous hands (Dex1-1). Unitree's developer surface is SDK-centric — there is no public REST or gRPC cloud API. Robot control happens on-device over DDS (Data Distribution Service) via the unitree_sdk2 (C++) and unitree_sdk2_python libraries, with high-level message bindings published as unitree_ros and unitree_ros2. The company maintains an active GitHub presence at github.com/unitreerobotics with 46+ public repositories covering SDKs, ROS packages, MuJoCo and Isaac Lab simulation environments, reinforcement learning frameworks (unitree_rl_gym, unitree_rl_lab), teleoperation tooling (xr_teleoperate, kinect_teleoperate, televuer), imitation learning (unitree_lerobot), a vision-language-action model (unifolm-vla), and a Unitree App Store template repo. Documentation lives at support.unitree.com/home/en/developer. Unitree's revenue model is direct robot hardware sales via shop.unitree.com and partner distribution; there is no metered API service tier.

providers.name: Alta Resource Technologies
providers.description: Alta Resource Technologies is a Colorado-based deep-tech company reinventing how critical minerals are sourced. It uses advanced biochemistry — customizable, engineered proteins licensed from Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory and co-developed with researchers at Pennsylvania State University — to selectively separate high-purity rare earth elements and other strategic metals from low-grade ores, mining tailings, and electronic-waste streams such as end-of-life hard disk drives. The protein-based platform binds target elements out of complex, low-concentration solutions with high selectivity while dramatically reducing the environmental footprint of conventional mining and refining, strengthening U.S. and allied critical-mineral supply chains. Alta emerged from stealth in January 2025 and expanded its Series Seed to $10M, backed by DCVC, Voyager Ventures, In-Q-Tel, and Orion Industrial Ventures.
