As a materials-science and biochemistry company, Alta does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal; this API Evangelist profile carries its identity and website properties only.

providers.name: Aptos Orbital
providers.description: Aptos Orbital (legal entity Cryptosat, Inc.) is a space technology company, founded in 2021 and backed by the Techstars Space Accelerator, that builds integrated hardware for satellites and spacecraft. Its flagship Aptos Terminal combines space-hardened, radiation-tolerant edge compute (with proprietary SEU/SEL protection), persistent global satellite communications, and cloud connectivity to platforms such as AWS and Azure into a single device. The company advertises 5.5+ years of proven orbital operation, 99% global data coverage, and TRL9 readiness for LEO applications, with development licenses, engineering models, and flight models offered to spacecraft builders. Aptos Orbital was added to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio lead; as of this pass the company publishes hardware brochures and a "start developing" onboarding form but no public API, SDK, developer portal, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: August Home
providers.description: August Home is a consumer smart-home and access-control brand best known for its retrofit August Smart Lock, Smart Lock Pro, Wi-Fi Smart Lock, Smart Keypad, Doorbell Cam, and the August Connect Wi-Fi Bridge. Founded in San Francisco and acquired by ASSA ABLOY, August products are now sold and supported alongside the Yale Home brand and operated through the shared Yale Access mobile app. August does not publish a public developer API or developer portal; programmatic access to August locks is reached through the private mobile/app API or via third-party universal-access platforms such as Seam, and integrations exist with Google Home, Amazon Alexa, Apple HomeKit, Airbnb, and Yale. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Cowboy Ventures and enriched from public sources.

providers.name: Blaize
providers.description: Blaize (NASDAQ: BZAI) is an edge AI company headquartered in El Dorado Hills, California that builds a programmable inference platform uniting silicon and software. Its Graph Streaming Processor (GSP) powers the Pathfinder and Xplorer accelerator families — SoM, M.2, EDSFF and PCIe form factors plus the DST developer station and Blaize Inference Server — and its software layer pairs the Picasso SDK (C++, Python, OpenVX, with TensorFlow/PyTorch/ONNX import via NetDeploy) with AI Studio, a code-free environment spanning the full edge AI DataOps/DevOps/MLOps lifecycle. In April 2026 Blaize announced a planned Blaize AI Services platform that packages multimodal inference, business logic and orchestration as modular application-level APIs across vision, video, document, speech and moderation workloads. The developer surface — SDK downloads, repositories and reference material — is served from a self-hosted GitLab at software.blaize.com and requires an account, so no public machine-readable API contract is published.

providers.name: Bright View Technologies
providers.description: BrightView Technologies, Inc. is a Durham, North Carolina optical film company specializing in computational optics and the design and manufacture of Micro Lens Array (MLA) solutions that shape, diffuse, and manage light. Founded in 2002 on intellectual property licensed from Duke University, the company engineers precision optical films and micro-optical structures used in automotive displays, head-up displays, and LiDAR; consumer and mini/micro-LED displays (gain enhancement and LED-hiding films); LED and architectural lighting (beam shaping and diffusion); and augmented- and virtual-reality beam-shaping optics. BrightView is a hardware and materials manufacturer serving OEMs and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead of Battery Ventures and enriched from the company's public website.

providers.name: Celus
providers.description: CELUS GmbH is a Munich-based electronics design automation company building an AI-driven, cloud design platform that automates the early stages of printed circuit board (PCB) engineering. The CELUS Design Platform turns high-level product requirements into schematics, part selections and layout-ready outputs in minutes rather than days by combining AI-powered component search with its proprietary CUBO component knowledge base, then handing off EDA-compatible files to tools like Altium and KiCad. Founded by Alexander and Tobias Pohl and backed by Earlybird and Speedinvest, CELUS targets hardware engineers and manufacturers pursuing digital transformation of the electronics design workflow. The platform is a closed SaaS product accessed through app.celus.io; as of this enrichment pass CELUS publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal.

providers.name: Fractile
providers.description: Fractile is a UK-based semiconductor startup, founded in 2022 and headquartered in London with an engineering base in Bristol, designing a new class of AI inference processors. Its architecture physically interleaves memory and compute to overcome the memory-bandwidth bottleneck that limits large language model inference, targeting frontier model serving up to 25x faster and at roughly 1/10th the cost of existing hardware. The company takes a full-stack approach spanning transistor-level circuit design through cloud inference server logic, and in May 2026 raised $220M to build the next generation of inference hardware. Backers include Accel and Felicis. Led by founder and CEO Walter Goodwin, Fractile is a hardware/compute company and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Greentoe
providers.description: Greentoe is a name-your-price e-commerce marketplace where shoppers make an offer on brand-new electronics, cameras, TVs and home theater, appliances, baby gear, watches, and optics, and manufacturer-authorized retailers compete to fulfill the order at the buyer's price. Built to bring the negotiation model of big-ticket purchases online, Greentoe reports more than $100M saved by its customers, backs every order with manufacturer warranties and a 30-day return policy, and is backed by 500 Global and Y Combinator. Greentoe operates as a consumer-facing web application and does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures its public web and security surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Intellitech
providers.description: Intellitech Corporation is a semiconductor test and design-for-test company based in Rochester, New Hampshire, specializing in IEEE 1149.1 (JTAG) boundary-scan technology. Its products include the Eclipse boundary-scan test development environment, the Scan Executive production test platform, and concurrent JTAG hardware testers such as the PT100 and JAF Pro, used for printed circuit board (PCB) testing, in-system FLASH programming, and FPGA configuration. Intellitech is an early Battery Ventures ("Battery Ventures I") portfolio company in the semiconductor sector. The company publishes product, legal, and customer-account pages on its website but does not expose a public developer API, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or MCP surface.

providers.name: Lumos Helmet
providers.description: Lumos (Lumos Helmet) is a consumer hardware company that designs and manufactures smart bike helmets and connected bike lights with integrated safety features such as turn signals, brake lights, and high-visibility LED lighting. Its product line spans commuter, e-bike, and kids' helmets plus standalone smart bike lights, controlled through companion iOS and Android mobile apps. Backed by Techstars, Lumos sells direct-to-consumer through an online store; it does not currently publish a public API, developer platform, or SDK. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline, which confirmed no programmatic API surface and captured the company's identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Ocean Aero
providers.description: Ocean Aero is a Gulfport, Mississippi maritime robotics manufacturer that designs, builds and operates the Triton, an environmentally powered Autonomous Underwater and Surface Vehicle (AUSV) that can both sail on the surface and submerge to collect data above and below the waterline and relay it back to shore. The 14-foot platform harvests wind and solar energy, carries pre-packaged or custom payloads for defense, ocean research and offshore energy missions, and is managed through Ocean Aero's own proprietary mission-control GUI with fleet-wide waypoint and payload management. As of this profile Ocean Aero sells vehicles, payloads and mission services — it publishes no public developer program, no API reference and no machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Senra Systems
providers.description: Senra Systems is an aerospace wire harness manufacturer based in Redondo Beach, California, that unites design, data, and production under one roof. The company builds complex electrical wire harnesses for aerospace and defense programs, spanning wire harness design and engineering support, prototype through full-rate production, component selection and supply chain optimization, and precision automation in a 15,000 square foot smart-manufacturing facility. Senra positions itself as delivering harnesses at roughly four times the speed of traditional vendors while maintaining aerospace-grade quality and certifications. Senra Systems is backed by Sequoia Capital, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, 8VC, and General Catalyst. The company does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Simplifyber
providers.description: Simplifyber is a sustainable footwear and materials technology company that manufactures shoe uppers and other components using a proprietary fiber-molding process. By casting products directly from a liquid, cellulose-based material it eliminates the spinning, weaving, and knitting steps and much of the cutting and sewing of traditional shoemaking, which it says lowers the CO2 emissions of a shoe upper by roughly 33x versus conventional methods. Its flagship Moon Shoe was developed with the fashion brand Ganni. Simplifyber is a Techstars-backed startup. It operates as a consumer and industrial manufacturer and does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation, or developer portal.

providers.name: Tennibot
providers.description: Tennibot builds AI-powered ball machines and autonomous ball collectors for tennis, pickleball, and padel. Its flagship Partner ball machine and Rover ball collector use computer vision and robotics to deliver realistic drills and eliminate manual ball pickup, controlled through the Tennibot mobile app for iOS and Android. The company, based in Auburn, Alabama and backed by Techstars, sells direct-to-consumer hardware; it ships a companion mobile app but does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record; no external API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Anthro Energy
providers.description: Anthro Energy is a battery materials company based in Alameda, California, developing next-generation electrolyte technology for lithium-ion and next-gen battery cells. Its flagship Proteus platform is a drop-in electrolyte that increases energy density, improves safety, and adds mechanical integrity without requiring changes to existing gigafactory manufacturing infrastructure, and is compatible with a wide range of anodes, separators, and cathodes. Spun out of research at Stanford, Anthro Energy is a portfolio company of Union Square Ventures and Ultratech Capital. It is a physical-materials company with no public API surface; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company and market discovery.

providers.name: Tozuda
providers.description: Tozuda is a Philadelphia-based safety technology company that makes mechanical, non-electronic head impact indicators for helmets. The patented indicator changes from clear to red when a helmet sustains force exceeding a set G-force threshold, making hidden helmet damage visible to workers, athletes, and safety inspectors across ANSI, DOT, EN, CSA, CPSC, and SNELL helmet types. Tozuda is a Techstars portfolio company and does not currently publish a public API or developer program.

providers.name: A. Schulman
providers.description: A. Schulman was a global supplier of high-performance plastic compounds, composites, and powders used by manufacturers across packaging, automotive, electronics, and consumer goods industries. The company was acquired by LyondellBasell in 2018 and now operates as the Advanced Polymer Solutions division, continuing to supply engineered plastics, masterbatches, compounds, and specialty powders to global manufacturers.

providers.name: Iceotope
providers.description: Iceotope Technologies is a Sheffield, UK precision liquid cooling company founded in 2005 as a research-driven "green computing" venture, now supplying chassis-level liquid cooling for AI, HPC, data center and edge infrastructure. Its "direct to everything" single-phase immersion approach removes heat from every component rather than the processor alone, and ships as two product lines: KUL BOX for near-edge AI and HPC deployments, and KUL AI liquid-cooled server chassis for high-density rack environments. The company licenses its thermal IP (228 patents granted, allowed and pending) and works through OEM/ODM partnerships with vendors including HPE, Intel and nVent. Iceotope is a hardware and thermal-engineering business: it publishes no developer program, no public API, and no machine-readable API contract on any host it controls.

providers.name: Mojo Vision
providers.description: Mojo Vision is a Saratoga, California semiconductor and display company building a "wafers-in, wafers-out" micro-LED platform. Founded in 2015, it originally developed the world's smallest, densest dynamic display for an AR smart contact lens, then pivoted in 2023 to commercializing micro-LED displays and optical interconnects. Its platform combines a 300mm silicon architecture with GaN-on-Silicon emitters, proprietary quantum dots and micro-lens arrays, and has demonstrated a monolithic RGB panel at 4µm pixel pitch (6,350 ppi). Target markets are XR and AI-enabled glasses, automotive heads-up displays, large-format displays, and high-density optical I/O for AI infrastructure. Partners include Marvell, DigiLens and CY Vision; investors include Khosla Ventures, NEA, Future Ventures, HP Tech Ventures, Amazon's Alexa Fund and Dolby Family Ventures. Mojo Vision is a hardware/silicon company and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: NextSilicon
providers.description: NextSilicon is a deep-tech compute company building intelligent, software-defined acceleration hardware for high-performance computing, AI, and vector-database workloads. Its flagship Maverick-2 is a dataflow accelerator built on the Intelligent Compute Architecture (ICA) that reconfigures itself at runtime, and its Arbel product is a server-class RISC-V CPU core on TSMC process. A developer toolchain supports C/C++, FORTRAN, OpenMP, and Kokkos, with planned CUDA and HIP/ROCm paths, letting teams run existing code faster without rewrites or vendor lock-in. NextSilicon publishes no public web API, SDK registry package, or open developer portal; its documentation site is gated, so this profile captures company identity, its GitHub organization (largely upstream compiler/Kokkos forks), and domain-security posture.

providers.name: nEye Systems
providers.description: nEye (nEye.ai, formerly nEye Systems) is a silicon photonics company in Santa Clara and Emeryville, California building an optical circuit switch on a chip — a programmable photonic integrated circuit that combines silicon photonics, MEMS and CMOS to switch light directly between GPUs, CPUs and memory inside AI and high-performance computing data centers, marketed as the SuperSwitch. The company was spun out of University of California, Berkeley research by co-founder and chief scientist Ming C. Wu and is led by CEO Ashish Vengsarkar. It raised an $80M Series C led by Sutter Hill Ventures in April 2026, bringing total funding to $152M with participation from CapitalG, M12 and Socratic Partners, and it participates in the Open Compute Project Open OCS effort alongside Google, NVIDIA and Microsoft. nEye is a semiconductor and optical hardware company: as of this profile it publishes no developer program, API, SDK, webhook surface or machine-readable contract of any kind, and its entire public surface is a seven-page marketing site.

providers.name: NinjaBlocks
providers.description: Ninja Blocks Inc was an Australian Internet-of-Things startup (founded 2012, backed by 500 Global / 500 Startups) behind the Ninja Block and Ninja Sphere home-automation hubs. It offered a cloud-connected platform with a RESTful API (base https://api.ninja.is/rest/v0/) for reading sensor data and controlling actuators, plus first-party client libraries for Node.js, PHP, Ruby, Lua and Arduino, a `ninja-toolbelt` CLI, and OAuth-based authentication. The company ceased operation and its web and API hosts are no longer online; this profile preserves the surviving first-party open-source client libraries and API tooling published to npm and GitHub. Added to the API Evangelist network from the 500 Global portfolio and enriched from public package registries and the github.com/ninjablocks organization.

providers.name: Prophetic
providers.description: Prophetic is a San Francisco-based neurotechnology startup, incorporated in January 2023, building the world's first wearable device for stabilizing lucid dreams. Its "Halo" headband pairs EEG sensing with targeted transcranial focused ultrasound (tFUS) to noninvasively stimulate the prefrontal cortex, driven by an in-house AI model, Morpheus-1, that takes brain activity as its prompt and generates shaped ultrasonic waveforms as output. Backed by BoxGroup and a16z's Scout Fund, Prophetic sells its neuromodulation headbands direct-to-consumer. The company was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this pass Prophetic publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or programmatic integration surface — it is a consumer hardware and wellness company.

providers.name: Sleep Number
providers.description: Sleep Number Corporation (NASDAQ: SNBR) designs, manufactures, and retails smart adjustable-firmness beds and sleep-wellness products, sold through an omnichannel US retail model. Its Sleep Number 360 smart beds run the proprietary SleepIQ operating system, which captures biometric sleep data each night and returns actionable insights to improve sleep health. Sleep Number does not publish a public developer API or developer portal; the SleepIQ platform is a closed, undocumented backend consumed only by the first-party mobile and web apps. The community has reverse-engineered unofficial SleepIQ client libraries (Python, Go, PHP), but these are not first-party and are not endorsed by Sleep Number. This profile was surfaced as a legacy portfolio lead of Norwest Venture Partners and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Westmag
providers.description: Western Magnetics (Westmag) designs and manufactures brushless DC (BLDC) drone motors and robot actuators in South San Francisco, California. Built and scaled in America and NDAA-compliant from day one, Westmag is a vertically integrated motor company spanning design, manufacturing, and supply chain — producing high-volume BLDC drone motors for Group 1, 2, and 3 UAS platforms (20-100mm stators, Kv 100-3,000, outrunner and inrunner) and integrated actuators for humanoid and mobile robots (torque 1-150Nm, 24-48V, gearing 6:1-12:1). Founded by David Hansen (CEO) and Jordan Sanders (COO) and backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, Lux Capital, Menlo Ventures, and NFDG. This is a hardware company; it currently exposes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Alloy Enterprises
providers.description: Alloy Enterprises is a Burlington, Massachusetts advanced-manufacturing company that makes single-piece aluminum thermal management components using Stack Forging, its patented digital fabrication process. Rather than printing from metal powder, Stack Forging laser-cuts sheets of aluminum and diffusion-bonds them under controlled heat and pressure into monolithic, porosity-free parts carrying complex internal geometries that casting, forging and machining cannot produce. The company sells cold plates, liquid-cooling components, vapor chambers and oscillating heat pipes into data-center cooling, defense electronics, photonics, semiconductor equipment, e-mobility, heavy equipment and industrial fluid-handling markets, and states its parts cut pressure drop by up to 4x and improve thermal resistance by more than 35%. Founded in 2020 and spun out of work begun in Somerville, Massachusetts, Alloy Enterprises was acquired by Johnson Controls in a deal signed 2026-02-18 and closed 2026-05-13, and now operates as part of that company's data-center thermal management business. Alloy Enterprises is a hardware and materials manufacturer: it publishes no public developer API, developer portal, SDK, CLI, sandbox, status page or machine-readable specification of any kind. See x-coverage below.

providers.name: Diligent Robotics
providers.description: Diligent Robotics is an Austin, Texas-based healthcare robotics company founded in 2017 by Andrea Thomaz (CEO) and Vivian Chu (CIO), both trained as roboticists at MIT, Georgia Tech, and the University of Texas at Austin. The company builds Moxi, a socially intelligent mobile manipulator that operates autonomously inside hospitals to handle non-clinical material transport — delivering medications, lab samples, supplies, PPE, and patient items so nurses and clinical staff can focus on patient care. Moxi combines mobile manipulation (grasping, opening doors, riding elevators), social navigation, and human-guided learning, and is deployed 24/7 with minimal facility infrastructure (existing Wi-Fi). Operationally, Moxi has logged 500,000+ deliveries and 100,000+ autonomous elevator rides across customer hospitals including UTMB, Shannon Health, ThedaCare, Carilion Giles Community Hospital, and Medical City Denton. The platform is HIPAA compliant, SOC 2 Type II audited, and TX-RAMP Level 2 certified. Diligent has raised roughly $100M across rounds led by Canaan, True Ventures, Tiger Global, DNX Ventures, Next Coast Ventures, and Northwestern Medicine Innovation. Diligent's revenue model is robot deployment/leasing and enterprise services; there is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release for Moxi or its underlying robotics stack.

providers.name: Osmo
providers.description: Osmo (Tangible Play) makes hands-on, screen-interactive learning games for iPad and Fire tablet that pair a physical reflector base placed over the device camera with digital games spanning math, coding, spelling, drawing, and problem-solving for children. Backed by Accel and GV, Osmo is a consumer educational-technology brand that sells hardware kits and companion apps direct to families and schools. As of this enrichment pass it does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its public web identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Pebble
providers.description: Pebble is a Silicon Valley electric-vehicle and consumer-hardware company that designs and manufactures the Pebble Flow, an all-electric travel trailer (RV) with an integrated battery, solar, and motor-assist drivetrain. The product line pairs the trailer with the Pebble mobile app for remote control and monitoring, offering features such as autonomous "Magic Hitch" coupling, remote-control positioning, automatic leveling and setup, and up to seven days of off-grid capability. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, Pebble sells direct-to-consumer under the tagline "Where Home Meets the Road." As of this enrichment pass Pebble publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or documented API surface; its only software touchpoint is the consumer-facing Pebble Control Center app.

providers.name: Xsight Labs
providers.description: Xsight Labs is a fabless semiconductor company redefining AI and cloud connectivity with end-to-end, software-defined silicon for hyperscale data centers. Its X-Series programmable Ethernet switch silicon (X1, X2) delivers 3.2-12.8 Tbps with sub-700ns latency and is programmable through XISA, the first fully open, documented switch instruction set architecture, published under MPLv2. Its E-Series is billed as the industry's first fully software-defined 800G DPU family, placing 64 Arm Neoverse N2 cores directly in the data path and programmable with standard Linux tooling (XDP, DPDK, SPDK) with no proprietary SDK. Xsight Labs contributes SONiC platform code and a SAI implementation through its public GitHub organization. Backed by Battery Ventures among other investors. The company publishes technical documentation, XISA specifications, and programming examples rather than a hosted web API; no public OpenAPI, REST endpoints, or hosted API surface were found during enrichment.

providers.name: 3D Glass Solutions
providers.description: 3D Glass Solutions (3DGS) is a US-based pure-play glass foundry in Albuquerque, New Mexico that manufactures photo-definable glass-ceramic substrates for advanced semiconductor packaging. Its patented APEX Glass material supports through-glass vias (TGV), high-density interconnect, integrated passive devices, RF substrates, micro-cavities and 3D heterogeneous integration for wireless communications, aerospace and defense, photonics, HPC/AI and sensor markets. The company sells wafer processing, custom fabrication and design-enablement services — including process design kits (PDKs) delivered through EDA partners such as the AWR software group — rather than software, and publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Arena AI
providers.description: Arena AI (now operating as Arena Physica) is a New York-headquartered applied-research company building what it calls "electromagnetic superintelligence." Its flagship product, Atlas, is an AI-powered hardware-engineering platform that pairs general intelligence with deterministic physics models to accelerate the design, verification, and debugging of electronic and RF hardware. Atlas ingests telemetry, schematics, CAD files, and firmware, then connects via API or MCP (Model Context Protocol) to engineering toolchains such as Jira, GitHub, Altium, Cadence, and SPICE simulators, and to test equipment from vendors like Keysight and Tektronix. Atlas RF Studio, the company's RF design tool, is currently in beta. The company operates from New York City (HQ), San Francisco, and Los Angeles.

providers.name: Astrus
providers.description: Astrus is an AI-powered microchip design company automating the physical layout of analog circuits. Founded in 2022 by Brad Moon (CEO) and Zeyi Wang (CTO) and based in Toronto and Waterloo, Canada, Astrus applies deep reinforcement learning — inspired by AlphaGo-style self-play — to generate thousands of manufacturable analog chip layouts in seconds, targeting high-speed SERDES interconnects used in data-center GPUs. The platform lets circuit designers submit a schematic and receive optimized layouts in minutes rather than the weeks of manual transistor-by-transistor placement that analog EDA traditionally requires. Astrus raised $8M in seed funding led by Khosla Ventures with participation from Pradeep Sindhu, 1517 Fund, Drive Capital and Alumni Ventures. This profile was surfaced as a Khosla Ventures portfolio company; Astrus publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: BRINC
providers.description: BRINC builds a connected ecosystem of drones, software, and services purpose-built for public safety in the United States. Its Drone as First Responder (DFR) systems — the Guardian and Responder outdoor drones, the Lemur 2 indoor tactical drone, and the throwable BRINC Ball — pair with LiveOps teleoperations software (livestreaming, two-way comms, evidence management) to put a camera overhead within seconds of a 911 call. BRINC reports deployments across 900+ public safety agencies in all 50 states, sub-70-second average drone arrival times, and a recent $125M funding round. The company also runs its Safeguard upgrade-and-repair program and grant/DFR playbook services. BRINC exposes no public developer API, SDK, or MCP surface as of this profile; this entry is enriched from the company's public web presence.

providers.name: Frontlinewildfire
providers.description: Frontline Wildfire Defense is a wildfire protection company that designs, manufactures, and installs exterior sprinkler defense systems for homes, businesses, wineries, summer camps, and new-home communities. The system combines roof- and ground-mounted sprinklers, a pump, and water/foam concentrate with a mobile app (iOS and Android) that lets property owners remotely activate the system, monitor nearby wildfires on a live fire map, and receive evacuation alerts. The company also publishes wildfire risk maps, home-hardening and defensible-space guidance, and works through a network of partner installers. Backed by Norwest Venture Partners. This is a consumer/hardware company profile; no public developer API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Polycom
providers.description: Polycom, Inc. was a pioneer of unified communications and video conferencing, known for its RealPresence video collaboration platform, SoundStation conference phones, and Group Series and HDX room video endpoints. Polycom merged with Plantronics in 2018 to form Poly, which HP acquired in 2022; the polycom.com domain now redirects to HP's Poly product line. For developers, Polycom exposed the RealPresence Platform REST API (via the RealPresence Resource Manager and Distributed Media Application, later branded Clariti) along with device REST APIs on its VideoOS endpoints, enabling programmatic conference control, scheduling, provisioning, resource monitoring, and billing integration. Developer resources are now consolidated under HP's Poly developer portal.

providers.name: RS Legacy
providers.description: RS Legacy Corporation is the post-bankruptcy successor entity of RadioShack Corporation, the iconic American consumer electronics retailer founded in 1921. RadioShack filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2015, with RS Legacy Corp assuming the remaining obligations. The RadioShack brand was subsequently acquired by Unicomer Group (El Salvador-based) in 2023, which now operates the brand globally in approximately 70 countries including the United States, Canada, Europe, and Latin America. RadioShack continues to sell consumer electronics, components, batteries, cables, and accessories online at radioshack.com and through franchise locations. No public developer API is currently documented.

providers.name: Albemarle
providers.description: Albemarle Corporation is a global specialty chemicals company and leading provider of lithium, bromine, and other essential elements. Operating from its global headquarters in Charlotte, NC, Albemarle serves customers in approximately 70 countries with world-class hard-rock and brine lithium resources, state-of-the-art lithium conversion facilities, advanced lithium material and process development, bromine production facilities, and the US's only producing lithium resource in Silver Peak, NV. The company serves critical markets including electric vehicle batteries, energy storage, flame retardants, pharmaceutical ingredients, catalysts, and specialty chemicals, employing approximately 7,800 people and holding over 1,500 active patents worldwide.

providers.name: Carnot Fleet
providers.description: Carnot Fleet (Carnotfleet) is a Seoul-based cold-chain technology company that converts non-refrigerated vehicles into temperature-controlled units in under 30 minutes using modular insulation panels and proprietary solid-state thermoelectric heat pumps, spanning frozen, chilled, and ambient ranges with humidity control. Its Adaptive Thermal Control System (ATCS) is an AI-based autonomous control platform delivering cloud-connected temperature monitoring at 10-second intervals. Carnot Fleet surfaces its capabilities through the CF Mobile Application, the CF Portal, and CF APIs that let customers integrate the ATCS into existing logistics solutions to detect, analyze, prevent, and discover cold-chain data points and reduce post-harvest to pre-retail loss across the supply chain.

providers.name: Exowatt
providers.description: Exowatt is a clean-energy technology company redefining power generation for the AI era. Its flagship Exowatt P3 is a modular, dispatchable solar-thermal energy platform that captures solar energy with proprietary Fresnel lenses and heat exchangers, stores it in a high-efficiency heat battery, and dispatches electricity on demand via a proprietary heat engine, delivering up to 24 hours of dispatchable baseload power. The systems are factory-built in the USA from abundant, low-cost materials without rare-earth minerals, and are aimed at energy-intensive customers such as AI data centers and utilities. Backed by a16z and Felicis, Exowatt is added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it currently publishes no public developer API or documentation surface.

providers.name: Heron Power
providers.description: Heron Power is an industrial power-electronics company modernizing the electrical grid with solid-state transformers and integrated power conversion systems. Founded by former Tesla executive Drew Baglino, the company builds Heron Link products that combine a solid-state transformer with a power supply or inverter for two markets: data centers (AI and hyperscale power delivery, including 800 VDC datacenter architectures) and solar-and-storage renewable energy systems. Heron Power targets the grid infrastructure bottlenecks of the clean-energy transition, replacing century-old passive transformer technology with dense, controllable, software-defined power hardware. The company is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Breakthrough Energy. Heron Power is a hardware and infrastructure company and does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company intelligence.

providers.name: Humatics
providers.description: Humatics Corporation is a Waltham, Massachusetts microlocation company founded in 2015 by MIT professor David Mindell and led by CEO James Kinsey. It builds radio-frequency positioning systems — ultra-wideband beacons, RF-pulse ranging, radar and inertial sensors fused in software — that locate people, vehicles and robots at centimeter- to millimeter-scale precision. Two product lines are on sale today: MILO, a sub-millimeter positioning system for industrial automation and in-motion robotics, advertised as compatible with Yaskawa, Mitsubishi Electric, FANUC, Universal Robots and KUKA; and Mobility, a rail and transit portfolio covering the FOCUS track-geometry monitoring kit and the Humatics Rail Navigation System (HRNS), used on New York City MTA subway signalling projects. Humatics publishes no developer portal, no API documentation and no machine-readable description of any product API. Two rounds of probing humatics.com returned HTTP 404 for every /.well-known/ path, /llms.txt, /openapi.json, /openapi.yaml, /swagger.json, /api-docs and /graphql; *.humatics.com is a DNS wildcard onto one retired address, so api., docs., developer., portal. and status. resolve but time out on connect. The only machine-readable HTTP interface on any Humatics host is the WordPress REST API of the marketing site itself at humatics.com/wp-json/ — 375 routes across 19 stock core and commercial-plugin namespaces, exposing pages and posts rather than positioning, and so recorded as evidence rather than catalogued as a Humatics API. The GitHub organization github.com/Humatics is real and public, but 31 of its 33 repositories are forks of third-party embedded and robotics open source (Fast-RTPS, Fast-CDR, FreeRTOS, Orange Pi BSP, Yocto meta-layers, EIPScanner, donkeycar); the two non-forks are internal tools. There is no first-party SDK, client library or specification, and no package named humatics exists on npm or PyPI. Marketing material for the earlier KinetIQ OS / Spatial Intelligence Platform referenced an "extensible API", but no public interface for it was ever documented, and the news host that carried those announcements (now.humatics.com) no longer answers.

providers.name: Lumotive
providers.description: Lumotive is a Seattle-based semiconductor company building programmable optics on its patented Light Control Metasurface (LCM) technology — solid-state, software-defined beam steering implemented in a standard CMOS process with no moving parts. Its products include the LM10 and LX10 LCM beam-steering chips, the LCM Evaluation Kit (LEK), the M30 iToF and NM120 3D-sensing development kits, and the M30/TX10 reference designs, applied to industrial automation, intelligent traffic systems, automotive ADAS and autonomy, defense, and optical circuit switching for AI data centers. Lumotive publishes an "Open Lidar API" — a real-time control interface for software-defined Lidar 2.0 hardware covering region-of-interest scanning, frame rate, resolution and range, plus a common point-cloud format — and ships C/C++ LCM control libraries with Python bindings alongside its evaluation kits. That interface is an embedded hardware-control API, not a public web API: no developer portal, documentation site, machine-readable specification, or self-service sign-up is published, and access is granted to selected partners through the Technology Access Program by contacting the company.

providers.name: roli
providers.description: ROLI (Luminary ROLI Ltd.) is a British music-technology company known for expressive electronic instruments — the Seaboard, LUMI Keys keyboards, and the modular BLOCKS system — together with companion software such as ROLI Dashboard, ROLI Connect, Equator, and ROLI Learn. Its instruments pioneer MPE (MIDI Polyphonic Expression) for per-note pitch, timbre, and dynamics control. For developers, ROLI publishes first-party SDKs under the github.com/weareroli organization — the C++ BLOCKS-SDK and roli_blocks_basics for building applications that talk to BLOCKS hardware, and the archived mpejs library for MPE MIDI in the browser. ROLI is backed by Balderton Capital and Index Ventures. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead and enriched with real developer, SDK, and domain-security artifacts.

providers.name: zincfive
providers.description: ZincFive is a power solutions company that manufactures nickel-zinc (NiZn) battery technology for mission-critical and backup power applications, including data center UPS systems, AI dynamic power, and grid storage. Its product line covers BC Series UPS battery cabinets, NiZn retrofit kits, monobloc batteries, and cylindrical cells, positioned as non-flammable, high-power-density, and highly recyclable alternatives to lead-acid batteries. ZincFive publishes technical documents, papers, and industry insights reports, but does not expose a public developer API or SDK surface.

providers.name: Agility Robotics
providers.description: Agility Robotics is a Salem, Oregon humanoid robotics company building industrial bipedal robots for warehouse and factory automation. Founded in 2015 as a spin-out of Oregon State University's Dynamic Robotics Laboratory, its flagship product is Digit — described as the first humanoid robot in commercial production deployment — and Arc, the cloud-based automation platform that operates Digit fleets, provides real-time visibility, manages task assignments, and connects Digit to existing warehouse automation including AMRs, WMS, and WES systems. Digit has commercial deployments and pilots with Amazon, GXO Logistics, Schaeffler, Toyota Motor Manufacturing Canada, and Mercado Libre, with an expanded NVIDIA partnership for foundation-model and simulation tooling. Agility operates RoboFab, a humanoid robot factory in Salem, OR with capacity to produce 10,000 robots annually. Digit has surpassed 100,000 totes moved in commercial deployment at a single Georgia facility. Agility Robotics does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or open-source release for Digit or Arc; integration is performed by Agility's solutions team and partners through a gated low-level JSON-over-WebSocket API and pysdk delivered with the robot. The company's public GitHub org primarily contains forks of infrastructure tooling (JFrog, Bazel, Fluent Bit, Kubernetes Cluster API) plus an archived documentation repo for the earlier Cassie research platform.

providers.name: Corning
providers.description: Corning Incorporated is a Fortune 500 American technology company that specializes in glass science, ceramic science, and optical physics. Founded in 1851, Corning manufactures specialty glass, ceramics, and related materials and technologies for industrial and scientific applications. Corning's businesses include Optical Communications (fiber optic cable and hardware), Display Technologies (LCD and OLED glass substrates), Specialty Materials (Gorilla Glass for mobile devices), Environmental Technologies (ceramic substrates and filters for emissions control), and Life Sciences (laboratory glassware, cell culture, and bioprocess products). Corning does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: FANUC
providers.description: FANUC Corporation is a Japanese multinational headquartered in Oshino, Yamanashi at the base of Mount Fuji, and is one of the world's largest suppliers of factory automation, industrial robots, and CNC (computer numerical control) systems. Founded in 1972 after spinning out of Fujitsu's numerical control division (originated 1955) under Seiuemon Inaba, FANUC pioneered commercial NC and CNC technology and by the early 1980s held roughly half of the global CNC market. The company operates three primary business segments: FA (CNC systems, servo motors, lasers, and PMC controls for machine tools), Robot (industrial arms from the LR Mate and M-series through the heavy-payload M-2000iA, plus the CRX collaborative robot family), and ROBOMACHINE (ROBODRILL machining centers, ROBOCUT wire EDM, and ROBOSHOT all-electric injection molding machines). FANUC's primary developer surface is FOCAS (FANUC Open CNC API Specification), a licensed C/C++ library (fwlib32.dll) used by machine builders and MES/OEE vendors to read CNC state over Ethernet, plus KAREL and Teach Pendant (TP) programming on the robot controllers and a published ROS 2 driver for the CRX collaborative arms. FANUC does not operate a public REST developer portal or publish OpenAPI specifications; integrations are partner-driven through MTConnect adapters, OPC UA servers, FIELD system edge apps, and the FANUC America customer/training portals.

providers.name: KUKA
providers.description: KUKA AG is a German industrial automation company headquartered in Augsburg, Bavaria, founded in 1898 and majority-owned by China's Midea Group since 2016. KUKA designs and manufactures industrial robots, autonomous mobile robots (AMRs), production cells, controllers, and the software stack that drives them. Its product portfolio spans six-axis articulated robots (KR series), sensitive collaborative robots (LBR iiwa, LBR iisy), mobile platforms (KMR iiwa, KMP), and palletizing/welding/CNC cells, controlled by the KR C4 and KR C5 / KR C5 micro controller generations. The robot software stack centers on KUKA System Software (KSS/VSS) for KR C4-class hardware, the newer iiQKA.OS / iiQKA.OS2 operating system for KR C5, and the KUKA Robot Language (KRL) for motion programming, with extension surfaces including KUKA.RobotSensorInterface (RSI), KUKA.EthernetKRL, KUKA.PLC mxAutomation for external PLC control, KUKA.OPC UA, and KUKA.AppTech / iiQKA App Builder for option packages. Engineering and simulation are delivered through iiQWorks (iiQWorks.Sim, iiQWorks.App Builder, iiQWorks.Copilot) and KUKA.Sim, while operational software includes KUKA Xpert (documentation/cloud), KUKA iiQoT (condition monitoring), and KUKA Connect / my.KUKA customer portals. KUKA does not publish a first-party public REST/OpenAPI developer API or an official GitHub organization for its robot control stack; integration is performed through proprietary protocols (RSI, EthernetKRL, mxAutomation, OPC UA, PROFINET, EtherCAT) and SDKs distributed via the iiQKA Creator portal and KUKA Xpert. A meaningful body of open-source KUKA integration code lives in the community-maintained kroshu GitHub organization (ROS 2 drivers, external-control SDK, URDF robot descriptions) and the roboticsapi / openkuka projects. KUKA serves automotive, electronics, battery, metal, consumer goods, healthcare, aerospace, and e-commerce logistics customers, and through its Swisslog subsidiary extends into warehouse and intralogistics automation.

providers.name: MEQ Solutions
providers.description: MEQ Solutions is an Australian agrifood technology company delivering what it calls the world's only end-to-end measurement of red meat quality and yield. Its integrated hardware-and-software suite — MEQ Probe, MEQ Camera, MEQ Live, and MEQ Insights — gives producers, feedlots, processors, brands, retailers, and food-service operators objective, real-time carcass and eating-quality data. Deployed across Australia, New Zealand, the United States, and Brazil, MEQ has completed over 10 million scans across 60+ deployments and reports a demonstrated 10x ROI. The company is backed by Insight Partners. No public developer API surface is currently published; the meqinsights.com portal is a customer login.

providers.name: ECOVACS Robotics
providers.description: ECOVACS Robotics is a global home service robotics company founded in 1998 and headquartered in Suzhou, China, that designs, manufactures, and sells AI-powered autonomous cleaning devices for consumer and commercial use. Its product families include DEEBOT robotic vacuum and mopping robots, WINBOT window-cleaning robots, GOAT robotic lawn mowers, ULTRAMARINE pool-cleaning robots, and the DEEBOT PRO commercial line, all managed through the ECOVACS HOME mobile app. The company was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of IDG Capital; as of this enrichment pass ECOVACS publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documented API surface — this profile captures its public web, support, and legal properties plus a domain-security probe.

providers.name: Silicon Box
providers.description: Silicon Box Pte Ltd is an independent advanced semiconductor packaging and chiplet integration company headquartered in Tampines, Singapore, founded in 2021 by Byung Joon Han, Sehat Sutardja and Weili Dai. It operates a $2B panel-level packaging foundry and provides the back-end interconnection infrastructure that makes chiplet adoption practical — from early design collaboration through final manufacture and test — functioning as an OSAT with an added design-consulting practice. It has shipped over 500 million units at high yield, joined the imec Automotive Chiplet Program, and is building a second €3.2B facility in Novara, Piedmont, Italy. Silicon Box is a semiconductor manufacturer, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer program, no API documentation and no machine-readable API contract. See x-coverage below for the measured basis of that statement.

providers.name: Xtalic
providers.description: Xtalic Corporation is a materials technology company founded in 2005 out of MIT by professor Chris Schuh and Dr. Alan Lund, headquartered in Marlborough, Massachusetts, with technical support and sales teams in Shanghai, South China, and Singapore. Its patented computational materials design platform tailors nanostructured metal alloys - XTRONIC nickel, LUNA silver, XTALIUM aluminum, PALLEX palladium, XENERGY soft magnetic, and XEFORM nickel-gold - as high-performance, sustainable replacements for traditional metals and precious-metal plating in electronics connectors, EV powertrains and charging systems, wireless charging, and wearables. Xtalic publishes no public API or developer surface.

providers.name: 21 Market
providers.description: 21 Market is the API Evangelist network profile for 주식회사 21세기전파상 (21st Century Electronics Shop Co., Ltd.), a South Korean consumer-electronics resale company that operates the Repercent (리퍼센트) service at repercent.com. Repercent buys used smartphones and mobile devices — iPhone, Galaxy, tablets, and laptops — from individual sellers, providing instant online price quotes, fast payment, and a simple pickup/logistics flow for secondhand device trade-in. The company is a 500 Global portfolio company and was surfaced into the network as a venture portfolio lead. As of this pass the company publishes no public developer program, API, or documentation surface; this profile captures verified company identity, its live web properties, and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Alterego
providers.description: Alterego is a Boston-based startup, spun out of the MIT Media Lab in 2025, building a near-telepathic silent-speech interface: a minimal, non-invasive wearable that detects the faint neuromuscular signals produced when a person internally verbalizes words, letting them interact with AI and computers without typing, tapping, or speaking aloud. Its "Silent Sense" technology responds only to intentional internal speech, keeping private thoughts private while enabling hands-free, screen-free messaging, queries, and information access. The company is pre-launch, backed by investors including Canaan, Granite Ventures, Mayfield, Rembrandt Venture Partners, and Cisco Investments. As of this profile Alterego publishes no public API or developer platform.

providers.name: Armstrong Robotics
providers.description: Armstrong Robotics is building general-purpose robots for commercial kitchens, beginning with autonomous dishwashing systems that load, run, and unload dishware without human intervention. Backed by Bloomberg Beta, the company is an early-stage robotics startup focused on kitchen labor automation. It currently exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation; it was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-sourced lead awaiting a public API surface, and this profile carries only the identity and domain-security signals that could be verified from its public website.

providers.name: B2X
providers.description: B2X is a Munich-founded hardware lifecycle orchestration company that manages the complete service journey of electronic devices for global brands and operators — from warehousing, staging and onsite deployment through customer support, maintenance and repair, returns management, refurbishment and recycling. Its proprietary B2XONE platform combines ONE Connect (self-service customer portals with track & trace and appointment booking), ONE Service (operations management for repair, warehouse, inventory and logistics) and ONE Analytics (real-time KPIs and predictive insights), delivered through a network of 155+ certified service partners across 25+ countries. B2X serves mobile and consumer electronics, retail automation, B2B/enterprise and mission-critical segments. As of this profile, B2X does not publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: De-Ice
providers.description: De-Ice Technologies is a Somerville, Massachusetts deep-tech aviation startup building a chemical-free aircraft de-icing system that replaces conventional glycol spray with electrically heated strips applied to aircraft surfaces, removing snow and ice prior to takeoff. The technology eliminates weather-related departure delays, cuts glycol spraying costs, and reduces CO₂ emissions from idling fuel burn and chemical production. Named to Time's Best Inventions of 2024, De-Ice counts Air Canada as its launch customer and is backed by Techstars. This is a physical-hardware aviation company and does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Opalcamera
providers.description: Opal Electronics is an original hardware company based in California specializing in the design and engineering of premium webcams and creator-focused camera devices. Its products include the Opal C1, a professional-grade webcam built around a large image sensor and DSLR-style optics, and the Opal Tadpole, an ultra-compact clip-on webcam for laptops, paired with the Opal Composer desktop software that adds virtual-camera, scene, and streaming controls. The company is backed by Kindred Ventures. Opal runs a consumer hardware business and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or partner platform; this profile captures its public web presence and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Prototyping.io
providers.description: Prototyping.io is a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) startup building AI-driven autonomous manufacturing for mechanical parts. The platform converts CAD designs into finished physical parts by automating design-for-manufacturability analysis, manufacturability evaluation, production planning, machine execution, and quality control across CNC machining, sheet metal, 3D printing, injection molding, extrusion, and die casting. Founded by Revanth Bodepudi (CEO) and Prerit Oberai (CTO) in the San Francisco Bay Area, it targets hardware teams in robotics, AI infrastructure, energy, automotive, and defense, aiming to cut hardware iteration cycles from weeks to days with no minimum order quantities and tight tolerances. The company is in early-access/waitlist stage and does not yet publish a public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Seeqc
providers.description: Seeqc is developing the first digital quantum computing platform for businesses, integrating all core functions of a quantum computer - qubits together with classical control logic - onto a single superconducting chip operating at millikelvin temperatures. Founded in 2019 and holding over 115 patents, the company combines classical and quantum technologies to address the efficiency, stability, and cost challenges endemic to scalable quantum computing, and also offers superconducting chip foundry services. As a quantum-hardware and foundry company, Seeqc currently publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: The Bot Company
providers.description: The Bot Company is a San Francisco robotics startup founded in 2024 by Kyle Vogt, the co-founder and former CEO of Cruise, building a helpful general-purpose robot for every home to automate everyday household chores. Its team draws from Tesla, Cruise, OpenAI, Google, and Pixar, and the company has raised roughly $301M (reportedly valued near $2B) from investors including Spark Capital and SV Angel. As of this profile the company operates a marketing and careers site only and publishes no public developer API, SDK, documentation, or developer portal.

providers.name: Visibl Semiconductors
providers.description: Visibl Semiconductors builds an AI-enabled coordination layer for custom chip design teams, positioning itself as "the first coordination layer for chip design." Its platform continuously monitors specifications against implementation to detect drift early, investigates issues by assembling evidence bundles, and proposes fixes through AI agents that require human approval before any change is deployed. The company frames this as a faster path to custom silicon and is backed by Y Combinator. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a marketing website only and exposes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Neat Pulse API
providers.description: The Pulse API enables direct management of your Pulse devices and organisation. Update device settings, create new rooms and locations, access device sensor data and more.

providers.name: Newlight Technologies
providers.description: Newlight Technologies, Inc. is a Huntington Beach, California biotechnology company founded in 2003 and incorporated in Delaware that produces AirCarbon, a PHB biomaterial made by naturally-occurring ocean microorganisms that consume air and greenhouse gas. The company operates a commercial-scale biomanufacturing plant and sells AirCarbon as resin to industrial partners and as finished goods under the Restore foodware and Covalent fashion-accessory brands, positioning the material as a carbon-negative, home-compostable, ocean-degradable replacement for petroleum plastic. Newlight is a materials manufacturer, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer program, no API reference and no machine-readable contract. Its only agent-reachable surface is the Wix platform Site MCP endpoint that its marketing site advertises in its own llms.txt.

providers.name: Prewitt Ridge
providers.description: Prewitt Ridge builds SysGit, "the collaboration layer for complex hardware" — an enterprise platform that applies software development practices to systems engineering. SysGit provides Git-based version control for requirements and system models, Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) workflows, AI-assisted systems engineering automation, and SysMLv2 compliance for open-standards adherence. The platform targets defense and aerospace teams, with customers including the US Air Force, GTRI, Leidos, and Anduril. Prewitt Ridge is a Techstars-backed company added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, SDK, developer documentation, or .well-known documents.

providers.name: Medivis
providers.description: Medivis is a medical technology company building AI-powered augmented reality solutions for surgery and medical education. Its flagship product, SurgicalAR, is an FDA 510(k)-cleared platform that runs on Microsoft HoloLens 2 and transforms 2D medical imaging (CT and MRI) into interactive 3D holographic visualizations for surgical planning and navigation, including FDA-cleared systems for spine and cranial procedures. Medivis also offers AnatomyX, an AR platform for anatomy and medical education. The company reports deployment across 40+ institutions and use in 2,000+ surgeries. Medivis is a Microsoft technology partner and a portfolio company of Initialized Capital. Medivis publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK; its software surface is delivered as HoloLens and iOS applications for clinical and educational users.

providers.name: Zipline
providers.description: Zipline is a South San Francisco–headquartered autonomous logistics company operating the world's largest commercial drone delivery network, with more than two million customer deliveries flown across the United States, Rwanda, Ghana, Nigeria, Kenya, Côte d'Ivoire, and Japan. Zipline designs, builds, and operates two end-to-end aircraft platforms: Platform 1 (P1, "Sparrow"), a long-range fixed-wing aircraft that launches from a catapult, parachutes payloads from altitude, and is used primarily for national-scale healthcare logistics — delivering blood products, vaccines, medicines, and lab samples to hospitals and clinics — and Platform 2 (P2), a short-range hybrid VTOL aircraft with an autonomous tethered "droid" delivery vehicle that lowers packages from a hovering aircraft directly to a designated point on the ground, enabling precision quick-commerce delivery from restaurants, retailers, pharmacies, and hospitals. Zipline's customer roster includes Walmart, OhioHealth, Michigan Medicine, Cleveland Clinic, Mayo Clinic Florida, MultiCare, Sweetgreen, GNC, Jet's Pizza, the governments of Rwanda, Ghana, Nigeria, and Kenya, and Japan's Toyota Tsusho, with the P2 platform actively scaling across the Dallas–Fort Worth Metroplex, Pea Ridge (AR), and expanding into Houston and Phoenix in 2026. The company also operates one of the largest civil autonomous aviation stacks in the world — proprietary detect-and-avoid, route planning, weather, fleet operations, and flight-control software — and in 2025 received the first-ever FAA Part 135 BVLOS (beyond-visual-line-of-sight) operational approval permitting drone package delivery without visual observers. Zipline is a privately held company; its revenue model is drone-as-a-service contracts with healthcare systems, retailers, restaurant brands, and governments. There is no public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, GitHub organization, status page, changelog, or self-service developer portal — integrations with customer systems (order management, EHR, WMS, dispatch) are delivered as managed enterprise integrations rather than as a public programmable API.

providers.name: DisplayLink
providers.description: DisplayLink, a brand of Synaptics Incorporated, develops USB-based virtual graphics technology that pairs host driver software with a device-side decoder SoC to act as a virtual graphics card. Its adaptive-compression technology powers universal docking stations, USB monitors, adapters, and multi-display setups over USB-C, USB, and Ethernet, spanning products from the entry-level DL-3000/4000 series to the quad-display DL-7000 professional series. DisplayLink is a hardware/semiconductor and driver-software product line rather than a public web-API provider; its developer surface consists of chip SDKs, firmware tooling, and host driver software.

providers.name: Schrödinger
providers.description: Schrödinger is a New York-headquartered (NASDAQ: SDGR) computational science company that develops a physics-based and AI-driven molecular simulation platform used across drug discovery and materials science. Its flagship desktop modeling environment is Maestro (MS Maestro for materials science), which integrates a deep stack of computational tools — Glide (docking), FEP+ (free energy perturbation), Desmond (molecular dynamics), Jaguar (quantum chemistry), Prime (protein structure prediction), BioLuminate (biologics), LigPrep, QikProp, SiteMap, and WaterMap — together with the Schrödinger-maintained PyMOL visualization system. LiveDesign is the cloud-native enterprise design lab where chemists, biologists, and program teams collaborate on molecules, run computational workflows, and integrate experimental data; it exposes a snap-in API framework for connecting in-house and third-party tooling. The Schrödinger Python API (current release 2026-1) is the primary developer surface, providing programmatic access to molecular structures, Maestro automation, jobcontrol, Glide, FEP+, Desmond, Jaguar, MacroModel, Prime, BioLuminate, and LiveDesign integration (login, export, dataset and column management). Schrödinger also ships KNIME extensions, command-line drivers for every computational product, and maintains a meaningful open-source footprint on GitHub — including PyMOL, maeparser, coordgenlibs, sketcher, gpusimilarity, csmiles, and the fixed-data-table-2 React component. The business has two segments — software licensing to global pharma, biotech, and materials companies, and a co-developed and proprietary drug discovery pipeline. There is no public developer signup or self-serve REST API; access to the platform, Python API, and LiveDesign is gated through commercial licensing and the my.schrodinger.com customer portal.

providers.name: Biren Technology
providers.description: Biren Technology (Shanghai Biren Technology Co., Ltd.) is a Chinese fabless semiconductor company that designs general-purpose GPUs (GPGPUs) for AI training, inference, and high-performance computing. Its flagship BR100-series accelerators are programmed through BIRENSUPA, a CUDA-like software platform that bundles the BRCC compiler, a hardware abstraction layer, deep-learning and general-compute acceleration libraries, and a developer toolchain with support for PyTorch, TensorFlow, and PaddlePaddle. Biren distributes its drivers, SDK, and documentation through its developer.birentech.com developer community rather than a public web/REST API. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners.

providers.name: Lassen Peak
providers.description: Lassen Peak, Inc. is a Seattle-area public-safety technology company founded in 2019 by veterans of ultra-high-speed wireless, imaging radar, broadband communications and law enforcement. It builds AirFrisk, a handheld terahertz imaging-radar scanner that detects concealed weapons at a distance without a hands-on pat-down, and ImageVault, the companion cloud console that manages AirFrisk users, devices, scan data, retention policy, alerts, reporting and audit logs for an agency under FBI-CJIS compliant storage. The company has raised roughly $22M across Series A and A1 rounds and holds multiple issued US patents. Lassen Peak sells a device plus a customer-tenant cloud console to police, sheriff and security agencies; as of this profile it publishes no public developer program, no API documentation, no SDKs and no machine-readable contract of any kind on its own domain.

providers.name: Lyte
providers.description: Lyte is a Mountain View, California perception company building an end-to-end integrated vision system for robotics and Physical AI. Founded in 2021 by Alexander Shpunt, Arman Hajati and Yuval Gerson — architects of Apple's depth-sensing and Face ID perception stack, and, in Shpunt's case, co-founder and CTO of PrimeSense — the company emerged from stealth in January 2026 with $107M in aggregate funding from Fidelity Management & Research, Atreides Management, Exor Ventures, Key1 Capital, Avigdor Willenz's group and Venture Tech Alliance. Its flagship product, LyteVision, combines 4D sensing (distance plus velocity), RGB imaging and inertial motion awareness with custom silicon and software into a single plug-and-play perception platform for robots, mobility and next-generation automation; it won a CES 2026 Best of Innovation award in Robotics and was named an honoree in Vehicle Tech and Advanced Mobility. Lyte is collaborating with NVIDIA to stream perception into GPUs over Holoscan Sensor Bridge (zero-copy, Jetson Thor, CUDA, NITROS) and into Omniverse and Isaac Sim for real-time digital twins. Lyte ships hardware and an embedded perception stack rather than a developer platform, and publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable contract as of this profile.

providers.name: xiaoyi
providers.description: Xiaoyi Technology (小蚁科技), operated by Shanghai Yunyi Zhilian Technology (上海云蚁智联) and best known for its YI-brand cameras, is a Shanghai-based smart-imaging company that emerged from the Xiaomi ecosystem. It builds action cameras, the M1 mirrorless camera, smart home/security cameras, dash cams and in-car rearview systems, VR cameras, and handheld gimbals, and now positions itself around computer vision, edge intelligence, and edge computing solutions for smart mobility, smart home, smart retail, smart parks, and smart communities, selling through JD and Tmall storefronts. Surfaced as a Qiming Venture Partners portfolio company. No public developer API surface was found during enrichment - the developer subdomain (dev.xiaoyi.com) returns 502, api.xiaoyi.com serves only a placeholder page, and no API documentation, OpenAPI specs, official GitHub organization, or first-party registry packages were located.

providers.name: Hexcel
providers.description: Hexcel Corporation (NYSE: HXL) is a global leader in advanced composite materials for the aerospace, defense and space, and industrial markets. Headquartered in Stamford, Connecticut and operating roughly 18 manufacturing facilities worldwide with about 5,800 employees, Hexcel produces HexTow carbon fiber, HexPly prepregs, HexWeb honeycomb, HexForce reinforcements, HexBond adhesives, HexFlow infusion resins, and HexTool tooling materials supplied into commercial aircraft, military platforms, space launch vehicles, wind energy blades, and industrial structures. Hexcel is a critical materials supplier to Boeing and Airbus and supports more than 100 defense programs; it has no public developer portal, REST APIs, SDKs, or machine-readable product catalog. Customer interaction with technical resources is PDF-based (datasheets, technology manuals, brochures), and the company's GitHub organization (github.com/Hexcel) is registered but empty.

providers.name: Physicsx
providers.description: PhysicsX is an AI-native engineering software company, founded in 2020 and headquartered in London (Shoreditch) with an office in New York, building a platform that embeds physics AI directly into industrial engineering and manufacturing workflows. The platform unifies simulation, physics AI, data, and engineering applications into a single foundation, pairing fast AI-driven physics inference (Deep Physics Models) with numerical simulation to compress development cycles and expand the design space engineers can explore. It integrates with industry-standard CAE/CAD tooling (ANSYS, CATIA, Siemens NX, OpenFOAM, Siemens Star-CCM+), runs cloud-agnostically across AWS and Azure plus hybrid and on-premises deployments, and serves aerospace and defense, automotive, semiconductors, materials, and energy and renewables. Born out of Formula One, PhysicsX has raised roughly $489M across five rounds from investors including General Catalyst, Atomico, Temasek, NVIDIA, Siemens, and Applied Materials. There is no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time; this profile captures the company identity and public web properties.

providers.name: Aclarity Water
providers.description: Aclarity, Inc. (Aclarity Water) is a Medway, Massachusetts cleantech company that designs and manufactures on-site PFAS destruction technology. Its flagship Aclarity Octa system uses electrochemical oxidation to break the carbon-fluorine bond in per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), destroying these "forever chemicals" at landfills, centralized waste-treatment facilities, industrial sites (laundry, pulp and paper, automotive), municipal and industrial wastewater, drinking-water treatment, and AFFF-contaminated aviation sites. Aclarity is a portfolio company of DCVC. It is a physical water-treatment hardware and services business with no public developer API surface; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company intelligence.

providers.name: Eleqtron
providers.description: eleQtron GmbH is a German quantum computing hardware company founded in 2020 as a spin-off from the Quantum Optics Department at the University of Siegen by Prof. Dr. Christof Wunderlich, Dr. Michael Johanning (CTO), and Jan Leisse (CEO). Based in Siegen, Germany, eleQtron develops freely programmable, scalable trapped-ion quantum computers built on its proprietary MAGIC (Magnetic Gradient Induced Coupling) technology, which controls qubits with microwaves rather than lasers for higher precision and a clearer path to scaling. The company aims to become a leading provider of quantum computing time for industrial applications across chemicals, pharmaceuticals, automotive, logistics, finance, and machine learning. eleQtron's systems are made accessible to developers through cloud platforms and standard quantum frameworks (Qiskit, Cirq, PennyLane) rather than a first-party public REST API. Backed by Earlybird Venture Capital.

providers.name: Frore Systems
providers.description: Frore Systems is a Silicon Valley thermal-management company that develops solid-state active cooling technology for high-performance computing in space-constrained devices. Its flagship AirJet solid-state cooling chips (AirJet Mini and AirJet PAK families) and LiquidJet direct-to-chip liquid cooling for data centers enable higher power density, quieter operation, and thinner designs across consumer devices, mini PCs, industrial embedded systems, and data-center compute trays. The company partners with Intel, Qualcomm, NVIDIA, AMD, Phison, and Zotac, is headquartered in Silicon Valley with manufacturing in Taiwan, and reached unicorn status following a Series D round. Frore is a hardware/semiconductor company with no public developer API surface; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company identity and market coverage.

providers.name: Graphite Innovation and Technologies
providers.description: Graphite Innovation and Technologies Inc, operating as GIT Coatings, is a Canadian materials-science company that develops sustainable, graphene-based marine coatings for commercial ships. Its biocide-free hard foul-release hull and propeller coatings, including XGIT-FORCE, XGIT-VORTEX, and XGIT-PROP, cut fuel consumption, reduce drag, and eliminate leaching to protect the marine environment. The company is a Techstars-backed portfolio company. It is a physical-products manufacturer and publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company-level discovery and coverage.

providers.name: MeetFuture Technology
providers.description: MeetFuture Technology (弥费科技) is a Shanghai-based, global-leading supplier of semiconductor Automated Material Handling Systems (AMHS) and core components, founded in 2014. It designs and manufactures overhead hoist transport (OHT), stocker/storage, purge, and AMHS control-software solutions for semiconductor wafer fabrication plants, integrating with fab MES systems over SEMI equipment communication standards (E37/HSMS, E30/GEM, E82, E84, E10). MeetFuture holds 300+ intellectual-property items, operates China's largest AMHS cleanroom test center, authored China's first semiconductor OHT standard (T/SICA 006—2024), and won the 2025 SEMI Product Innovation Award. It is a Qiming Venture Partners portfolio company. MeetFuture is an industrial semiconductor-equipment maker and does not publish a public web API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile is maintained for network identity and discovery.

providers.name: Orqa
providers.description: Orqa is an aerial robotics company founded in 2018 and headquartered in Osijek, Croatia, that designs and manufactures mission-ready FPV (first-person view) drone systems for the defense and enterprise markets. With full vertical integration, Orqa builds every component in-house — tactical drones such as the MRM1-5 and MRM2-10, FPV goggles (FPV.One Pilot), controllers, simulators, and detection equipment — to keep its supply chain secure and its systems high-performance. The company is ISO 9001 certified and backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners (Seed round, 2024, partners Antoine Moyroud and Alexander Schmitt). As of this profile Orqa is a hardware manufacturer and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a programmatic developer surface; this repository tracks it for identity and network completeness.

providers.name: Oxford Ionics
providers.description: Oxford Ionics is a quantum computing hardware company founded in Oxford, UK that designs and builds trapped-ion quantum computers powered by its proprietary Electronic Qubit Control (EQC) technology, which uses integrated semiconductor chips rather than lasers to control qubits. The company holds published records across single-qubit gate fidelity, two-qubit gate fidelity, and state preparation/measurement, and builds compact, field-upgradeable, data-center-ready QPUs that fit standard server racks and integrate with AWS and NVIDIA stacks. Its roadmap targets 16-64 qubits (2025), 256+ qubits (2026), and 10,000+ qubits (2027). Oxford Ionics was acquired by IonQ in 2025. As of this profile the company publishes no public developer API, SDKs, MCP server, or API documentation surface.

providers.name: Syntetica
providers.description: Syntetica is a French cleantech company using green chemistry to close the loop on synthetic textiles, starting with nylon. Its proprietary chemical process depolymerises nylon-blend fabrics, separating and purifying Nylon 6 and Nylon 6,6 from elastane, cotton, and other fibres in a single process to produce virgin-quality, low-carbon recycled polymers that drop in as replacements for fossil-derived nylon across textile, automotive, and high-performance applications. Backed by EQT Ventures, Bpifrance, SWEN Capital Partners, lululemon, and MAS Holdings, the company raised a $30M Series A in July 2026 to build its first commercial demonstration facility in France. Syntetica is a materials-science and manufacturing company; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: 6K
providers.description: 6K Inc is a North Andover, Massachusetts advanced-materials company that produces engineered powders and battery materials with UniMelt, its patented microwave-based production-scale plasma system. Named for the roughly 6,000 K plasma temperature it operates at — the temperature of the surface of the sun — UniMelt uses tightly controlled thermal plasma beams to melt or vaporize precursor feedstock into particles with precise size distribution and crystalline phase, in seconds rather than the days conventional processes require, while cutting energy use and eliminating wastewater. The company operates through two divisions. 6K Additive, with production in Burgettstown, Pennsylvania, makes sustainably sourced metal powders for additive manufacturing — titanium Ti-6Al-4V, nickel superalloys Ni625 and Ni718, stainless SS316L, refractory tungsten, niobium C103, copper C18150 and the HEA1000 refractory alloy — reclaiming CNC scrap and revert metal into premium AM powder. 6K Energy produces domestically sourced lithium-ion battery cathode and solid-state materials including NMC, LFP, LLZO, LMO, LTO and LNMO. Additional applications span semiconductor CMP, specialty ceramics, advanced coatings, lighting and display materials, nano-engineered powders, and federal/defense programs; 6K has received US Department of Defense and Department of Energy awards for domestic critical-materials capacity. 6K is a privately held company whose shares trade on secondary markets. Enrichment probing on 2026-07-31 found no public developer API, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI/GraphQL contract, developer portal, SDK, MCP server, agent card, or event surface — 6K is a materials manufacturer, not an API provider.

providers.name: Claros
providers.description: Claros is a data center power delivery company reimagining how energy moves from chip to grid for AI and high-performance computing infrastructure. Based in Torrance, California with an office in McLean, Virginia, the company builds two hardware-and-software product lines: an Integrated Voltage Regulator (IVR) that targets the roughly 40 percent of chip power lost to heat at the point of delivery, and a Power Gateway that manages broader data center power distribution where 30 to 50 percent of power is lost to transmission, conversion, and cooling.
