Claros is an early-stage hardware company backed by General Catalyst and Red Cell Partners; its founding team collectively holds 286 patents and has brought more than 80 gigawatts of projects to market. As of 2026 it is pre-product (prototypes in development, engineering samples planned for 2026, low-volume production 2027, high-volume scale 2028) and publishes no developer API, SDK, or public documentation surface yet — this profile captures its public identity for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: CMC Materials
providers.description: CMC Materials is a global supplier of consumable materials primarily to the semiconductor industry, including chemical mechanical planarization (CMP) slurries and polishing pads. Acquired by Entegris in 2022, CMC's materials portfolio is now part of the Entegris specialty chemicals and CMP solutions business, serving semiconductor manufacturers through advanced materials and process technologies.

providers.name: I-Pulse
providers.description: I-Pulse Inc. is a U.S.-based industrial technology company founded in 2007 by Robert Friedland and Laurent Frescaline that commercializes High Pulsed Power (HPP) — releasing very short, extremely high-power electrical discharges from small amounts of stored energy to generate magnetic forces, shockwaves, electrical arcs and electric fields. I-Pulse holds 55 patents licensed exclusively to its operating businesses across natural-resource transformation (I-ROX rock comminution, I-Mine, iTerra non-chemical weed control, IPW), the energy transition (G-Pulse pulsed-power geothermal drilling, Blue Spark Geothermal), manufacturing (Bmax electromagnetic metal forming and welding, CSI Technologies high-energy capacitors) and R&D (I-Cube, Typhoon). It operates from Albuquerque, New Mexico and Toulouse, France, with offices in Canada, the UK and Singapore, and signed a $250 million CHIPS R&D award with the U.S. Department of Commerce in 2026 for semiconductor and pulsed-power development. I-Pulse is a hardware and industrial-process company; it publishes no developer program, API documentation or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Novo Space
providers.description: Novo Space develops high-performance, radiation-tolerant, modular electronics for the most ambitious space missions. Founded by Rodrigo Diez (CEO) and Facundo Jorge (CTO), the company builds SpaceVPX single-board computers, mass memory and GPU boards, tailored subsystems, and radiation-tolerant FPGA IP cores (SpaceWire, SpaceFibre, Ethernet/TCP-IP, CCSDS, NAND controllers, floating-point units) that let satellite and spacecraft builders reuse qualified hardware instead of re-engineering every mission. Customers and partners include Maxar, MIT, Thales Alenia Space, BAE Systems, Leonardo DRS, Mitsubishi, the US Air Force, Nvidia, Ansys, and Microchip. Novo Space is a space-computing hardware provider and does not publish a public web API, developer portal, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: Asto CT
providers.description: Asto CT, Inc. is a Middleton, Wisconsin medical-imaging device manufacturer that designs and builds Equina, a robotically positioned, weight-bearing fan-beam computed tomography (CT) scanner purpose-built for imaging mildly sedated, standing horses. Founded on a 2016 concept and first installed at UW-Madison in 2019, the company sells capital imaging equipment plus installation, training and ongoing clinical support to equine hospitals and veterinary teaching hospitals worldwide, with offices in Middleton, Wisconsin and Crawley, United Kingdom. Asto CT is a hardware company: the Equina system is operated from an on-site console and the company publishes no public developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable interface contract.

providers.name: Avicena Tech
providers.description: Avicena Tech Corp. is a privately held semiconductor company founded in 2019 and headquartered in Sunnyvale, California, with a subsidiary in Edinburgh, Scotland. Avicena develops LightBundle, a microLED-based optical interconnect architecture for chip-to-chip, die-to-die and rack-scale links in AI/ML training clusters, high-performance computing, memory disaggregation, sensors, 5G wireless and aerospace. The technology pairs patented microLED emitter arrays with photodetector arrays and an integrated ASIC, supporting greater than 1Tbps/mm shoreline density at sub-picojoule-per-bit energy efficiency over reaches beyond 10 meters. The company ships a LightBundle eKit evaluation system to AI infrastructure customers and is backed by Tiger Global, SK hynix, Samsung Catalyst Fund, Micron Ventures, Clear Ventures, Cerberus Capital Management, Hitachi Ventures, LAM Research, Maverick Silicon, Prosperity7 Ventures and VentureTech Alliance. Avicena is a hardware and photonics company: it publishes no public developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Cambridge Terahertz
providers.description: Cambridge Terahertz (thzcorp.com) is an MIT-spinout physical security company building compact, AI-powered terahertz imaging sensors that detect concealed weapons -- guns, knives, explosives, and 3D-printed weapons -- as people walk naturally through entrances, without pat-downs or metal detectors. The 2-pound sensors mount like security cameras, serve hospitals, enterprises, and government facilities, and integrate with existing VMS and security systems over standard REST APIs, though the company publishes no public developer portal or API documentation. Backed by Felicis with a $12M seed round and an NSF SBIR Phase II grant.

providers.name: Onsitego
providers.description: Onsitego is a Mumbai-based Indian consumer device-protection company that sells extended warranty, accidental and liquid damage protection, and repair and maintenance (AMC) plans for consumer electronics and home appliances including mobile phones, laptops, televisions, refrigerators, washing machines and air conditioners. Sold at point of sale through 10,000+ retail stores and serviced via 3,300+ service centers, the company reports 2.5+ crore (25M+) customers and lets buyers activate coverage, manage devices and plans, and request service online. Onsitego is a portfolio company of Accel. No public developer API, documentation, or programmatic surface was found during enrichment; this profile captures the company identity and probed domain security posture.

providers.name: SCENARIO-X GLOBAL HOLDING PTE. LTD.
providers.description: SCENARIO-X GLOBAL HOLDING PTE. LTD. (Scenario X) is a financial-technology company building an AI- and quantum-computing-powered platform for financial risk analysis, stress testing, and regulatory reporting. The integrated platform is organized into four modules — Scenario (adverse market-condition design), PPNR (Pre-Provision Net Revenue projection), Risk (market, counterparty, credit, and operational risk), and Console (financial-data aggregation) — plus a quantum-computing offering for predictive financial modeling. It serves banks, insurers, family offices, independent wealth managers, and commodity traders. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and tracked in the API Evangelist network; no public API or developer surface has been found to date.

providers.name: ClearMotion
providers.description: ClearMotion is an automotive motion-technology company founded out of MIT in 2012 by Zack Anderson and Shakeel Avadhany, headquartered at its US innovation lab in Billerica, Massachusetts, with a UK engineering hub at MIRA Technology Park in Nuneaton, a Shanghai office, and a production plant in Changshu, China. Its CM1 fully active suspension system pairs the ActiValve digital hydraulic actuator with software that counteracts road disturbances in milliseconds, and its RoadMotion service is a crowdsourced, cloud-based road-surface intelligence layer that fuses data from vehicle sensors into a high-definition surface map accurate to better than 20mm, feeding proactive suspension, chassis and ADAS decisions. The company absorbed the Bose Ride and Project Sound active-suspension programs, is led by CEO Christian Steinmann, and ships with NIO (ET9, ES9) alongside collaborations with Porsche, BWI Group and Sona Comstar. Marketing material describes RoadMotion as an "end-to-end cloud API solution", but ClearMotion publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, machine-readable specification, SDKs or /.well-known discovery surface — the API is an OEM/B2B integration rather than a self-serve public API.

providers.name: Efference AI
providers.description: Efference AI is a robotics perception and compute company building the hardware-plus-software foundation for data-driven robotics at scale. Founded in 2025 by Gianluca Bencomo and based in San Francisco (Y Combinator Fall 2025), Efference treats machine vision as a software problem, pairing affordable stereo-camera hardware with learned 3D-perception foundation models ("cheap hardware + great algorithms"). Its M1 device targets distributed, robotics-grade data collection at scale, while the H1 stereo system is built for real-time cloud inference with foundation models. The company serves autonomous vehicles, humanoid robots, and drones, and publishes hardware-interfacing documentation and firmware through its GitHub organization. As of this profile Efference exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or authenticated service surface.

providers.name: Firestorm
providers.description: Firestorm (Firestorm Labs, Inc.) is a San Diego based defense technology company founded in 2022 that builds expeditionary manufacturing systems and modular unmanned aerial systems. Its xCELL containerized production unit uses HP Multi Jet Fusion additive manufacturing to 3D print industrial-grade PA-12 nylon composite airframes and spare parts at the tactical edge, feeding modular UAS platforms including the Tempest fixed-wing family and the Squall FPV drone. The company holds a five-year, $100M U.S. Air Force IDIQ and closed an $82M Series B in April 2026 led by Washington Harbour Partners. Firestorm ships hardware, not software: as of this profiling pass it publishes no developer portal, no public API, and no machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Hydrow
providers.description: Hydrow (legally True Rowing, Inc., Boston, Massachusetts) is a connected-fitness hardware company that makes the Hydrow indoor rowing machine and the LYQUID strength-training platform, sold with a subscription to a library of live and on-demand athlete-led workouts filmed on real water. Members interact with Hydrow through its rower touchscreens and the Hydrow iOS/Android companion apps, which sync workout summaries outward to Strava and Apple Health. Hydrow operates a real production backend for those apps, but publishes no public developer program, no API reference, no OpenAPI or other machine-readable contract, and no first-party SDK in any package registry; its developer-facing subdomains do not resolve to a service. Its public machine-readable surface is limited to an Atlassian Statuspage.

providers.name: OctoAI
providers.description: OctoAI (formerly OctoML) was a Seattle-based AI inference platform founded in 2019 as a University of Washington Allen School spin-out of the Apache TVM project. The company originally focused on machine-learning model optimization and compilation across CPUs, GPUs, and accelerators, and in June 2023 launched a generative-AI SaaS inference platform that served open-source foundation models (Llama 2, Mixtral, SDXL, Stable Diffusion, Whisper) behind OpenAI-style REST APIs with Python and TypeScript SDKs. In January 2024 OctoML formally rebranded to OctoAI and in April 2024 unveiled OctoStack, a self-contained generative-AI production stack for deploying models inside customer VPC and on-premises environments across NVIDIA GPUs, AMD GPUs, and AWS Inferentia. NVIDIA acquired OctoAI in September 2024 for a reported $165M (down from a 2021 peak valuation of ~$900M), with CEO Luis Ceze and key staff joining NVIDIA. OctoAI sent customers a "Wind down of OctoAI Services" notice and terminated all hosted endpoints, accounts, and SDK access on 31 October 2024. The octo.ai domain now 301-redirects to nvidia.com and no public OctoAI product, API, dashboard, or developer portal remains; the technology has been absorbed into NVIDIA's internal AI inference stack and is not separately purchasable. This catalog entry is a historical record of the former OctoAI developer surface and the GitHub artifacts that remain.

providers.name: clounix
providers.description: Clounix (云合智网, Yunhe Zhiwang) is a fabless semiconductor company founded in 2020 and headquartered in Shanghai, with additional offices in Hangzhou, Nanjing, Beijing, and Chengdu. It designs high-end networking and communication silicon — high-performance programmable Ethernet switch chips, DPUs (Data Processing Units), and SmartNIC intelligent network cards — along with cloud-native infrastructure hardware and customized software for data centers and 5G networks. Its switch platforms run the open-source SONiC network operating system, and the company maintains a public GitHub organization with SONiC/SAI networking software. Clounix is a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. It currently publishes no public developer-facing API, SDK, or documentation portal.

providers.name: Dotterel
providers.description: Dotterel Technologies is an Auckland, New Zealand acoustics and audio-hardware company founded in 2015 out of the Callaghan Innovation C-Prize. It began by solving drone noise, building acoustic shrouds, low-noise propellers, and onboard active audio-recording systems for UAVs used in film, security, and noise mapping. That work led to Konos (now marketed as Konos Digital), an 80-element directional MEMS microphone array with a continuously variable 60-300 degree beam width that streams four channels of AES67 / SMPTE ST 2110 audio over a single Power-over-Ethernet cable, targeting film, broadcast, and live-sports production. The microphone exposes a firmware-updatable on-device HTTP control interface (a web page plus a POST control endpoint for beam steering) rather than a public developer web API. Dotterel is backed by Techstars (Adelaide 2017 cohort) and is tracked here as a hardware company; it publishes no public API specification, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Entalpic
providers.description: Entalpic is an AI-driven materials science company that designs molecules and materials for industrial processes by combining machine learning, atomistic simulations, and experimental feedback loops to engineer surfaces and materials at the atomic scale. Its work spans a Discovery Engine for high-throughput screening of chemical spaces, process modeling with ML-plus-CFD digital twins, and quantum/atomistic simulation for surface chemistry, applied to semiconductors and thin-film coatings, battery cathode and interface chemistry, catalysis and active-site design, and advanced specialty materials. Founded in 2024 with research roots at the Mila AI lab, the company is based at Station F in Paris and Mila in Montreal and raised an 8.5M euro seed round. Entalpic does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation; this profile tracks its public web surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: KEENON Robotics
providers.description: KEENON Robotics is a global commercial service-robotics company founded in 2010 and headquartered in Shanghai, China, designing and manufacturing autonomous service robots deployed across more than 70 countries and 600+ cities. Its product lines span catering and delivery robots (the T-series and W3), the KLEENBOT commercial floor-cleaning range (C20/C30/C40/C55), heavy-load delivery robots (S100/S300), humanoid service robots (XMAN-R1/XMAN-F1), hospital and hotel logistics solutions (including the WITMED medical line), and the Keenmow K1 domestic robot. KEENON is a hardware-and-solutions company; as of this profile it publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI. This record is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company profile.

providers.name: MKS Instruments
providers.description: MKS Instruments is a global provider of foundational technology solutions for semiconductor manufacturing, electronics and packaging, and specialty industrial markets. Its product portfolio spans vacuum and gas delivery systems, photonics, lasers, optics, motion control, and process control. No public developer API or developer portal has been identified at the corporate level; technical integration is typically handled through product-level documentation, sales engineering, and partner channels.

providers.name: Nothing
providers.description: Nothing is a London-based consumer technology company designing smartphones (Phone series), wireless earbuds (Ear series), and other consumer hardware under the Nothing and CMF by Nothing brands, backed by EQT Ventures and GV. Surfaced as a portfolio-company lead in the API Evangelist network. An enrichment pass confirmed Nothing publishes a consumer web presence (support centre, community, careers, playground) but no public developer API, API documentation, developer portal, SDK, or webhook surface as of this pass.

providers.name: Apptronik
providers.description: Apptronik is an Austin, Texas-based humanoid robotics company founded in 2016 as a spinout from the Human Centered Robotics Lab at the University of Texas at Austin. Co-founded by Jeff Cardenas (CEO), Dr. Nick Paine (CTO), and Dr. Luis Sentis (scientific advisor), the company designs and manufactures Apollo, a general-purpose humanoid robot standing 5'8", weighing 160 lbs, capable of lifting 55 lbs, and running for roughly 4 hours on a swappable battery. Apollo targets warehouse, manufacturing, and logistics applications including trailer unloading, case picking, palletization, machine tending, and workcell delivery. Apptronik has commercial pilot programs and partnerships with Mercedes-Benz (automotive manufacturing logistics), GXO Logistics (multi-phase R&D in U.S. distribution centers), Jabil (supply-chain partner helping scale production and an internal Apollo deployment), and Google DeepMind (Apollo integrates Gemini Robotics vision-language-action models). The company previously built NASA's Valkyrie humanoid and ten-plus other research robots. As of February 2026 Apptronik had raised more than $935M (including a $520M Series A-X extension) at a reported $5B valuation, with investors including B Capital, Google, and Mercedes-Benz. The company sells/leases Apollo to enterprise customers via a direct contact-sales motion and ships a proprietary "point-and-click" control suite for deploying solutions; there is no public developer portal, no published REST/AsyncAPI/gRPC API, no public SDK, no open-source release, and no public GitHub repositories under the `apptronik` org.

providers.name: Auradine (Velaura AI)
providers.description: Auradine, Inc. is a Silicon Valley semiconductor and infrastructure company founded in 2022, in 2026 rebranded as Velaura AI, Inc. The company designs ultra-low-power compute solutions for data center, edge, and physical AI applications, anchored by its Titan Core silicon design and IP platform that reduces the power required for AI compute while maintaining performance. Its Teraflux product line delivers high-efficiency Bitcoin mining hardware (3nm ASICs, air- and hydro-cooled miners, containers, and fleet management software) deployed by leading Bitcoin data center operators. Auradine raised over $300 million across its funding rounds, including a $153M Series C, and is backed by investors including DCVC. This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; Auradine/Velaura AI publishes no public developer API or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Teradar
providers.description: Teradar is a Boston, Massachusetts semiconductor and sensing company founded in 2020 by Matthew Carey, Gregory Charvat and Nicholas Saiz that is commercializing terahertz-band vision sensors for vehicles, defense and security screening. Its Modular Terahertz Engine (MTE) is an all-solid-state chip architecture built from proprietary transmit (TX), receive (RX) and Teracore processing silicon, delivering 0.13-degree native angular resolution at 300+ meters in day, night, rain, fog and snow, positioned to sit alongside cameras and to displace radar and lidar in SAE L1-L5 driver assistance and autonomy programs. The company emerged from stealth in late 2025 with a $150M Series B led by VXI Capital with Ibex Investors, Capricorn Investment Group, The Engine Ventures and Lockheed Martin Ventures, and is working with global OEMs and Tier-One suppliers toward a 2028 model-year launch. Teradar is a hardware and silicon company: it publishes a marketing site and product specification sheets, but no public developer program, API, SDK, or machine-readable interface contract.

providers.name: Mips
providers.description: MIPS is a processor IP and compute company building embedded and edge AI silicon for automotive, robotics, and mission-critical systems. Its portfolio spans the MIPS RISC-V CPU families (M8500, I8500, P8700, S8200), the ARC processor and NPX/VPX accelerator lines, and development tooling such as MIPS Atlas Explorer virtual platforms and the ASIP Designer / ASIP Programmer toolchains. MIPS frames its offering around a "Sense, Think, Act, Communicate" signal chain for real-time autonomy — what it calls Physical AI at the edge. MIPS is a semiconductor IP licensor rather than a public web-API provider; this profile was surfaced as a Mayfield portfolio company and enriched with identity and probed security posture.

providers.name: Path Robotics
providers.description: Path Robotics is a Columbus, Ohio autonomous welding robotics company founded in 2018 by brothers Andy and Alex Lonsberry (CEO and CTO) out of Case Western Reserve University. The company builds AI-powered intelligent welding cells that automate metal fabrication for defense shipyards, utility and energy infrastructure, data centers, and heavy industry. Its core technology is Obsidian, a physical-AI reinforcement-learning agent trained inside Path's proprietary Weld World Model on tens of millions of welded inches; Obsidian runs at the edge of each cell and makes real-time, seam-by-seam welding decisions using a sensor stack of two cameras plus four lasers that deliver sub-millimeter 360-degree awareness around the torch. Path markets the cells with a CapEx-free consumption model and reports 97%+ first-pass yield, 4x productivity, and 30% lower welding costs across customers including HII (America's largest military shipbuilder), Saronic, LAD Services, Tycrop, Mine Rite Technologies, and Millerbernd. In April 2026 Path announced Rove, a mobile welding system mounted on a quadruped platform, extending its addressable geometry beyond fixed-cell applications. The company has raised approximately $271M across Seed through Series D from Drive Capital, Matter Venture Partners, Tiger Global, Addition, and Yamaha Motor Ventures, with the most recent $100M Series D closing in October 2024. Path Robotics has no public developer API, SDK, or webhook surface; its GitHub organization contains roughly 50 repositories that are almost entirely upstream open-source forks (ROS, protobuf, abseil, ceres-solver, pytorch3d, etc.) used as internal build dependencies rather than published developer artifacts. Revenue is earned through welding-cell deployments, services, and the consumable weld-output model — not API monetization.

providers.name: AheadComputing
providers.description: AheadComputing Inc. is a Portland, Oregon fabless semiconductor startup founded in 2024 by former Intel CPU architects — CEO Debbie Marr, Jonathon Pearce, Mark Dechene and Srikanth Srinivasan — that designs and licenses high-performance 64-bit RISC-V application processor cores. The company markets a clean-slate, massive out-of-order "big core" architecture aimed at eliminating per-core CPU bottlenecks for AI, cloud, client, mobile and edge workloads, and has raised roughly $53M across a $21.5M seed and a $30M Seed2 round co-led by Eclipse, Toyota Ventures and Cambium. Its product is silicon IP licensed to chip designers rather than software, so it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Cambium
providers.description: Cambium is an advanced materials company (Cambium Biomaterials, El Segundo, California, founded 2019) that molecularly re-engineers polymers from first principles, pairing AI-driven molecular design with chemistry, materials science, biology, and agile domestic manufacturing to develop and scale next-generation materials roughly 10x faster than traditional methods. Product lines span thermal protection systems, high-temperature structural polymers, and laser/directed-energy protection, serving aerospace, space, defense, motorsport, automotive, marine, and industrial customers. Its SHD Advanced Composites business runs rapid-response prepreg manufacturing across the US, UK, and EU. Backed by 8VC. Cambium publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal; this profile captures corporate identity and probed domain security only.

providers.name: DeepSight Technology
providers.description: DeepSight Technology is a medical-imaging company reinventing diagnostic ultrasound. It is building a semiconductor-based ultrasound sensor and imaging platform (including its NeedleVue technology) to deliver a step-change in ultrasound performance, making this safe, non-invasive, radiation-free, low-cost imaging modality far more usable across clinical applications. The company is a hardware and medical-device business backed by Wing Venture Capital and Deerfield; it is added to the API Evangelist network as a Wing portfolio lead. It does not currently publish a public developer program, API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Diamond Foundry
providers.description: Diamond Foundry is a deep-tech materials company that manufactures semiconductor-grade single-crystal diamond wafers and diamond transistors to overcome the thermal limits of silicon in AI chips, datacenters, and electric vehicles. The company operates its own foundries and has built a full technology stack for producing diamond at scale as a sustainable substrate for high-performance and power electronics. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a planetary-health portfolio company of Obvious Ventures; it publishes no public developer API or documentation at this time.

providers.name: Ecolectro
providers.description: Ecolectro is an Ithaca, New York materials-science company developing alkaline exchange membrane (AEM) technology for green hydrogen production. Its patented ionomers and membranes combine the low-cost, non-precious-metal chemistry of traditional alkaline electrolysis with the performance and efficiency of PEM electrolyzers, targeting roughly a 78% reduction in electrolyzer stack cost and a 33% reduction in the overall levelized cost of green hydrogen. A Cornell University spin-out backed by Techstars, Ecolectro partners with industrial gas and energy companies to manufacture and deploy its membrane materials at scale. Ecolectro publishes no public API or developer surface; this profile captures its corporate identity and domain security posture.

providers.name: Eyebot
providers.description: Eyebot is a health-technology company building automated, self-serve vision testing kiosks that generate precise eyeglass prescriptions in minutes without a traditional eye-doctor appointment. The company deploys robotic screening kiosks into retail environments — partnering with large retailers such as Walmart and Sam's Club — to make refractive vision care faster, cheaper, and more accessible. Founded by Matthias Hofmann (CEO) and Jack Moldave (CTO) with Chief Medical Officer Alex Martin OD FAAO, Eyebot raised a $20M Series A and is backed by General Catalyst, Ubiquity Ventures, Village Global, and the National Science Foundation. Eyebot is currently a hardware-and-retail company with no public developer program, API, or SDK surface; this profile tracks its identity in the API Evangelist network pending any future developer offering.

providers.name: Integral Geometry Science
providers.description: Integral Geometry Science Inc. (IGS) is a Kobe University deep-tech spinout founded on 2 April 2012 by Dr. Kenjiro Kimura, who published the first analytical solution to the inverse problem of wave scattering. IGS turns that mathematics into measurement hardware and imaging software that makes the inside of an object visible without cutting it open: microwave mammography for painless, radiation-free breast cancer screening (designated under Japan's Sakigake scheme), non-destructive current-density imaging for rechargeable battery inspection, walk-through security screening for concealed hazardous materials, and rebar corrosion and fracture inspection for civil infrastructure. The company is headquartered in Kobe, Hyogo, Japan, holds patents across Japan, the United States, China and Europe, and is backed by SBI Investment and Japan's NEDO deep-tech program. IGS sells instruments and diagnostic systems to hospitals, manufacturers and infrastructure operators; it publishes no public developer program, API, or SDK.

providers.name: INURU
providers.description: INURU (Inuru GmbH) is a Berlin-based printed-electronics company that manufactures ultra-thin, flexible printed OLED lighting for smart packaging, labels, apparel, and medical products. Its core product, the Elf (Embeddable Luminous Film), combines an inkjet-printed OLED, a power source, and a microchip into a paper-thin, waterproof film that can glow in any shape and respond to touch, motion, or sound. Founded in 2016, Inuru operates the automated "Dragon Factory" OLED production line in Wildau and works with brands such as Coca-Cola and Marvel on interactive, sustainable smart-packaging and medication-adherence labels. This is a company/provider record in the API Evangelist network; Inuru is a hardware and smart-packaging manufacturer and does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: iTAC Software
providers.description: iTAC Software AG is an independent company of the Duerr Group and a leading provider of Manufacturing Execution System (MES) and Manufacturing Operations Management (MOM) software for discrete manufacturing. Its iTAC.MOM.Suite delivers production control, end-to-end traceability, quality management, and AI-supported analytics that help automotive, electronics, and medical-technology manufacturers implement Industry 4.0 and smart-factory operations. iTAC does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs; system integration is delivered through the MOM platform's IoT and connectivity layers as part of a project engagement.

providers.name: Lynq
providers.description: Lynq Networks develops infrastructure-free, long-range wireless connectivity for enterprise and OEM devices, bridging the gap between short-range Bluetooth and infrastructure-dependent cellular/5G. Its technology lets original equipment manufacturers build large-area device networks without deploying traditional network infrastructure, targeting construction, agriculture, military, and public-safety use cases. Lynq is a Techstars-backed portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API documentation; this profile captures its identity and a domain-security probe for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Nodal Industries
providers.description: Nodal Industries, operating as Nodal Security, is a network security company and 500 Global portfolio startup that makes Numa, a plug-and-play network security appliance providing protective oversight of every connected device on a home or small-office network. Rather than per-device antivirus software, Numa works at the network layer, intercepting malicious traffic before it reaches devices using real-time threat intelligence powered by Suricata, with automatic updates and minimal setup. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a marketing website only and exposes no public API, SDK, developer documentation, or event surface.

providers.name: Openlight
providers.description: OpenLight Photonics is a silicon photonics company that designs and manufactures custom Photonic Application-Specific Integrated Circuits (PASICs) using a heterogeneously integrated, open silicon photonics platform that builds active components such as lasers and modulators onto the same chip as passive waveguides. Operating an open foundry model out of Goleta, California, OpenLight offers three services: design enablement through its Process Design Kit (PDK) with component libraries, evaluation kits, and a PDK Sampler; in-house custom PASIC design; and production manufacturing. Its technology targets datacom, telecom, AI data-center interconnect, lidar, HPC, healthcare, quantum, and IoT sensing. Spun out of Synopsys as an independent, venture-backed company in 2025, OpenLight has raised roughly $84M (a $34M Series A in 2025 and a $50M Series A-1 in 2026) from investors including Mayfield. This is a hardware/semiconductor company; it publishes no public web API, developer portal, or OpenAPI at this time — its developer surface is the chip-design PDK.

providers.name: ProLogium Technology
providers.description: ProLogium Technology Co., Ltd. is a Taiwanese energy-innovation company founded in 2006 that develops and manufactures next-generation solid-state lithium ceramic batteries built around a 100% ceramic separator. It commercialized its first solid-state cells in 2013, opened the world's first giga-level solid-state lithium ceramic battery plant in Taoyuan, Taiwan in 2024, and operates a European R&D center at Paris-Saclay with a planned gigafactory in Dunkirk, France. Its product lines span FLCB, PLCB and LLCB cells plus battery modules and packs, targeting electric vehicles, energy storage systems, robotics, and consumer and industrial applications. ProLogium is a hardware manufacturer: it publishes no developer portal, no public API, and no machine-readable API contract of any kind.

providers.name: Aurorin CAD
providers.description: Aurorin CAD is a San Francisco company building a modern mechanical CAD application for engineers and hardware teams, founded in 2026 by Michael Baron and backed by Y Combinator (Winter 2026 batch). Rather than layering on top of the geometry kernels that underpin incumbent tools such as SolidWorks, NX, Creo, CATIA, Fusion 360 and Onshape, Aurorin has written its own parametric, B-Rep driven CAD kernel designed to exploit modern multi-core CPUs and GPUs and to be AI-native from the foundation rather than as a bolted-on assistant. The product ships as a native desktop application for macOS and Windows, pairing conventional direct and parametric editing with an integrated AI agent driven through a chat interface, with the stated goal of collapsing modeling work that traditionally takes twenty minutes into seconds and avoiding the slow rebuilds and cascading feature breakage common to older parametric systems. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or API documentation; its public surface is a marketing site, a blog, an about/contact page, and careers listings.

providers.name: Praan
providers.description: Praan (Praan Climate Technologies) is a deep-tech climate startup working to democratize access to clean, healthy air and to rebuild the atmosphere by capturing air pollution and greenhouse gases with novel filterless technology. Its products include HIVE, an air-purification device for homes and commercial spaces paired with a companion mobile application, and MK II, an air-purification system for industrial environments. Praan is backed by Prosus Ventures. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio-company lead and enriched through the API Evangelist pipeline; as of this pass Praan publishes a consumer hardware and mobile-app surface but no public developer API, SDK, or documentation.

providers.name: Blixt
providers.description: BL!XT (Blixt) is a Swedish deep-tech company building intelligent, programmable power infrastructure that turns electrical distribution from analog systems into digitally controlled, software-defined platforms. Its products include ZERO, a solid-state current-control switchgear for circuit-level protection, monitoring, and automation; X-VERTER, a software-defined voltage conversion system with integrated energy storage; and THE ZONE, an AI-driven software intelligence layer that coordinates connected distribution devices for real-time analysis, failure prediction, and load balancing. BL!XT serves data centers, industrial manufacturing, maritime vessels, grid providers, and defense. Headquartered in Kista, Sweden and backed by Union Square Ventures. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API or developer surface.

providers.name: Habana Labs
providers.description: Habana Labs is an artificial-intelligence processor company, now part of Intel, that designs deep-learning accelerators for AI training and inference. Its Gaudi (training) and Goya (inference) processors — sold today as the Intel Gaudi 2 and Gaudi 3 AI accelerators — are programmed through the SynapseAI software suite, which integrates with PyTorch and DeepSpeed and ships reference models, containers, and installation tooling. Habana was founded in 2016 in Israel and acquired by Intel in 2019. Its public developer surface is not a hosted web API but an open-source SDK and toolchain: the HabanaAI GitHub organization (reference models, PyTorch bridge, setup/install, plus vLLM and Megatron forks) and the Intel Gaudi documentation at docs.habana.ai. This profile catalogs that developer footprint for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Apoha
providers.description: Apoha is a deep-tech molecular-science company teaching machines to understand matter at the molecular level. Its Liquid State sensory-intelligence platform captures dynamic molecular fingerprints, measuring the biophysical behavior of molecules under stress from minimal sample amounts, to unlock a new fundamental data class for AI. Its first commercial product, VIBE (Variations in Inter-facial Behaviour Under Excitation), predicts how drugs, foods, and materials will behave in the real world, serving pharmaceutical, biotech, food-and-beverage, and materials-science R&D. Based in San Francisco and London, Apoha emerged from stealth in 2026 with $36M in funding led by Singular, alongside Draper Associates, Redalpine, Seedcamp, Wilbe, and Nucleus.

providers.name: Chef Robotics
providers.description: Chef Robotics is a San Francisco, California physical-AI company building AI-enabled robots for high-mix food production. Its core product is an NSF-certified food-assembly robot that picks, scoops, and deposits a wide range of ingredients — fresh, cooked, IQF, sauces, leafy greens, mixed vegetables, and discrete piece items — into trays, burritos, wraps, pizza bases, and other containers on conveyor lines. The robots are powered by ChefOS, a proprietary Generalized Food Manipulation Model trained on tens of millions of real-world servings and tens of thousands of hours of production data, combining vision, decision-making, and robot control across a See / Think / Act stack with continuous Fleet Learning. Chef Robotics sells via a Robotics-as-a-Service (RaaS) model that bundles hardware, software updates, 24/7 monitoring, and customer success. Deployed customers include Amy's Kitchen, Sunbasket, Cafe Spice, and Chef Bombay, with the fleet having produced 98+ million servings across the US, Canada, and Europe. The company is venture-backed (Kleiner Perkins, Avataar Ventures-led $43M Series A, Bloomberg Beta, Construct Capital) and serves frozen meals, fresh meals, co-manufacturing, D2C meal delivery, medically tailored meals, meatpacking, airline catering, and foodservice verticals. There is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release for ChefOS — the platform is operated as a closed, fleet-managed service on Chef-owned hardware deployed inside customer facilities.

providers.name: Fishbit
providers.description: Fishbit is a smart-aquarium management company whose platform pairs a mobile app (iOS/Android) with connected hardware — the Fishbit Monitor, which tracks water parameters such as pH, temperature, and salinity in real time, and the Fishbit Controller, which wirelessly automates aquarium equipment. Hobbyists and reef keepers use the system to remotely monitor tank conditions and automate lighting, pumps, and dosing. The company sells its monitoring and control hardware through an online store and ran a device-manufacturer partner program (e.g. RapidLED Corona integration). No public API, developer portal, or SDK is currently published; this API Evangelist profile tracks the company as a connected-hardware / IoT lead.

providers.name: GATE Space
providers.description: GATE Space is an Austrian aerospace company redefining in-space mobility with high-thrust chemical propulsion systems for satellites, capsules, and landing vehicles. A TU Wien spinout founded in 2022 and backed by Techstars, the company builds the GATE Jetpack — a plug-and-play, refuelable propulsion module running on green propellants that lets satellites perform rapid orbit and attitude maneuvers with no integration effort. Its patented engines have been validated across 8,000+ hot-fire tests in atmospheric and vacuum conditions, manufactured in a European facility with a 98% local supply chain. GATE Space raised €6.3M via the EIC Accelerator and its propulsion system will fly on BeaconSat, Austria's first military satellite. This is a hardware manufacturer with no public developer/API surface; the profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company identity record.

providers.name: iRobot
providers.description: iRobot Corporation is a Bedford, Massachusetts consumer robotics company best known for the Roomba robot vacuum and the Braava and Braava jet robot mop product lines. Founded in 1990 by MIT roboticists, iRobot pioneered the home cleaning robot category and has sold tens of millions of units worldwide. Its current portfolio includes the Roomba Max, Roomba Plus, and Roomba 100/200 series vacuums and combo (vacuum + mop) models, along with AutoWash and AutoEmpty docks, the iRobot Home App for scheduling and mapping, and a cleaning accessories and trade-in program. The proposed acquisition by Amazon was abandoned in January 2024 after regulatory pushback from the European Commission, after which iRobot underwent a major restructuring and layoffs. iRobot's revenue model is direct robot and accessory sales plus recurring consumables; it does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI specification, and its homesupport documentation explicitly notes that Wi-Fi connected Roombas do not have an open API. A community of unofficial reverse-engineered libraries (dorita980, rest980, pyirobot) exists but is not endorsed by iRobot.

providers.name: NcodiN
providers.description: NcodiN is a French deep-tech company developing optical interconnect technology for high-performance computing and AI infrastructure. Founded in Palaiseau, France, the company builds miniaturized lasers integrated directly on silicon to replace traditional copper connections between chiplets and processors, aiming to break the "copper wall" that limits AI scaling. Its photonic interconnects promise petabit-per-second bandwidth with roughly a thousand times less energy to move data than copper links, targeting AI, telecommunications, autonomous driving, smart cities, healthcare, and climate modeling. NcodiN is backed by venture firms including Earlybird, Elaia, OVNI Capital, and Verve Ventures, is advised by major chip and equipment makers such as NVIDIA, Qualcomm, Intel, and ASML, and joined the FrenchTech2030 cohort in November 2025. As a semiconductor and photonics hardware company it sells to chipmakers and does not currently expose a public developer API, SDK, or developer documentation surface.

providers.name: Physical Property Testing
providers.description: Physical Properties Testers (PPT) Group is a Halifax, UK based multinational manufacturer of physical property test and measurement instrumentation, built through acquisition around four brands: James Heal (textile testing including bursting strength, abrasion and tear), Mecmesin (universal testing machines, torque testers and digital force gauges), Alluris (handheld force gauges and force/torque instrumentation) and Lansmont (shock, vibration and drop testing systems). The group designs, produces and services testing equipment that verifies the physical integrity and quality of raw materials, components and finished products across textiles, packaging, manufacturing and consumer goods. It is a hardware and laboratory-instrumentation business with no public developer API, SDK, or webhook surface. Registered in England and Wales (company no. 09210539); a portfolio company of SK Capital Partners since March 2025 (previously backed by Battery Ventures). This profile was surfaced as a VC portfolio lead and enriched with company identity from public sources.

providers.name: Reframe
providers.description: Reframe (usereframe.ai) is a San Francisco-based Y Combinator Winter 2026 company, founded in 2025 by Bryan Zin (previously a Product Design Engineer on the iPhone team at Apple) and Eric Wiener, building an AI-native hardware procurement platform. Reframe automates the manual procurement process in hardware supply chains: instead of emails and spreadsheets, AI agents handle purchase orders, supplier follow-ups, and part tracking for both COTS and custom-manufactured components, with Slack and Gmail integrations for team workflows. This API Evangelist profile tracks Reframe as a company in the network; the company does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Sandbar
providers.description: Sandbar is a consumer hardware and AI company behind Stream, a private voice ring and conversational notes app. Worn on the finger, Stream pairs a discreet private microphone, a glass touchpad, and silent haptics with an on-device "Inner Voice" assistant so people can capture notes, reminders, and todos, dictate speech-to-text across any iOS or Mac app, and think aloud without reaching for a phone. Backed by Kindred Ventures and True Ventures, Sandbar is a preorder-stage consumer product; it publishes a marketing site, an About/Us page, and a Careers page, but no public developer portal, API, or SDK surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Sunrise
providers.description: Sunrise Robotics builds intelligent, two-armed autonomous robotic cells for manufacturing. The AI-driven system combines built-in perception and environmental awareness with autonomous execution to transform existing production processes, increase capacity, and free human workers for higher-value tasks. Cells deploy quickly (needing only a three-phase outlet), are flexible across manufacturing applications, and are built to ISO 10218 / TS 15066 safety standards. The company is backed by Seedcamp and Slow Ventures.

providers.name: SupplyHog
providers.description: SupplyHog is an ecommerce platform built specifically for hardware and building-materials retailers, giving independent hardware and building-supply stores a branded online storefront to sell their products. The platform provides co-op and custom product catalogs, flexible fulfillment (in-store pickup, ship-to-store, local delivery, and ship-to-home with Shippo shipping labels), Stripe-powered payments, TaxJar tax calculation, real-time ERP inventory and pricing synchronization, custom branding and domains, location-aware search, and admin tools for order fulfillment and abandoned-cart recovery. Founded in 2010 as the Nopone.com reverse-auction marketplace, SupplyHog went through the DreamIt and 500 Startups accelerators, pivoted to full ecommerce services, and was acquired by construction-supply retailer R.P. Lumber in 2016. It does not publish a public developer API surface; it acts as a consumer of Stripe, TaxJar, and Shippo.

providers.name: teaBOT
providers.description: teaBOT is a Toronto-based hardware startup (Y Combinator, Summer 2015) that builds an automated loose-leaf tea-making robot offered to offices, showrooms, and lounges as an amenity-as-a-service. For a flat monthly fee, teams use the companion teaBOT app to explore premium teas and dispense a custom-blended cup in under 30 seconds, which companies such as Google, HubSpot, and McKinsey use as a workplace recruiting and retention perk. Founded by robotics PhD Rehman Merali, teaBOT runs a physical-product and mobile-app business and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: Oculus VR
providers.description: Oculus VR is the pioneering virtual reality company founded in 2012 and acquired by Facebook (now Meta) in 2014. Its Rift, Go, and Quest headsets defined consumer VR, and the Oculus brand has since been folded into Meta Quest and Meta Horizon OS. The former developer.oculus.com and oculus.com properties now redirect to Meta's developer platform. There is no distinct public REST/OpenAPI surface; developers build against SDK-based tooling (Unity, Unreal Engine, native OpenXR, and the Meta Spatial SDK) rather than a hosted web API. Backed originally by a16z; consumer VR/AR hardware and platform.

providers.name: Aerialoop
providers.description: Aerialoop is a drone technology and urban logistics company that designs, builds, and operates intelligent aerial networks for cargo delivery, surveillance, and infrastructure inspection. Founded in 2020 and headquartered in Miami with operations rooted in Quito, Ecuador, it is one of the fastest-growing drone delivery operations in Latin America. Its ALT 6-8 delivery drone carries a 5kg payload for urban logistics, while the ALT 6-ISR line adds HD, infrared, and night-vision cameras with AI-powered intrusion detection; extended-range variants operate up to 120km using LEO satellite connectivity for beyond-visual-line-of-sight flights. The company has completed over 50,000 flights across six countries. Aerialoop is a Techstars Miami (powered by J.P. Morgan) portfolio company. It currently publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Peer Robotics
providers.description: Peer Robotics builds collaborative autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) for manufacturing and warehouse material movement, designed to learn directly from humans to lower the cost and complexity of traditional automation. Its lineup includes the Peer 3000 collaborative mobile robot and the RM250 and RM500 AMRs (250kg and 500kg payloads) that handle pallets, trolleys, bin delivery, and machine tending through an intuitive human-robot dashboard interface. Backed by Techstars, the company operates a hardware and robotics product line rather than a public developer API surface; no public API, SDK, developer documentation, or GitHub repositories were found during enrichment probing.

providers.name: Standardkernel
providers.description: Standard Kernel Co. is an AI infrastructure company that automatically generates high-performance compute kernels for GPUs and TPUs. It targets the traditionally manual, expertise-intensive process of writing optimized low-level accelerator code, operating at the CUDA and PTX level to fully exploit new hardware features rather than relying on higher-level abstractions, delivering better performance on compute-bound machine-learning workloads and newer accelerator architectures. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Felicis and added to the API Evangelist network; the company is early-stage and publishes no public API, developer portal, or specification at this time.

providers.name: Kintra Fibers
providers.description: Kintra Fibers is a Brooklyn, New York materials-science company that has developed a proprietary bio-based and biodegradable synthetic yarn as an alternative to conventional petroleum polyester. Its polymer is a novel form of polybutylene succinate (PBS) made from renewable corn- and wheat-derived sugar feedstocks, melt-spun on the same commercial equipment already used for polyester so that mills, spinners and extruders can adopt it without re-tooling. The company sells four physical products into the apparel supply chain — resin for extruders, staple fiber for spinners, 75D/72F multifilament yarn in FDY, ATY and DTY forms for mills, and finished performance fabric for brands. Co-founded by Billy McCall and Alissa Baier-Lentz, Kintra runs an in-house resin and fiber science lab in Brooklyn, launched a Fashion for Good consortium with Inditex, Bestseller and Reformation, and closed a funding round led by H&M Group. Kintra is a manufacturer of physical materials, not a software company: it operates no developer program, publishes no public API, SDK, webhook or machine-readable API contract, and its only web property is a Webflow marketing and contact site.

providers.name: Monumental
providers.description: Monumental builds autonomous construction robots and the software that runs them. Its robots lay bricks and blockwork on real building sites, coordinated by Monumental's software platform (Atrium) and fleet operations (Fleet). The venture-backed company operates across the Netherlands, the United Kingdom, and the United States, and has raised multiple funding rounds (including a reported $32M raise and Series B rounds in the US and UK). Monumental was surfaced as a portfolio company of Northzone and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this profile the company publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation - this record captures its identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Ossia
providers.description: Ossia, Inc. is a Redmond, Washington wireless power technology company founded by physicist Hatem Zeine (incorporated as Omnilectric in 2008, operating as Ossia from 2013) and the inventor of Cota Real Wireless Power — a patented RF smart-antenna system that delivers targeted energy over the air to multiple moving devices at a distance, without pads, plugs, cables or line of sight. A Cota receiver emits a beacon and the Cota transmitter returns a focused 2.4 GHz or 5.8 GHz power signal along the same path, which is how the system tracks and powers devices in motion. Ossia does not manufacture products for sale: it licenses the Cota technology to manufacturers, brands and OEMs, ships Cota developer and reference design kits (receiver chip, sample hardware, software components, test instructions) to authorized licensees, and works through joint ventures and development partners such as Motherson Ossia. The company holds 180+ US and international patents, is FCC certified under Parts 15 and 18, and carries regulatory approval in the US, UK and 45+ other countries. Ossia publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable contract of any kind — the developer surface it does have is hardware and firmware delivered under license.

providers.name: Skeleton Technologies
providers.description: Skeleton Technologies is an Estonian-German energy storage manufacturer, founded in Tartu, Estonia in 2009 by Oliver Ahlberg and Taavi Madiberk, that designs and builds high-power supercapacitor and SuperBattery systems on its patented Curved Graphene material. Its product line spans SkelCap ultracapacitor cells, supercapacitor modules, and the GrapheneUPS, GrapheneGPU and GrapheneBBU power systems aimed at AI data centers, grid stability, defense, automotive, heavy transportation and industrial customers. The company has raised close to EUR 400 million, counts Marubeni and Siemens among its backers, and manufactures at its ISO 9001 / ISO 14001 certified Leipzig Superfactory in Germany, a Varkaus facility in Finland and a Curved Graphene plant in Bitterfeld-Wolfen. Skeleton sells physical power hardware; it operates no public developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Tractive
providers.description: Tractive is an Austrian pet-technology company, founded in October 2012 in Pasching, Austria and led by CEO Michael Hurnaus, that builds GPS location and health-monitoring trackers for dogs and cats. Its collar-attached devices (such as the DOG and CAT GPS trackers) pair with a subscription mobile app to deliver real-time worldwide location, virtual fences, activity, sleep and, more recently, resting heart-rate and respiratory-rate health intelligence to more than 1.4 million active subscribers. Tractive was acquired by Italy's Bending Spoons in 2026. Tractive does NOT publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal — its backend HTTP API (api.tractive.com) is private to its own apps; the only clients are unofficial, community reverse-engineered libraries. This profile enriches the company's identity for the API Evangelist network; there is no official API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Qunnect
providers.description: Qunnect Inc. is a quantum networking hardware company headquartered at the Brooklyn Navy Yard in New York, founded in 2017 by Mehdi Namazi and Mael Flament and led by CEO Noel Goddard. Qunnect builds room-temperature, rack-mountable devices that turn existing telecommunications fiber into scalable quantum networks without cryogenics or vacuum systems: the Qu-Source polarization-entangled photon-pair generator, the Qu-Mem atom-based quantum memory, and the turnkey Carina product suite, which combines entangled photon generation, single-photon counting detection and adaptive polarization compensation in a single rack unit for fiber spans up to 100 km. Carina deployments include New York City, Berlin, Montana State University and the ABQ-Net network in New Mexico. Qunnect is backed by Airbus Ventures, Cisco Investments and Quantonation. The company sells physical quantum networking hardware to research, defense and telecommunications customers and publishes no public API, SDK, or developer program.

providers.name: Acacia
providers.description: Acacia (Acacia Communications) is a coherent optical networking company, an early Matrix Partners portfolio company that was acquired by Cisco. Acacia designs and manufactures high-speed coherent optical interconnect solutions built on silicon photonics, low-power DSP, and 3D siliconization, including performance-optimized modules (AC1200, CIM 8), MSA pluggable modules (CFP, CFP2, OSFP, QSFP-DD, QSFP28), and client optics components (PAM4 DSP, optical engines). These power AI scale-out and scale-across fabrics, data center interconnect, metro and long-haul networks, submarine cables, access and cable networks, and space communications. Acacia is a hardware/components provider and does not publish a public developer API or programmatic platform.

providers.name: Astro Mechanica
providers.description: Astro Mechanica is a San Francisco aerospace company, founded in 2021 by Ian Brooke, reinventing supersonic flight for a new jet age. Its flagship Duality electric combined-cycle engine is engineered to stay efficient from takeoff through Mach 3+ by reconfiguring between turbofan, turbojet, and ramjet modes using a hybrid turboelectric architecture. The company designs engines, airframes, and flight systems in-house, has been selected to develop an engine for the U.S. Air Force Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) program, and is backed by a16z, Lowercarbon Capital, and Y Combinator. It was added to the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio company. As an aerospace hardware manufacturer, Astro Mechanica publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures the company's public web and identity surface only.

providers.name: ATMI Sales
providers.description: ATMI Sales (Advanced Technical Marketing Inc.) is a manufacturers' representative and technical sales firm serving the electronics and semiconductor industry across the Pacific Northwest and Western Canada. The company connects customers with component suppliers through a research, development, and build model — identifying suitable technology solutions, building supplier relationships, and ensuring component availability and supply-chain sourcing in the regions where products are manufactured. ATMI maintains a line card of partner technologies and works with distributors to fulfill orders. This is a non-developer B2B sales and distribution company; it publishes no public API, SDK, or developer program. Surfaced as a portfolio company of sierra-ventures and profiled in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Atom Semiconductor
providers.description: Atom Semiconductor (Atom Semiconductor Technologies Limited) is a fabless mixed-signal chip design company founded in Hong Kong in October 2020, with offices in Shenzhen and Shanghai. It designs high-performance analog and mixed-signal semiconductors for consumer and industrial IoT systems across three product lines: digital sensor chips (temperature/humidity, pressure, optical), analog-to-digital converters (24-bit Sigma-Delta, high-precision SAR, and high-speed GSPS ADCs), and microprocessors. Its first product, the AS1412 24-bit Sigma-Delta ADC, shipped for customer trials in late 2021. The company raised roughly 100M yuan in a pre-A round led by Qiming Venture Partners (with Venus Medtech and Alibaba Entrepreneurs Fund) and was named to the Forbes Asia 100 To Watch 2022. It is a hardware chip designer and does not publish a developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Axera Tech
providers.description: Axera Intelligence (爱芯元智), operating as Axera Tech, is a Chinese fabless semiconductor company building AI-inference SoCs for edge and endpoint computing. Its chips pair the Axera Tongyuan mixed-precision NPU with the Axera Zhimu AI-ISP to power on-device vision perception, smart-vehicle autonomous-driving and intelligent-cabin platforms, and multi-tier edge-AI inference across IoT and industrial scenarios. Axera Tech was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners; it is a hardware/silicon provider and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Calxeda
providers.description: Calxeda was an Austin, Texas semiconductor startup — founded in 2008 as Smooth-Stone by Barry Evans, Larry Wikelius and David Borland — that built ARM-based EnergyCore system-on-chip server processors (ECX-1000, ECX-2000/Midway) aimed at low-power, high-density data center workloads. It raised roughly $90-103M from venture investors including Battery Ventures, and its silicon shipped in Boston Limited Viridis appliances and HP Project Moonshot systems. Calxeda ceased operations in December 2013 after a refinancing round fell through, and its ARM server IP resurfaced under Silver Lining Systems in December 2014. The company published no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API artifacts, and calxeda.com is now a parked domain listed for sale, so there is no live API surface for the API Evangelist network to catalog.

providers.name: Carpenter Technology
providers.description: Carpenter Technology Corporation is a U.S.-based producer and distributor of premium specialty alloys — including titanium alloys, powder metals, high-temperature stainless steels, tool steels, and soft magnetic alloys — serving the aerospace, defense, medical, transportation, energy, and industrial end markets. The company supports customers through technical product resources such as its Alloy Finder, alloy technical data sheets, conversion tables, and a member-only Customer Portal for order and account self-service, but does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Daqstra
providers.description: Daqstra is an AI-native operating platform for complex test infrastructure, giving aerospace, energy, and robotics teams observability and orchestration for the physical world. The platform connects data-acquisition hardware (National Instruments, PLCs, and custom equipment) at the edge, centralizes and versions test data in the cloud, and orchestrates hardware sequences and test logic as code through Python and REST APIs. Daqstra Edge streams live signals from physical hardware, Daqstra Hub (Strata Hub) organizes test-campaign data with AI-powered insight, and the Daqstra API lets engineers drive test runs programmatically instead of through manual CSV workflows. The company was founded by aerospace-propulsion and avionics engineers and is backed by Y Combinator (S26 batch).

providers.name: Fabheads
providers.description: Fabheads is a carbon fiber and composite manufacturing company (Fabheads Automation) that delivers end-to-end composite product development — design, analysis, tooling, prototyping, and production — using its own fiber-printing and automated-layup technology alongside traditional craftsmanship. It serves aerospace, mobility, marine, robotics, medical, and sports customers from aerospace-grade facilities, and publishes the C6 Slicer tool for composite fiber printing. Backed by Accel. As a hardware manufacturer it exposes no public developer API; this profile captures identity and domain-security posture rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Holo
providers.description: Holo (Holo AM, operating under Greene Group Industries) is an advanced metal additive manufacturing company founded in 2017 and backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners. Its PureForm metal 3D printing platform uses digital light processing (DLP) with metal powder-filled photopolymer resins to produce high-resolution, complex metal components with features as small as 50 microns, in pure copper, stainless steels (17-4PH, 316), and in-development cobalt alloy, titanium, nickel superalloys, tool steels, and alumina. Customers submit CAD files and receive prototyped-to-production parts with roughly two-week turnaround, serving medical technology, precision micro-robotics, and general advanced manufacturing. Holo is a hardware manufacturer and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: LiquidLight
providers.description: LiquidLight, Inc. (Liquid Light) was an electrochemistry company based in Monmouth Junction, New Jersey that developed and licensed process technology for converting carbon dioxide into industrial chemicals. Founded in 2009 by Kyle Teamey, Emily Cole, Andrew Bocarsly, Fouad Elnaggar and Nety Krishna around technology licensed from Princeton University, the company built a portfolio of more than 100 patents covering the electrochemical production of chemicals including monoethylene glycol (MEG), propylene and acetic acid, with MEG as its lead target market. It raised seed funding from Redpoint Ventures and a $15 million Series B in September 2014 from investors including VantagePoint Capital Partners and BP Ventures, and was also a Battery Ventures portfolio investment. Avantium acquired Liquid Light on January 10, 2017 and the company ceased operating independently. LiquidLight was a materials and process-technology company: it never published a public API, developer portal, SDKs or any machine-readable developer surface, and no company web property survives the acquisition. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an accurate, non-API portfolio record.

providers.name: Orbital Arc
providers.description: Orbital Arc is a Houston-based deep-tech spacecraft propulsion startup founded in 2023 by Jonathan Huffman, building Gas-Phase Field Effect Electric Propulsion (Gas FEEP) thrusters and the RIOT Drive (Relativistic Ion Thrust Drive) for satellites and in-space transportation. Its ultra-lightweight electric thrusters use solid naphthalene fuel that sublimates at room temperature instead of noble gases, targeting high specific impulse for satellite constellations. Backed by Techstars and Capital Factory, the company completed a sub-scale physics demonstration at Oak Ridge National Laboratory (TRL 3). This is a hardware company with no public API, SDK, or developer surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Owl Labs
providers.description: Owl Labs is a Boston-based video conferencing hardware and software company building smart devices for hybrid meetings. Its flagship Meeting Owl line is a 360-degree AI-powered camera, microphone, and speaker that automatically focuses on whoever is speaking, alongside accessories such as the Owl Bar, Whiteboard Owl, and Expansion Mic. The Nest is its cloud fleet-management platform for provisioning, updating, and monitoring deployed devices across an organization. Owl Labs sells to enterprises, schools, and distributed teams, and publishes an annual State of Hybrid Work report. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Matrix Partners and Playground Global. Owl Labs does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or webhook surface; this profile captures its identity, security posture, and public web properties.

providers.name: Quantumdiamonds
providers.description: QuantumDiamonds (QD) is a Munich-based German deep-tech company that develops diamond-based quantum sensing systems for semiconductor inspection and failure analysis. The company markets what it describes as the world's first commercially available quantum sensing system for semiconductor inspection, using nitrogen-vacancy (NV) diamond quantum microscopy to detect defects and current-flow anomalies that traditional inspection methods miss. QuantumDiamonds is a portfolio company of the venture firm Earlybird and was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile. As a quantum hardware and instrumentation company, it does not currently expose a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its public web presence and company identity.

providers.name: Quintessent
providers.description: Quintessent is a Goleta, California deep-tech photonics company developing quantum dot laser and optical interconnect technology to scale computing and AI infrastructure. The company builds quantum dot epitaxial wafer supply chains (in partnership with IQE) and optical connectivity solutions for AI optical interconnects, targeting the bandwidth and energy-efficiency bottlenecks of next-generation data centers. Backed by Sierra Ventures, Quintessent is a hardware and semiconductor company; as of this profile it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API documentation.

providers.name: Sagence AI
providers.description: Sagence AI is a semiconductor company building analog in-memory computing hardware for AI inference. Its "analog inference machine" combines deep subthreshold computing with multi-level flash memory cells to run large AI models at a fraction of the power and cost of conventional digital GPUs, targeting datacenter and edge workloads such as generative AI, recommendation systems, real-time defect detection, and video security. Backed by Khosla Ventures, the company positions its technology against offerings like Nvidia's B200, claiming large gains in performance-per-watt and cost efficiency for AI inference. Sagence AI is a hardware/silicon company and does not currently publish a developer API, SDK, or public developer portal.

providers.name: Substrate
providers.description: Substrate is a semiconductor manufacturing company building America's next-generation chip foundry, with the stated mission of returning the United States to dominance in advanced semiconductor fabrication. Rather than designing chips, the company is inventing manufacturing technology intended to extend Moore's Law while lowering the cost of building state-of-the-art fabs and the wafers they produce. Substrate is a hard-tech / advanced-manufacturing venture backed by General Catalyst; it is a physical-infrastructure company and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced from the General Catalyst portfolio and enriched with the provider's public identity and security surface.

providers.name: The Exploration Company
providers.description: The Exploration Company GmbH is a European space transportation startup building reusable space vehicles "for humanity." Its flagship program, Nyx, is a reusable capsule designed to carry cargo and, eventually, crew between Earth and low Earth orbit destinations such as commercial space stations, featuring orbital propulsion, autonomous docking, and re-entry recovery. The company is also developing Storm, a high-thrust reusable rocket engine (up to 180 tons of thrust) built through European partnerships toward a globally competitive launcher. Backed by Balderton Capital and a certified B Corp, it markets itself as one of the fastest-growing space startups in the world. The company operates a marketing and careers web presence but publishes no public developer program, API, SDKs, or machine-readable API artifacts at this time. Surfaced as a Balderton Capital portfolio company and enriched in the API Evangelist network with verified identity and domain-security signals.

providers.name: Tile
providers.description: Tile is a consumer-electronics company known for its Bluetooth tracker devices, used to locate everyday items such as keys, wallets, bags, and phones through a companion mobile app and a crowd-sourced Find network. Tile was acquired by Life360 in 2021; its former site thetileapp.com now 301-redirects to life360.com. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners, Tile publishes no public developer API — this profile captures its security posture (security.txt, a HackerOne responsible-disclosure program, and probed domain security).

providers.name: VXB Aerospace
providers.description: VXB Aerospace is an Australian space technology company founded in 2022 by Alexander Ryan, developing generative design software and Hall-effect plasma propulsion for the satellite market. Its platform automates the design, manufacturability analysis, multi-physics modeling and validation of complex aerospace hardware such as propulsion systems, antennas and satellite layouts, while its ZEPHYR-35 Hall-effect thruster (Argon/Krypton/Xenon) provides in-orbit mobility, refueling, servicing and de-orbiting. The company was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio lead and enriched in the API Evangelist network; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Arago
providers.description: Arago (Arago Computing SAS) is a Paris-based deeptech semiconductor startup, founded in 2024 by Nicolas Muller, Ambroise Muller, and Eliott Sarrey, building energy-efficient AI accelerators powered by light rather than electricity. Its photonic processor, codenamed JEF, uses a proprietary multi-physics computing core that encodes values with lasers instead of thousands of transistor switches, targeting 10x to 30x reductions in energy and cost overhead for AI workloads at equivalent performance to leading GPUs. Arago pairs the hardware with a full software stack called CARLOTA, which abstracts the complexities of photonic computing and exposes a programmable interface compatible with mainstream AI frameworks such as PyTorch and TensorFlow, while remaining fabbable using standard semiconductor processes. The company operates across France, North America, and Israel, and in July 2025 raised an oversubscribed $26 million seed round co-led by Earlybird, Protagonist, and Visionaries Tomorrow, with backing from executives and investors tied to Apple, Arm, Nvidia, Microsoft, Amazon, Uber, PayPal, and Hugging Face. Arago was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Earlybird; as an early-stage hardware company it does not yet publish a public developer API or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: Artiphon
providers.description: Artiphon is a Nashville-based music technology company that designs smart, portable musical instruments for everyday creativity. Its products, including the Instrument 1, Orba, Orba 2, Orba 3, and Chorda, combine strumming, tapping, sliding, and looping into palm-sized MIDI controllers and synthesizers, paired with companion apps that let anyone make beats, loop sounds, and explore music anywhere. Artiphon sells direct and through retailers such as Guitar Center and Sweetwater. It does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a consumer-hardware company reference.

providers.name: Avnet
providers.description: Avnet is a global technology distributor and solutions provider that delivers electronic components, embedded solutions, and design and supply chain services to industrial and commercial customers.

providers.name: Majestic Labs
providers.description: Majestic Labs is a semiconductor and AI-infrastructure company building power-efficient AI servers that put memory first. Its rearchitected server uses custom chips that disaggregate memory from compute, giving processors direct access to a massive uniform, high-bandwidth memory pool (reportedly up to 128 TB per server and roughly 1000x more memory available to compute than a conventional design). The company claims a single Majestic rack can hold the memory capacity of about 25 Nvidia NVL72-class racks while consuming a fraction of the power, targeting frontier language models, agentic and reasoning AI, graph neural networks, and video generation. Founded by Ofer Shacham, Sha Rabii, and Masumi Reynders, Majestic Labs is backed by Lux Capital (2024). This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a company lead; the company does not currently publish a public developer/API surface.

providers.name: Manufactured
providers.description: Manufactured is a supply-chain and production platform for hardware and consumer-product brands, backed by Bullpen Capital. Its web application (app.manufactured.com) helps teams run overseas production end to end — issuing sourcing requests to vendors, managing supplier and vendor profiles, negotiating order estimates and contracts under master procurement agreements, tracking production timelines and calendars, and financing purchase orders through production and repayment terms. The product also embeds an AI assistant built on LangChain. At the time of enrichment the public marketing site and the api/docs/developer subdomains were unreachable, and the GraphQL, Lambda and bot backends are private and authentication-gated (introspection blocked), so no public API specification, developer portal, or documentation could be harvested. This profile captures the real, observable surface only.

providers.name: Mirana Toys
providers.description: Mirana Toys (Mirana Innovations Pvt Ltd) is an India-based smart-toy company and OEM/ODM manufacturer of electronic toys — RC cars, monster trucks, drones, educational toys, and AI/AR toys. It pairs its consumer products with the Mirana smart app (iOS and Android), a mobile gaming platform that lets kids and adults control and play with Mirana toys over Bluetooth. As an OEM partner it offers in-house PCB/PCBA design and SMT assembly, tooling and mold design, mobile app development, compliance support (ASTM, EN-71, RoHS, ISO, SMETA), and global logistics for toy brands and retailers. Backed by Accel. The company publishes a consumer e-commerce storefront and support center but no public API or developer platform.

providers.name: Simantic
