providers.description: Simantic builds simulated hardware for embedded QA, modernizing embedded firmware development through hardware simulation designed for AI adoption in hardware engineering. Its platform emulates microcontroller (MCU) systems so engineers can inject sensor readings and observe how their firmware reacts over CAN, Ethernet, and BLE, running full firmware test suites in CI (for example GitHub Actions) on every push and pull request without physical boards. A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server lets AI agents step through firmware, inspect peripheral state, and replay scenarios against a simulated MCU, and a CLI drives simulations locally. Simantic offers private, self-hosted deployment so firmware and test data never leave a team's own servers. Founded in 2025, Simantic is a Y Combinator (Fall 2026) company.

providers.name: BYD
providers.description: BYD Company Ltd. is a Chinese multinational manufacturing conglomerate headquartered in Shenzhen, founded in 1995 by Wang Chuanfu and publicly listed in Hong Kong (1211) and Shenzhen (002594). Originally a rechargeable-battery maker, BYD has grown into one of the world's largest producers of new-energy vehicles (battery-electric and plug-in hybrid cars, buses, and trucks), power batteries (including the Blade Battery), consumer and automotive electronics, rail transit systems (SkyRail/SkyShuttle), forklifts, and solar and energy-storage products. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of hongshan and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; BYD is a hardware and manufacturing company and does not publish a public developer or API program.

providers.name: ConvenientPower
providers.description: ConvenientPower (Chengdu ConvenientPower Semiconductor, 成都市易冲半导体有限公司) is an analog and mixed-signal integrated-circuit design company founded in 2016 and headquartered in Chengdu, Sichuan, China, with offices in Beijing, Shanghai, Xi'an, Shenzhen, Hong Kong, Taiwan, and Silicon Valley. The company designs high-performance power-management ICs spanning the full link from 220V mains to battery: wireless-charging transmitters and receivers (Qi, up to 100W), USB Power Delivery and UFCS protocol controllers, AC/DC flyback and synchronous rectifier controllers, GaN-integrated solutions, battery-charging management, LDOs and DC/DC converters, and automotive-grade power ICs (wireless charging, LED lighting, eFuse protection, switches). Its parts ship into consumer electronics, accessories, and automotive markets, with more than 330 million units shipped and 160+ patents; automotive ICs are AEC-Q100 qualified. As a hardware semiconductor vendor, ConvenientPower exposes developer resources as chip SDK toolkits, reference designs, and design software rather than a public web API. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners.

providers.name: Gbatteries
providers.description: GBatteries (GBatteries Energy Canada Inc.) is an Ottawa, Ontario battery technology company developing lithium-metal battery cells and an intelligent, adaptive battery management system for the next generation of electric mobility, from land to air. Its technology targets fast charging (sub-15-minute charge), high energy density (450+ Wh/kg), extended cycle life, and enhanced safety by actively reducing irreversible internal cell damage. The company reports 60+ granted or pending patents and 9+ years of R&D, and was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company. GBatteries is a hardware and battery-management deeptech firm; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: LINSOL Co.,Ltd.
providers.description: LINSOL Co.,Ltd. (린솔) is a safety-technology company headquartered in Daejeon, South Korea, founded as an in-house venture spun out of Hanwha Aerospace. LINSOL adapts acoustic detection techniques originally developed for defense landmine applications into commercial real-time hazard, accident, and environmental detection. Its product line includes Karang F (driving-environment detection), Karang S (precision acoustic signal transmission), SkyShield (fall detection), BR, Acoustic Eye (aerial security), and Safety Nova (smart integrated safety platform), sold into industrial safety, ESG, and defense security use cases. The company operates a Daejeon headquarters and research center plus a Goheung branch. LINSOL ships hardware and integrated platforms; as of a 2026-07-19 probe it publishes no public developer API, portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Marvell Technology
providers.description: Marvell Technology, Inc. is a Fortune 500 fabless semiconductor company headquartered in Santa Clara, California. The company designs and develops data infrastructure semiconductor solutions including custom ASICs, data processing units, Ethernet controllers, optical and copper PHYs, switches, and storage controllers used in data centers, enterprise networking, carrier infrastructure, automotive, and consumer markets. This repository captures any APIs, developer tools, and machine-readable API artifacts associated with Marvell. Public developer documentation is gated behind a customer support portal and is not openly accessible.

providers.name: Pivotal Commware
providers.description: Pivotal Commware develops millimeter wave (mmWave) infrastructure for 5G networks, built around its Holographic Beam Forming technology and what it calls the world's first smart repeater ecosystem. Its product line includes WaveScape network-planning software, the Pivot 5G outdoor network repeater, the Echo 5G subscriber repeater for indoor mmWave coverage, and IBMS, an Intelligent Beam Management System that pairs machine learning with smart repeaters for real-time network optimization. The company is venture-backed by Lux Capital. As of this enrichment pass Pivotal Commware publishes a corporate and marketing site (datasheets, white papers, videos, and a blog) but no public developer portal, API, or SDK surface was found.

providers.name: Pliops
providers.description: Pliops is an Israeli data-acceleration semiconductor company, founded in 2017 and headquartered in Ramat Gan, that builds the Extreme Data Processor (XDP) — a low-profile PCIe accelerator card that offloads storage and key-value data-path work from server CPUs. Its software surface is delivered as host libraries rather than as a web API: XDP-AccelKV and XDP-Rocks expose a RocksDB-API-compatible key-value engine (the "storelib" shared library) used as a drop-in under MySQL/MyRocks, Redis, KVRocks, TiDB, Kafka and Spark, and XDP LightningAI extends the same acceleration to GenAI KV-cache offload for vLLM-based inference. Pliops raised roughly $205M from investors including Intel Capital, NVIDIA, AMD, SoftBank Ventures Asia and Western Digital, and was acquired by Astera Labs in February 2026, which took certain assets, IP and about half the staff into a new Israeli R&D center. Pliops has never operated a public developer program: there is no developer portal, no public API reference, no published OpenAPI or other machine-readable contract, and no published SDK in any package registry — product and library access runs through a sales/evaluation conversation.

providers.name: Rapid Silicon
providers.description: Rapid Silicon is a fabless semiconductor company founded in 2019 and headquartered in Los Gatos, California, building AI- and intelligent-edge-focused FPGAs and embedded FPGA (eFPGA) IP on an open-source technology base. Its product line covers the Gemini FPGA family, the Vega eFPGA IP core (a customizable, scalable embeddable FPGA fabric from roughly 1.5K to 100K+ logic cells with configurable BRAM and DSP MAC tiles), and the Rapid eFPGA Configurator for self-service eFPGA resource sizing. Design work is done in the Raptor Design Suite, the company's RTL-to-bitstream EDA tool-chain covering simulation, synthesis, placement, routing, bitstream generation and device configuration, released under GPL3 as what the company describes as the first complete commercially available open-source FPGA tool-chain. Rapid Silicon raised a $15M seed round in 2021 and a $30M Series A in January 2023 from Cambium Capital Partners and Chengwei Capital, and is led by chairman and CEO Naveed Sherwani. The company's products are silicon IP and locally installed design software rather than a hosted service, so it publishes no public web API, developer portal or machine-readable API contract; as of 2026-05-25 its rapidsilicon.com website no longer serves company content and redirects to a domain-brokerage page.

providers.name: Sygaldry
providers.description: Sygaldry Technologies builds quantum-accelerated AI servers — augmenting classical data-center infrastructure with quantum processors purpose-built for AI to deliver exponential speedups on specific training and inference tasks. Founded in 2024 in Ann Arbor, Michigan by Chad Rigetti (founder of Rigetti Computing), Idalia Friedson, and Michael Keiser, the company combines multiple qubit types within a single fault-tolerant architecture to accelerate model training, fine-tuning, and token generation while cutting compute cost and energy use. A Y Combinator Spring 2025 company, Sygaldry has raised $139M ($34M seed led by Initialized Capital and a $105M Series A led by Breakthrough Energy Ventures, with Bloomberg Beta among its investors). Sygaldry currently publishes no public developer API; this profile is maintained for API Evangelist network discovery.

providers.name: Anoria
providers.description: Anoria is a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) human-interaction company building a wearable bracelet for the EQ era that measures and tracks emotional states in real time. The device uses the company's proprietary SOMI (state-of-mind inference) model to correlate roughly 150 audio and biometric signals into a "Flow Score" that reflects a user's energy, mood, and focus, then explains why the user feels that way and what they can do about it. Anoria targets founders and creatives who treat their mental state as a performance asset, with the goal of making emotional intelligence trainable. As of mid-2026 the company is an early-stage prototype running an early-access waitlist; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation yet, so this API Evangelist profile captures verified company identity only.

providers.name: Atlas Motion Systems
providers.description: Atlas Motion Systems (atlasmotion.com) designs and builds brushless DC (BLDC) motors and actuators for defense and robotics applications, engineered around a customer's specific program and manufactured at scale. The public web presence is a single-page marketing site (hero plus a contact page); it is a hardware company that does not publish a developer portal, public API, SDKs, documentation, or well-known discovery surface. This profile was seeded as a Homebrew-portfolio lead and enriched with verifiable identity and live domain-security probe data only. Enrichment found no API surface to harvest.

providers.name: FIMI Technology
providers.description: FIMI Technology Ltd. (Beijing FIMI Technology Co., Ltd. / Shenzhen FIMI Robot Technology Co., Ltd.) is a consumer aerial-imaging hardware manufacturer founded in May 2014 as a member of the Xiaomi ecosystem. FIMI designs and sells affordable camera drones, handheld gimbal cameras, and smartphone gimbals, with a product lineup that includes the X8 series (X8 SE, X8 Pro, X8 Tele, X8T enterprise), the compact Mini 3, the Manta VTOL fixed-wing drone, and the PALM series gimbal cameras. The company holds hundreds of patents across flight control, wireless transmission links, mechatronic design, gimbal image-stabilization, and computer vision. FIMI is a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. This is a consumer-electronics company with no public developer program, API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Heaviside Industries
providers.description: Heaviside Industries is a defense-technology company founded in 2024 in Los Angeles, California, building autonomous precision munitions for U.S. and allied special operations and conventional forces. Its products — MOTH (land electromagnetic signal intelligence and spectrum awareness), TYR (autonomous aerial munition), and HYDRA (autonomous underwater munition) — are designed to deliver hyper-precise strike capabilities across air, land, and sea in GPS-denied and contested environments. Named after physicist Oliver Heaviside, whose electromagnetic theory enabled miniaturized electronics, the company emerged from stealth in May 2026 with a $28M Series A. It does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API artifacts.

providers.name: Mauna Kea Semiconductors
providers.description: Mauna Kea Semiconductors (mk-semi.com) is a Silicon Valley-based fabless semiconductor company founded by industry veterans to develop what it describes as the world's lowest-power Ultra-Wideband (UWB) solution for high precision location and direction-finding applications. Its UWB chips, modules, and integrated System-on-Chip solutions target smartphones, wearables, IoT devices, and automotive use cases, combining digital and analog/mixed-signal design expertise. Headquartered in Cupertino, California, with engineering operations in Shanghai, Beijing, and Shenzhen, the company is led by CEO Dr. Yifeng Zhang and is backed by Qiming. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Qiming; it is a hardware/silicon vendor with no public API or developer surface at this time (documentation, blog, and careers pages are marked "Coming Soon").

providers.name: Mira
providers.description: Mira is a San Francisco-based consumer hardware startup building AI-powered smart glasses positioned as an always-on "second brain." Founded in 2024 by Harvard builders AnhPhu Nguyen and Caine Ardayfio (rebranded from Halo), the camera-free glasses pair a dual-waveguide display, microphone, and iOS companion app to deliver live transcription, real-time translation across 60+ languages, hands-free AI assistance, and searchable memory of everyday conversations. Mira raised a $6.6M seed round led by General Catalyst and began shipping its first devices in January 2026. It is a privacy-first consumer wearable with an iOS companion app and does not currently expose a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: MOLG
providers.description: MOLG (molg.ai) is a circular manufacturing company tackling electronic waste. It operates autonomous robotic microfactories that disassemble complex devices like laptops and servers to recover components and materials for reuse, remanufacturing, and recycling. MOLG also partners with manufacturers on design-for-circularity (modular snap/press-fit/latch assembly instead of screws and adhesives) and offers OriginMark, a traceability platform for tracking devices, components, and materials across their lifecycle to calculate embodied carbon and supply-chain transparency. As of this enrichment pass MOLG publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or technical documentation; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Periodic
providers.description: Periodic (Periodic Labs) is an AI research company building "AI scientists" paired with autonomous laboratories to accelerate discovery in the physical sciences, with an early focus on materials science and higher-temperature superconductors. Their systems hypothesize, run physical experiments, and learn from the results, and they partner with industry to optimize experimental processes. Surfaced as a portfolio company of CRV and Felicis, the company is at an early stage and does not currently publish a public API, developer documentation, or developer platform. This profile records that honest result; it is not penalized for having no API surface.

providers.name: Pixcel
providers.description: PIXCEL Inc. is an early-stage deep-tech startup developing cutting-edge silicon photonics solutions and photonic integrated circuits (PICs) for optical communications and related systems. Based in Matawan, NJ, and co-founded by silicon photonics veteran Long Chen (previously at Cisco Systems and Acacia Communications), the company designs passive and active photonic components and collaborates with foundry partners to optimize process design kits (PDKs). PIXCEL is a hardware and semiconductor company with no public API, developer portal, or software product surface at this time; it was surfaced as a portfolio company of Matrix Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. This profile reflects an enrichment pass that confirmed there is no API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Preemadonna
providers.description: Preemadonna is a consumer hardware and software company best known for the Nailbot, a compact inkjet nail-art printer that prints custom designs onto fingernails, press-ons, gel, or bare nails in about five seconds. Backed by Version One Ventures, the company is building a creative-expression platform that pairs smart hardware with AI-powered design tools, consumables, and a creator marketplace, delivered through companion iOS and Android apps. The company holds 10+ utility patents. Preemadonna currently exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile captures its public web, support, and policy footprint for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Team Wildfire
providers.description: Team Wildfire develops jet engine-enabled fire suppression technology built to prevent catastrophic wildfire losses. Its mobile units, the "Hurricane" and "Storm Cell", apply fire retardant at scale to deny ground to advancing wildfires. The company offers fireground services, evacuation route hardening, asset protection, prescribed fire containment, and military base protection. Team Wildfire is a physical hardware and services company backed by Techstars; it publishes a marketing and services website but no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or developer documentation. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio lead and enriched with the identity and domain-security signals available for a non-API company.

providers.name: Ion Mobility
providers.description: ION Mobility is a Singapore-headquartered technology and automotive company that designs and builds affordable, zero-emission smart electric motorcycles for riders across Southeast Asia, with its flagship M1-S model and a companion rider mobile app. The company combines advanced hardware and software with human-centred design, spanning electric two-wheelers and energy charging and storage solutions, with additional offices in Jakarta and Shenzhen and backing from investors including 500 Global. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company's public developer and identity surface; ION Mobility currently publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or OpenAPI specification, operating a consumer waitlist/test-ride site and an internal open-source tooling estate on GitHub.

providers.name: MatX
providers.description: MatX is an AI-hardware company designing specialized semiconductors optimized for large language model workloads. Its flagship MatX One chip targets high-throughput, low-latency training, inference, and reinforcement learning for large dense and Mixture-of-Experts models, storing weights in SRAM to cut latency and reaching over 2,000 output tokens per second on large models. MatX is a hardware and research company with no public developer API surface; this profile captures its identity, research/blog output, open-source codebases, and domain-security posture. Backed by Jane Street, Spark Capital, and Situational Awareness LP.

providers.name: AMP Fund
providers.description: AMP (AMP PBC) is a public benefit corporation founded in 2025 by Anjney Midha, a former Andreessen Horowitz general partner, to build an independent "AI grid" — a pooled compute utility for frontier AI research teams. Rather than operating as a cloud provider or a conventional venture firm, AMP acts as an independent system operator: data center operators and labs contribute underutilized GPU capacity to a shared network, and member research teams draw base-load and burst compute from that pool at rates intended to sit below the volatile spot market. AMP pairs capital with compute, having raised roughly $1.3 billion for its first fund, and its PBC charter is structured so leadership can supply compute at cost without shareholder challenge. It has also committed a Public Wealth Fund of up to $500 million through 2030 toward education, workforce readiness, healthcare access, and economic resilience in communities affected by the AI transition. AMP publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Atom Computing
providers.description: Atom Computing is a Berkeley, California neutral-atom quantum computing company building large-scale, gate-based quantum computers using optically-trapped Ytterbium-171 nuclear-spin qubits. Founded in 2018 by Ben Bloom, the company became the first in the industry to exceed 1,000 qubits in a gate-based quantum computer with its second-generation platform in October 2023 (1,180 qubits across 1,225 sites). Its current commercial product, AC1000, is a universal gate-based, on-premises quantum computing system with 1,200+ physical qubits, all-to-all connectivity, mid-circuit measurement with qubit reuse and reset, real-time conditional branching, and better-than-threshold fidelities (>99.9% single-qubit, >99.6% two-qubit, >99.8% SPAM). The platform is programmable via OpenQASM and QIR (Quantum Intermediate Representation) and ships with a 20-qubit classical emulator. In January 2025 Atom Computing and Microsoft announced an on-premises 50-logical-qubit system (Magne), with additional strategic collaborations across Cisco (networked/distributed quantum, March 2026), NVIDIA NVQLink integration (March 2026), and a Letter of Intent for $100M from the U.S. Department of Commerce (May 2026). The commercial model centers on enterprise and national-lab on-premises system sales and partnerships; there is no public cloud API or self-serve developer portal — programmatic access is via the standard OpenQASM/QIR toolchains targeting customer-deployed AC1000 hardware.

providers.name: Ayar Labs
providers.description: Ayar Labs is a silicon-photonics company that develops co-packaged optics (CPO) and optical I/O technology to replace copper interconnects with light. Its products, including the TeraPHY optical engine and SuperNova external light source, connect thousands of GPUs across racks to deliver the bandwidth density and energy efficiency required by hyperscale AI infrastructure. Ayar Labs is backed by Insight Partners and Playground Global. It ships hardware and optical-interconnect technology rather than a public developer API; this API Evangelist profile tracks the company's public web properties and domain security posture.

providers.name: Baya Systems
providers.description: Baya Systems is a semiconductor IP company accelerating intelligent compute with chiplets. Backed by Matrix Partners and Intel Capital and based in Santa Clara, California (with offices in Austin, Texas and Bengaluru, India), Baya provides the WeaverPro software platform and the WeaveIP unified fabric and cache IP portfolio. Together they let system architects analyze, design and post-silicon tune optimal single-die or multi-die, chiplet-ready Network-on-Chip (NoC) interconnect systems, with multi-level coherency and multicast for AI acceleration scaling into petabytes per second across hyperscale, enterprise, AI, automotive, GPU and IoT markets. Baya Systems does not publish a public developer API, portal or SDK at this time; this API Evangelist network profile tracks the company as a portfolio lead awaiting a public API surface.

providers.name: Coolso
providers.description: Coolso develops wearable gesture-recognition technology. Using patented sensing that detects muscle-vibration signals processed through its own AI model, Coolso recognizes individual finger movements and strength levels with low-latency response, from a wrist-worn device or an ordinary smartwatch's accelerometer and gyroscope without dedicated hardware. Founded by Sheng-Kuei Hsu, Wei-Lin Lee, and Jack Wu and based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, the seed-stage company is backed by 500 Global and Alchemist Accelerator and targets AR/VR interaction, with potential expansion into medical rehabilitation and sports equipment. Coolso publishes no public API, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: DustPhotonics
providers.description: DustPhotonics is a fabless silicon photonics company founded in Israel in 2017 by Ben Rubovitch, Kobi Hasharoni and Amir Geron, building Photonic Integrated Circuit (SiPho PIC) engines and optical interconnect components for hyperscale and AI data centers. Its product line covers integrated laser engines (Oz4, Oz8, Carmel4, Carmel8) and external laser chips (Kfir, Kfir200, Tamar, Tamar200) spanning 400G to 1.6T, built around a proprietary L3C low-loss laser coupling technique that integrates lasers, modulators and photodetectors onto a single chip for optical transceivers, active optical cables and near-package optics. Credo Technology Group agreed to acquire DustPhotonics in April 2026 and completed the acquisition on 28 May 2026; the dustphotonics.com site now redirects into credosemi.com. The company sells silicon and optical hardware to system and transceiver makers and has never operated a public developer program, API, SDK or documentation portal.

providers.name: Eliyan
providers.description: Eliyan Corporation is a fabless semiconductor company in Santa Clara, California that develops chiplet and chip-to-chip interconnect physical-layer (PHY) IP for multi-die and AI infrastructure systems. Its NuLink die-to-die and die-to-memory PHY, NuLink-X chip-to-chip PHY, NuLink-XD 224G PAM4 SerDes for electro-optical modules, and NuGear chiplets let designers build multi-die architectures on standard organic substrates as well as advanced packaging, using simultaneous bidirectional signaling and support for UCIe, Bunch of Wires (BoW) and its own UMI interface. Eliyan licenses silicon IP and sells chiplets to semiconductor and hyperscale customers rather than operating a public web API; the company publishes no developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Lemnos Labs
providers.description: Lemnos Labs, Inc. is an early-stage deeptech venture capital firm that invests at the earliest phases of hardware company formation, helping founders better understand their customer, anticipate problems, and leverage their assets. Lemnos contributes engineering, manufacturing, marketing, and financial capital alongside the check, and deliberately keeps a minimal public presence — its site is a single page that lists only the active portfolio. That portfolio spans robotics and autonomy (Built Robotics, Fort Robotics, Path Robotics, Scythe Robotics, Simbe Robotics, Petra), agricultural technology (FarmWise, Ceres Imaging), autonomous cargo aviation (Elroy Air), space data and precise positioning (Spire, Swift Navigation), simulation (Duality), video analytics (Lumeo), and physical security (Rhombus). Lemnos itself publishes no API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification; it is catalogued in the API Evangelist network as a venture-capital entity whose value to the network is its portfolio graph — several of its companies are meaningful API providers in their own right.

providers.name: Projectx
providers.description: ProjectX is a San Francisco-based Y Combinator (Spring 2026) startup building Infinity (InfinityOS), a cloud operating system designed for AI agents. Infinity lets agents and humans orchestrate GPU workloads through a chat interface rather than traditional APIs, running multiple Windows and Linux applications — such as Blender, VS Code, DaVinci Resolve, Unreal Engine, and Isaac Sim — simultaneously, each on its own independent compute and GPU inside a single shared browser-based workspace with sub-minute cold starts. A public API, developer docs, status page, changelog, and blog are announced as coming soon; no programmatic API surface is published yet.

providers.name: PsiQuantum
providers.description: PsiQuantum is a Palo Alto, California photonic quantum computing company founded in 2016 by Jeremy O'Brien, Terry Rudolph, Pete Shadbolt, and Mark Thompson, building utility-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computers based on single-photon qubits at telecom wavelength. Its Omega chipset — a silicon photonic system integrating on-chip single-photon sources, superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors, barium-titanate optical switches, and low-loss fiber couplers — is manufactured on 300mm wafers at GlobalFoundries' flagship fab in Malta, NY, leveraging mature semiconductor processes rather than exotic cryogenic fabrication. The company is constructing two utility- scale, million-qubit, fault-tolerant quantum computing sites: one at Moreton Bay, Queensland, Australia (in partnership with the Australian and Queensland governments) and one at the Illinois Quantum and Microelectronics Park in Chicago, Illinois (with additional R&D at PsiLabs in Daresbury, UK and assembly at PsiFactory in Milpitas, CA). PsiQuantum exposes a developer surface aimed at fault-tolerant quantum algorithm researchers: Construct, an enterprise platform for FTQC algorithm development, resource analysis, and training; Circuit Designer, a free web tool for prototyping and visualizing fault-tolerant quantum circuits; Circuit Hub, a shared library of `.circuit` files; and two open-source Python projects on GitHub — Bartiq, a symbolic quantum resource estimator that compiles subroutine-level costs to global T-gate, Toffoli, qubit, and circuit-volume estimates, and QREF, an open JSON-Schema-based format for representing quantum algorithms as hierarchical DAGs with a Pydantic validation library and a `qref-render` visualization tool. NVIDIA's CUDA-Q is integrated into Construct for accelerated simulation. PsiQuantum does not currently publish a commercial cloud-access REST API, OpenAPI specification, or a general-purpose quantum-execution SDK comparable to those of gate-model quantum cloud providers — its public developer artifacts are confined to FTQC resource-estimation tooling and algorithm-design surfaces — and there is no public pricing or self-serve tier for the underlying quantum hardware.

providers.name: QMC
providers.description: QMC Telecom is a provider of shared telecommunications infrastructure for mobile networks, operating across Brazil, Mexico, Colombia, Peru, and Chile. The company develops, owns, operates, and leases indoor connectivity solutions, street-level solutions (SLS), and towers, rooftops, and special sites, positioning itself as a partner in 5G network densification. Originally surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub, this is a hardware and telecommunications-infrastructure company that publishes no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: Rivos
providers.description: Rivos is a Santa Clara-based silicon startup founded in 2021 that designs data-center class GPUs and AI accelerators around the open RISC-V instruction set architecture, fabricated on TSMC's 3nm process. The company is also developing a CUDA-to-RISC-V translation layer to ease migration of Nvidia-based AI workloads onto its silicon. Rivos raised a 250 million dollar Series A in 2024 led by Matrix Capital Management with Walden Catalyst and Dell Capital Partners, followed by additional rounds bringing total funding above 370 million dollars at a valuation north of 2 billion dollars. In October 2025 Meta announced an agreement to acquire Rivos to bolster its in-house custom silicon program. The company has operated in near-stealth mode and currently exposes no public website content, SDKs, or APIs, so this profile is intentionally an empty apis list with external press and acquisition references.

providers.name: Syntiant
providers.description: Syntiant Corp is an Irvine, California edge-AI semiconductor company founded in 2017 that designs ultra-low-power Neural Decision Processors (NDPs) and the deep-learning models and tooling that run on them, bringing always-on speech, audio, sensor and vision inference to battery-powered devices without a cloud connection. Its silicon family spans the NDP100/NDP101, NDP102, NDP115, NDP120, NDP200 and NDP250, paired with a Training Development Kit (TDK) that maps TensorFlow models onto the NDP core and an embedded SDK for integration into customer firmware. In December 2024 Syntiant completed the USD 150 million acquisition of Knowles Corporation's Consumer MEMS Microphones business, taking the company from roughly 70 to nearly 1,700 employees and making microphones the majority of its revenue. Syntiant is a silicon, module and embedded-software supplier rather than an API provider - enrichment probing found no public web API, no OpenAPI or other machine-readable contract, no developer portal, no first-party package-registry SDKs and no event surface; its SDK and TDK are distributed to customers through a private GitLab and under agreement.

providers.name: Twolabs
providers.description: Twolabs is a San Francisco robotics startup (Y Combinator, Spring 2026) building Tobi, a modular humanoid robot platform for builders to collect data, train skills, and deploy autonomous robots. The two-founder company vertically integrates hardware and AI in-house, streamlining robot training into a Record, Upload, Train, Deploy workflow, and is initially focused on caregiving applications in senior-care facilities such as feeding, dressing, medication reminders, mobility support, and companionship. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company; it does not yet publish a public developer API, documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Vathys
providers.description: Vathys is a deep learning hardware startup developing specialized chips to accelerate deep learning, focusing on data movement rather than computation as the main bottleneck, with the goal of a supercomputer on a chip reaching one petaflop on a single chip. Backed by DCVC (first investment 2018). As of July 2026 Vathys has no discoverable live web presence (vathys.ai and related domains do not resolve) and publishes no public API, developer documentation, packages, or GitHub organization.

providers.name: Aethero
providers.description: Aethero designs and manufactures radiation-hardened, space-rated edge computing systems and AI/ML software for satellites, space stations, and orbital data centers, enabling autonomous on-orbit processing of imagery and sensor data rather than downlinking raw feeds. Its NVIDIA Jetson Orin/Thor-based NxN-ECM and NxA-ECM edge computing modules, Titan and Phobos platforms, the Aether fleet-management software framework, and the AMATDT model annotation/training/deployment tool let spacecraft run AI inference in orbit. Founded in 2023 and headquartered in San Francisco, Aethero raised an $8.4M seed round led by Kindred Ventures in June 2025. Aethero exposes no public web API today; this profile captures the company's identity and its live domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Altair Semiconductor
providers.description: Altair Semiconductor is a fabless semiconductor company that designs low-power, highly integrated cellular IoT chipsets. Its core products are the ALT1250 (a dual-mode LTE-M / NB-IoT modem and SoC with integrated iSIM, MCU and GNSS) and the ALT1350 (a next-generation 5G LPWA SoC that combines LTE-M/NB-IoT, unlicensed-spectrum and satellite NTN connectivity), used in smart meters, asset trackers, wearables, sensors and vehicle telematics. Altair was acquired by Sony in 2016, operated as Sony's cellular IoT unit, and in 2026 was spun back out as an independent company with $50M in funding led by Pitango. This is a hardware/semiconductor provider: it ships chipsets, evaluation kits and datasheets rather than a public developer API, so it carries no OpenAPI, SDK, MCP or developer-portal surface to enrich.

providers.name: Architect Labs
providers.description: Architect Labs is an AI lab building an AI system that explores, designs, and provably verifies custom silicon for the world's most demanding AI and compute workloads. The company is developing a platform that automates the chip-design and verification workflow, aiming to let AI model developers, robotics startups, and neocloud operators generate and verify custom chips without deep hardware-engineering expertise. Architect Labs raised a $24M seed round led by Kindred Ventures, with participation from investors including Aravind Srinivas and Lukasz Kaiser, and is scheduled to appear at DAC 2026. As of this profile the company publishes a marketing site (about, blog, careers) but no public API, developer documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Arlo Industries
providers.description: Arlo Industries is a San Francisco defense hardware company (Y Combinator, Spring 2026) building a passive sensing network for detecting and tracking drones and aerial threats without traditional radar. Its product, Mentat, uses a distributed mesh architecture of low-cost sensors that cooperatively detect and track targets in 3D while remaining invisible to the threats they monitor. The company frames its approach around "asymmetric economics" — sensor deployment cost grows linearly while tracking accuracy grows exponentially — making the system more scalable than conventional radar installations. Arlo has demonstrated its technology with Ukrainian military operators on active frontlines and maintains partnerships across the US, Ukraine, and Northern Europe. As an early-stage hardware startup it publishes no public API, developer program, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: Aspinity
providers.description: Aspinity is a Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania semiconductor company that develops analog machine learning (AnalogML) technology combining ultra-low-power analog signal processing with machine learning for always-on, battery-operated edge AI event detection and classification. Its analogML processors the AML100 and next-generation AML200 deliver TOPS-level inference in a microwatt power footprint, targeting automotive vehicle-security monitoring, smart-home sensing such as glass-break and water-leak detection, and IoT applications including voice and keyword detection and vibration monitoring. Aspinity is a hardware and semiconductor provider and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile tracks its public web and security posture in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Attotude
providers.description: AttoTude is a semiconductor and data-center infrastructure company building the first wired terahertz (THz) interconnect for AI and hyperscale networking. Its platform pairs the AttoEngine, an ASIC-based THz radio built on standard CMOS manufacturing, with AttoWire, a low-loss dielectric waveguide that carries 200/400/800 Gbit/s per lane over reaches up to roughly 40 meters, delivering the bandwidth density of optics without the cost, power, and complexity of photonics. Founded to relieve the interconnect bottleneck in everything-to-everything AI clusters, the company has raised roughly $143M across seed, Series A, Series B, and Series C rounds. This is a hardware company with no public API, developer portal, or SDK; the profile below is enriched only with the identity and domain-security facts the pipeline could verify.

providers.name: CIX Technology
providers.description: CIX Technology (此芯科技) is a Chinese fabless semiconductor company founded in 2021 that designs high-performance, general-purpose heterogeneous intelligent CPU chips for AI computing. The company builds low-power, high-efficiency compute platforms spanning personal computing (PC), vehicle/automotive computing, and edge computing, and partners across the Arm ecosystem (Arm, Arm China, Lenovo and others). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of the venture firm qiming and added to the API Evangelist network. CIX is a silicon/hardware company and publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or developer portal at this time; this profile captures its verifiable public identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Constelli
providers.description: Constelli (Constelli Signals Private Limited) is a Hyderabad, India based defence and aerospace signal-processing company founded in 2017 by Satya Gopal Panigrahi and Avinash Chenreddy. It designs and manufactures radar systems, radar target and echo simulators, deployable drone-based radar payloads, high-performance radar processors, and IRIG-standard digital telemetry receivers for ground, onboard, and satellite telemetry. Its products serve electronic warfare and defence R&D programs globally, including India's Ministry of Defence and DRDO. Constelli raised a $20M Series A led by General Catalyst (with Pravega Ventures and 360 One). It is a hardware/systems company and does not currently publish a public developer API, portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Daivin
providers.description: DAIVIN! is a deep-tech hardware company (Y Combinator Winter 2026, based in San Francisco and Finland) building tankless diving technology. Its core product, SPRING, is marketed as the "world's first tankless diving technology": instead of carrying heavy pressurized oxygen tanks, a diver wears a lightweight vest of electrolyzers and a battery belt that use electricity to split water on demand into breathable oxygen (O2) and hydrogen (H2), targeting depths up to 200 meters / 650 ft. Founder Leo Kankkunen frames breathing as "fundamentally an energy problem," and the company envisions applications beyond recreational and professional diving across space exploration, high-altitude rescue, hospitals, and aircraft. Added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-capital portfolio lead surfaced via y-combinator. Daivin runs a conceptual marketing website (Wix) and a news blog; it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or other machine-readable developer surface, so no API artifacts apply to this provider.

providers.name: Dynamics
providers.description: Dynamics Inc designs and manufactures battery-powered interactive payment cards that work with existing point-of-sale and card infrastructure. Its "Computer-in-a-Card" technology embeds a microprocessor, buttons, and a rewritable magnetic stripe into a standard-size card, enabling programmable multi-account cards, hidden card numbers, and on-card loyalty for banks, merchants, and consumers. The company is a fintech hardware manufacturer backed by Bain Capital Ventures. As of this profile it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this repository tracks its identity and public security posture in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: EdgeQ
providers.description: EdgeQ is a fabless semiconductor company headquartered in Santa Clara, California, building a converged "Base Station-on-a-Chip" that integrates 5G, 6G, non-terrestrial network (NTN), custom waveform, CPU, and antenna-controller functions into a single software-defined silicon platform. Its programmable baseband targets small cells, private enterprise 5G, open RAN, satellite (LEO/MEO) communications, and AI-enabled physical devices. EdgeQ is a hardware and silicon provider surfaced as a portfolio company of Threshold Ventures; it publishes a corporate site, a 5G engineering blog, newsroom, and careers, but exposes no public developer portal, API, or machine-readable API specification.

providers.name: Enfabrica
providers.description: Enfabrica is a semiconductor company building networking silicon and systems for large-scale AI and accelerated-computing infrastructure. Its ACF-S ("Accelerated Compute Fabric") SuperNIC targets maximum throughput with fault-tolerant, multipath connectivity across AI clusters, and its EMFASYS elastic memory fabric system provides memory offload for AI inference workloads. Enfabrica is backed by Spark Capital. The company publishes a technical blog and company news, but does not currently expose a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal, so this profile carries company identity and domain-security signals rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Fabric Cryptography
providers.description: Fabric Cryptography (legal entity Fabric of Truth, Inc.) is a Santa Clara, California semiconductor company founded in 2022 that builds the Verifiable Processing Unit (VPU) — a custom silicon chip whose instruction set is designed exclusively for the mathematical building blocks of modern cryptography. The VPU combines the programmability of a GPU with the performance of an ASIC: hundreds of number-theory units for 32-bit to 384-bit modular arithmetic, custom hash instructions, software-controlled scratchpad memory, a non-blocking network-on-chip, and an on-chip multi-core RISC-V processor for native witness generation. Products announced are the FC 1000 chip, the VPU 8060 card (three FC 1000 chips, ~1 TB/s memory bandwidth to 30 GB) and the "Byte Smasher" server (up to eight VPU 8060 cards). Software is an LLVM-based compiler plus a reconfigurable library of primitives targeting plonky2, plonky3, GKR, halo2, Jolt/Lasso, Nova and TFHE, with a stated future cloud offering. The company raised $33M in 2024 from Blockchain Capital, 1kx, Inflection and Protocol Labs, and has announced collaborations with Polygon Labs (AggLayer) and RISC Zero (Boundless). As of this pass Fabric publishes no developer program, API, SDK registry package or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Hermeus
providers.description: Hermeus is an American aerospace and defense company building rapidly reusable high-Mach and hypersonic aircraft for national-security missions in partnership with the U.S. Department of Defense. Founded in 2018 and headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia, the company applies a hardware-rich, rapid design-build-test approach to move quickly from concept to flight. Its programs include Quarterhorse, a reusable high-speed flight-test aircraft; Darkhorse, a multi-mission reusable hypersonic uncrewed aerial system (UAS); and Chimera, a hybrid turbine-based combined-cycle engine that transitions from turbojet takeoff through supersonic flight into hypersonic acceleration. Hermeus is a hardware manufacturer with no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile tracks the company's public web, security, and corporate properties in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Kets
providers.description: KETS Quantum Security is a Bristol, UK deep-tech company (incorporated 2016) building chip-based quantum-safe encryption and networking hardware. Its product line spans Quantum Key Distribution (QKD), Quantum Random Number Generators (QRNG), and the KETS KORE sub-system, delivering security grounded in the laws of physics rather than computational complexity. KETS technology hardens telecommunications networks, satellite and aerospace communications (including Airbus collaborations), data-center backups, and critical infrastructure control systems against the emerging threat of quantum computing. Backed by European quantum-specialist venture investors including Speedinvest and supported by multiple UK government funding awards, KETS is a hardware and photonics company; it does not currently publish a public API, SDK, or developer portal. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a Speedinvest portfolio lead and enriched with identity and domain-security signals.

providers.name: MITO Material Solutions
providers.description: MITO Material Solutions (MITO Materials) is a specialty chemical company that develops patented hybrid additive technology to strengthen composite and thermoplastic materials. Its platform functionalizes graphene and biomaterials to improve strength, durability, flexibility, and sustainability without requiring changes to a manufacturer's existing process. Core products include the MITO hybrid additive platform, MITO E-GO, MITO E-GO Res-1, and MITO ACRE, serving the sports and recreation, transportation, automotive, and infrastructure industries. The company is a Techstars portfolio company and was added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this pass, MITO publishes no developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Nitricity
providers.description: Nitricity is a climate-tech and agricultural-technology company that produces nitrogen fertilizer on-farm from only air, water, and renewable electricity. Founded in 2018 by Stanford graduate researchers Nicolas Pinkowski and Joshua McEnaney, the company uses a solar-powered plasma / electrochemical process to fix atmospheric nitrogen and produce nitric acid and calcium nitrate fertilizers on-site and on-demand, eliminating the fossil-fuel-intensive Haber-Bosch process and long-distance transportation that make conventional fertilizer responsible for roughly 5% of global greenhouse gas emissions. Backed by Khosla Ventures, Fine Structure Ventures, Lowercarbon Capital, and strategic investor Chipotle, Nitricity is a hardware and physical-product company; it publishes a corporate website, blog, and field-trial program but exposes no public API, developer portal, or technical integration surface.

providers.name: Photon Crystal Energy
providers.description: Photon Crystal Energy Technology Ltd. (广东光晶能源科技有限公司) is a China-based perovskite photovoltaic module manufacturer, founded May 2022 and headquartered in Foshan, Guangdong. The company commercializes full wet-process, full-printed perovskite PV modules for building-integrated photovoltaics (BIPV), photovoltaic curtain walls, rooftop distributed solar, carports and architectural solar applications. Product families include standard, semi-transparent, textured, architectural color and solar tile modules, and the firm operates a 100 MW full-printed perovskite pilot line with IEC 61215 / IEC 61730 certification milestones. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming and added to the API Evangelist network; it publishes a marketing/corporate website but no public API, SDK, or developer surface.

providers.name: Quantum Systems
providers.description: Quantum-Systems GmbH is a Gilching/Munich, Germany-based dual-use drone manufacturer founded in 2015 by former Bundeswehr helicopter pilot Florian Seibel. The company designs, builds, and operates small electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) fixed-wing unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) for reconnaissance, intelligence, surveillance, target acquisition (RSTA), surveying, and mapping. Its flagship platforms include the Trinity Pro (mapping/surveying VTOL with up to 90-minute endurance), the Vector tactical reconnaissance drone (the de facto main small UAS supplier to the German Bundeswehr and, with 619+ systems delivered as of April 2025, one of the most-used Western reconnaissance drones in Ukraine), the Reliant long-range Group 2 ISR/RSTA platform built for the U.S. market with 10+ hours endurance and hot-swappable MOD-compliant payload bays (EO/IR, SIGINT, EW, CRPA), and the Ukraine-manufactured Sparta drone carrier that delivers two FPV drones to a 200 km combat radius. All platforms are operated through QBase 3D, Quantum-Systems' proprietary Windows-based mission planning, control, and post-processing software with integrated ESRI terrain data and direct export to Pix4D, Agisoft, Propeller, and Trimble Business Center. The Vector tactical line is built on Auterion's flight stack. Backed by HV Capital, DTCP, Thiel Capital, Project A, Airbus Ventures, and Omnes Capital, the company reached unicorn status in May 2025 as "Europe's first dual-use unicorn." Quantum-Systems supplies the militaries of Germany, the United States, Ukraine, Australia, the Netherlands, New Zealand, Romania, and Spain. There is no public developer API, REST endpoint, SDK, or open-source release for QBase 3D or any Quantum-Systems platform; integration with Pix4D/Agisoft/Propeller/Trimble is via standard photogrammetry file exchange (GeoTIFF, RAW imagery, flight logs), not a programmable API.

providers.name: Quintessent Communications
providers.description: Quintessent is a deep-tech photonics startup based in Goleta, California, developing optical connectivity solutions that address the communication bottlenecks in large-scale computing and AI infrastructure. The company builds chip-to-chip optical interconnect technology grounded in quantum-dot laser epitaxy, and has established supply chains for quantum-dot epitaxial wafers used in AI optical interconnects. Quintessent is a hardware and semiconductor photonics company rather than a software/API provider; it exposes no public developer portal, API, SDK, or documentation surface. Backed by Battery Ventures, Entrada Ventures, Foothill Ventures, and Sierra Ventures, with research funding from DARPA, ARPA-E, and the NSF, the company was surfaced as a venture-portfolio lead and profiled here for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: SiLC
providers.description: SiLC Technologies is a silicon photonics company headquartered in Monrovia, California that builds integrated single-chip FMCW (frequency-modulated continuous-wave) LiDAR — coherent 4D vision systems that capture depth, instantaneous velocity via micro-Doppler, and dual-polarization intensity from one photonic chip. Its Eyeonic product family spans Eyeonic Trace Ultra (a Class 1 laser line scanner for industrial automation and inspection), Eyeonic Vista (an ultra-long-range perimeter security and counter-UAS vision system with detection beyond 2 km), and Eyeonic Edge (high-precision 4D inspection of large objects). The company sells sensors, modules and vision chips to industrial and AI robotics, perimeter security, and mobility customers. It was founded by Dr. Mehdi Asghari and is backed in part by Honda. SiLC ships hardware, not software services: as of this profile it publishes no public developer program, API, SDK, documentation portal, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Thrive Agritech
providers.description: Thrive Agritech is a horticultural lighting company that designs and manufactures high-efficiency LED grow lights and related power systems for commercial indoor farming, greenhouses, and vertical farming operations. Its product line includes fixtures such as Strata, Boost XE, and a 1050W LED grow light, along with a Remote Power System, backed by lighting design services, rebate assistance, and multi-year warranties. The company positions itself around energy efficiency, ROI, and long-term grower partnerships rather than a developer or API offering. Surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network, this profile was enriched by probing the public web surface; no public API, developer portal, documentation, or machine-readable specification was found.

providers.name: Vertical Semiconductor
providers.description: Vertical Semiconductor is an MIT spinout developing next-generation vertical Gallium Nitride (GaN) power devices for AI data centers and grid infrastructure. Built on a decade of research from MIT's Palacios Group, its vertical GaN transistors push energy conversion closer to the chip with less power loss and heat, targeting high-voltage applications from 100V to over 2kV. The company claims up to 30% higher efficiency, a 50% smaller power footprint, and 10% lower total cost of ownership versus silicon, and has demonstrated its platform on 8-inch wafers using standard silicon CMOS manufacturing. It is a hardware/deep-tech power-electronics company with no public API, developer portal, SDK, or OpenAPI surface. Backed by Playground Global.

providers.name: Vulcan Elements
providers.description: Vulcan Elements is a United States manufacturer of sintered permanent neodymium-iron-boron (NdFeB) rare earth magnets, founded in 2023 and headquartered in Research Triangle Park, North Carolina. The company produces high-performance rare earth magnets domestically for defense and commercial applications — the components that convert electricity into motion in motors, drones, robotics, vehicles and consumer electronics — as an alternative to a supply chain concentrated in China. In 2025 it announced a $65 million Series A, a $620 million loan from the Pentagon's Office of Strategic Capital, and a $1.4 billion partnership with the U.S. government and ReElement Technologies to build a vertically integrated domestic magnet supply chain, including a nearly $1 billion, 1,000-job magnet factory in Benson, Johnston County, North Carolina. Vulcan Elements is a physical-goods manufacturer: it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Zetwerk
providers.description: Zetwerk is a global contract-manufacturing and B2B supply-chain company that connects original equipment manufacturers with a vetted network of manufacturing partners across processes including CNC machining, die casting, forging, injection molding, and sheet-metal stamping. It serves industries such as aerospace and defense, automotive, consumer electronics, renewable energy, and industrial equipment, offering production sourcing, quoting, and program management. Backed by Accel, D1 Capital, Khosla Ventures, and Lightspeed Venture Partners, Zetwerk operates as a manufacturing services marketplace rather than a developer platform: as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or programmatic integration surface.

providers.name: SJSemi
providers.description: SJSemi (SJSemiconductor (Jiangyin) Corp.) is a Chinese semiconductor Middle-End-Of-Line (MEOL) pure-play foundry and outsourced assembly and test (OSAT) provider, founded in 2014 as a joint venture between JCET and SMIC and headquartered in the Jiangyin High-Tech Industrial Development Zone, Jiangsu, with offices in Shanghai and Santa Clara, California. The company operates a 12-inch wafer bumping, wafer-level chip-scale packaging, chip probing and final-test line, and supplies advanced packaging and 3D multi-die integration services — Cu pillar, RDL, fan-out, TSV and silicon interposer 2.5D — into smartphone, 5G communications, high-performance computing, data-center and automotive electronics supply chains. It is a contract manufacturer of physical semiconductor packaging services and publishes no public developer program, API, or machine-readable interface contract.

providers.name: Swiftmile
providers.description: Swiftmile is a California-based hardware and IoT company building universal charging and parking infrastructure for micromobility — docking stations that power, secure and organize shared and privately owned e-bikes and e-scooters, including solar-powered units and integrated digital advertising panels. Founded around 2014 and headquartered on the San Francisco Peninsula, it supplied secure charging docks to the New York City DOT public e-bike charging pilot alongside PopWheels and Swobbee. Company interviews describe a fleet- and battery-management backend with integrations offered to micromobility operators, but Swiftmile has never published a public developer program, API reference, SDK, or machine-readable contract of any kind, and as of 2026-08-29 swiftmile.com no longer serves the company website at all — the domain answers with a Nexcess hosting placeholder and a TLS certificate that does not match the hostname.

providers.name: Tidal Vision
providers.description: Tidal Vision Products, Inc. is a Bellingham, Washington biotechnology and specialty-chemicals manufacturer, and the only commercial-scale US producer of chitosan — a non-toxic, non-hazmat, biodegradable industrial biopolymer upcycled from crab and shrimp shell waste. Its zero-waste Chitofining process extracts, modifies and formulates chitosan chemistries that displace PFAS, halogenated chemicals, toxic antimicrobials and persistent plastics across three business lines: Tidal Clear water and wastewater treatment, Tidal Grow AgriScience crop and soil inputs, and Tidal-Tec Biomaterial Science performance materials. The company closed an oversubscribed $140M+ Series B in 2025 and acquired Clear Water Services. It is a materials-science manufacturer and publishes no public developer program, API, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: AICE
providers.description: AICE is a defense-technology company building the next generation of underwater defense systems: autonomous swarms of modular marine drones that secure naval assets and coastal infrastructure against evolving underwater threats. Founded in 2026 by former NASA engineer Gregoire Chomette and European Robotics Champion Remi Bouteiller, the company is part of the Y Combinator Spring 2026 batch, is based in the San Francisco Bay Area with hardware manufactured in France, and applies swarm robotics and AI to surveillance, detection, and protection of critical subsea infrastructure. AICE currently ships hardware and does not publish a public API, SDK, or developer platform; this profile tracks the company for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Aquantia
providers.description: Aquantia Corporation was a fabless semiconductor company headquartered in San Jose, California, that designed and marketed multi-gigabit Ethernet connectivity — AQtion client network controllers, Atlantic controllers, and multi-gig PHY transceivers for enterprise, data center, automotive, and consumer networking. Aquantia was acquired by Marvell Technology in 2019; the aquantia.com domain now redirects to marvell.com. It operated no public HTTP/developer API or developer portal — its published developer surface is silicon: Linux kernel and DPDK "Atlantic" NIC drivers, firmware, and tooling in the github.com/Aquantia organization. Retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio-lead stub; there is no API to enrich.

providers.name: Axalta Coating Systems
providers.description: Axalta Coating Systems is a global supplier of liquid and powder coatings for transportation and industrial end-markets, operating through Performance Coatings (refinish and industrial) and Mobility Coatings (light vehicle and commercial vehicle) segments. Brands include Cromax, Spies Hecker, Standox, Imron, and Voltatex. In July 2024 Axalta acquired The CoverFlexx Group from Transtar Holding for $285 million to expand its economy-tier aftermarket coverage in North America. In November 2025 Axalta announced a $17 billion all-stock merger of equals with AkzoNobel that is expected to close in late 2026 or early 2027, forming a coatings company with dual headquarters in Amsterdam and Philadelphia.

providers.name: Bouffalo Lab
providers.description: Bouffalo Lab (博流智能) is a fabless chip design company founded in 2016 and headquartered in Nanjing, China, focused on ultra-low-power AIoT (AI + IoT) and edge-computing system chips. Its product line centers on RISC-V based microcontrollers with integrated wireless connectivity — the BL602/BL604 (Wi-Fi 2.4G + BLE 5.0), BL702/BL704/BL706 (Zigbee 3.0 + BLE 5.0), BL606P (quad-mode dual-core Wi-Fi/BT/BLE/Zigbee), and the BL616/BL618 and BL808 families — combining wireless radios, audio/video processing, and on-device AI algorithms. The company ships the open-source BouffaloSDK (a merge of bl_mcu_sdk and bl_iot_sdk) under Apache 2.0 through its public GitHub organization, along with hardware abstraction drivers, Matter/Thread support, and NuttX RTOS ports. Bouffalo Lab is a hardware/firmware provider rather than a web-API provider; it exposes no public HTTP/REST developer API, so the enrichment pipeline captures its developer surface (GitHub SDK org) and domain security posture. It is a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners.

providers.name: Cuspai
providers.description: CuspAI is a Cambridge, UK artificial intelligence company, founded in 2024, building generative AI for materials discovery. Its platform lets users specify desired physical and chemical properties — such as selective CO2 binding — and then generates, evaluates, and optimizes candidate molecular and material structures for applications spanning carbon capture, energy storage, catalysis, water purification, electric vehicles, and healthcare. CuspAI has raised roughly $130M (a $30M seed and a $100M Series A in September 2025) from investors including Northzone and Prosus Ventures, and maintains open-source scientific computing tooling on GitHub. As of mid-2026 the company operates a placeholder marketing site with no public API, developer portal, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Cypress
providers.description: Cypress Semiconductor Corporation was a San Jose, California semiconductor company founded in 1982, and an early Mayfield venture investment. It designed and manufactured mixed-signal, embedded, and connectivity silicon — most notably the PSoC programmable system-on-chip microcontrollers, WICED Wi-Fi and Bluetooth wireless combos, USB controllers (EZ-USB), NOR flash and SRAM memory, and automotive Traveo microcontrollers — supported by the ModusToolbox and PSoC Creator developer tooling and the Cypress Developer Community. Infineon Technologies AG acquired Cypress in April 2020 for approximately 9.4 billion dollars; the business, its developer community, and its GitHub repositories have since been folded into Infineon. cypress.com now redirects to infineon.com and the developer resources live at community.infineon.com. Cypress shipped hardware SDKs and embedded toolchains rather than a public web/REST API, so there is no independent HTTP API surface to catalog for this entity — this profile documents it as a historical, acquired provider.

providers.name: Foundation Robotics Labs
providers.description: Foundation Robotics Labs — trading publicly as Foundation and incorporated as Foundation Future Industries, Inc. — is a San Francisco humanoid robotics company founded in April 2024 by Sankaet Pathak, Arjun Sethi and Mike LeBlanc. It builds Phantom, a general-purpose humanoid robot aimed at industrial automation, logistics, inspection, disaster response and defense, and Cortex, the company's self-described physics foundation model built on Deep Variational Bayes Filters that pairs physics-informed prediction with vision-language reasoning to drive the robot. The company's published master plan runs from building humanoids through fleet coherence and on to building cities, and it states explicitly that it designs for military environments, unlike U.S. competitors committed to non-weaponization. Foundation has raised a reported $111M and is traded on the secondary market via Forge Global. As of this profile Foundation publishes NO public developer surface — no developer portal, documentation, API reference, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI definition, SDK, package, MCP server or agent card. Its entire public web presence is a five-page Framer marketing site (home, Phantom, Cortex, master plan, culture, careers) with no /docs, /developers, /api, /pricing, /terms or /privacy paths and no llms.txt. Its GitHub organization (github.com/foundationbot, verified first-party by @foundation.bot commit-author domains) holds internal test benches and forks of open-source robotics tooling — Drake, jetson-containers, Kalibr, PlotJuggler, Fast-DDS, an EtherCAT master, actuator dyno benches and NXP S32K MCU demos — and contains no API specification of any kind.

providers.name: Harman International
providers.description: Harman International, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Samsung Electronics, is a global leader in connected technologies for automotive, consumer, and enterprise markets, including connected car systems, audio products, professional solutions, and connected services. Harman does not currently publish a public developer portal or open APIs; integrations with Harman platforms (such as Ignite, Ready Connect, and audio brands like JBL, Harman Kardon, and AKG) are typically delivered through commercial partnerships and OEM agreements.

providers.name: houmo
providers.description: HOUMO.AI (后摩智能) is a Chinese fabless semiconductor company founded in 2020 that develops compute-in-memory (CIM / storage-and-computation integrated) edge AI chips for running large language models and other AI workloads on endpoint devices. Its products include the MOMAGIC (H30) series processors, LIQING M.2 modules, and Limou (LM 5050 / LM 5070 / LM 30) AI acceleration cards, paired with the Houmo Avenue software toolchain (PyTorch / TensorFlow / ONNX, CUDA-style front end) for model quantization, compilation, and deployment. The company targets edge inference, autonomous driving, embodied robotics, and intelligent mobile devices, and runs a developer community with documentation and downloads. This profile is a hardware / AI-chip vendor with a developer toolchain rather than a public web API provider; no REST/OpenAPI, OAuth, or hosted API surface was found.

providers.name: INDEX Robotics
providers.description: INDEX Robotics is a South Korean humanoid robotics startup based in Seongnam (Bundang) building high-precision actuators and upper-body humanoid robots for high-mix, low-volume industrial work. Its core products are the IA Series, a family of high-precision actuators purpose-built for humanoid joints, and INDEX01, a compact upper-body humanoid prototype that deliberately foregoes a mobile base so it can slot into constrained factory workspaces for logistics handling, machining support, and precision assembly. The company treats joint precision, responsiveness under sustained repetitive motion, and long-run performance consistency as the core unsolved problems in humanoid commercialization. In February 2026 INDEX Robotics closed a $1M (KRW 1.5B) seed round led by Futureplay with Bass Ventures and 500 Global co-investing. This is a hardware company with no public API, SDK, or developer program at this time.

providers.name: Local Motors
providers.description: Local Motors was an American vehicle manufacturer founded in 2007 by John "Jay" Rogers Jr. that built vehicles through open co-creation and distributed "microfactories" rather than conventional mass production. Its community designed and the company produced the Rally Fighter off-road car from its first Chandler, Arizona microfactory, the Strati — the first car to be 3D-printed live, in 44 hours at IMTS 2014 — and, from 2016, Olli, a 3D-printed electric autonomous shuttle whose conversational passenger interface ran on IBM Watson and which was piloted at National Harbor, Maryland and other campus and transit sites. The company operated microfactories in Chandler, Knoxville and National Harbor and spun its crowdsourcing community out as Launch Forth. Local Motors ceased operations in January 2022 after fifteen years, having failed to raise further capital, and its intellectual-property portfolio was acquired by drone manufacturer RapidFlight of Manassas, Virginia in July 2023. Local Motors never operated a public developer program: the archive of localmotors.com holds an internal django-tastypie JSON API under /api/v1/ that served the co-creation community website, but no developer portal, API reference, SDK, or machine-readable specification was ever published, and its GitHub organization has zero public repositories. The domain is no longer the company's — it now answers HTTP 301 on every path to a third-party affiliate article — so there is no live API surface to catalog. This profile is retained as a historical record.

providers.name: Planqc
providers.description: planqc GmbH is a German quantum computing company building neutral-atom quantum computers, using individual atoms trapped in optical lattices as qubits on what it describes as the most promising path to fault-tolerant, scalable systems. Founded in 2022 as a spin-off of the Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich, the company delivers full-stack quantum computing — hardware, control software, and applications — including its MAQCS (Multicore Atomic Quantum Computing System) line for enterprise and scientific customers across aerospace, automotive, energy, and financial services. planqc operates from Garching and Ulm in Germany and Innsbruck in Austria, and is backed by investors including Speedinvest. As of this profile the company exposes no public developer API, SDK, developer portal, or programmatic cloud-access surface; access is arranged directly through the company. This profile is a portfolio-lead stub in the API Evangelist network, enriched with verified public identity and a domain-security probe.

providers.name: Qphox
providers.description: QphoX is a Delft, Netherlands-based quantum technology company founded in 2021 and spun out of Delft University of Technology (TU Delft). It develops quantum networking hardware to tackle the scaling challenges of quantum computing, centered on its Quantum Transducer, described as the first quantum interface between single optical and single microwave photons, enabling optical interconnects between superconducting quantum processors. Alongside the transducer, QphoX offers an Optical Control System for delivering RF signals into extreme cryogenic environments and a CryoSwitch Control Module for use with Radiall's cryogenic latching actuator. The company publishes open-source Python instrument-control libraries (QCoDeS drivers) on GitHub for operating its hardware. QphoX is backed by Speedinvest. QphoX exposes no public web API or developer portal.

providers.name: Upverter
providers.description: Upverter is a browser-based, collaborative electronic design automation (EDA) platform for schematic capture and PCB layout, founded in Toronto in 2010 (Y Combinator W11) and acquired by Altium in 2017. Surfaced as a Version One Ventures portfolio company. As of the July 2026 enrichment probe the upverter.com platform returns HTTP 502 on every path, its docs/blog/status subdomains no longer resolve, and no public API surface remains; the GitHub organization is dormant since 2019.

providers.name: Valinor
providers.description: Valinor Enterprises is a defense and government technology operational holding company — a "company of companies" that builds and buys mission-critical technologies to fill the gaps others ignore. It centralizes go-to-market, compliance, security, and operations while decentralizing engineering across lean Product Companies including Condor (attritable aerial systems), Dispatch (drone charging infrastructure, selected by DIU for the CADDS program), Harbor (expeditionary medical systems for the Marine Corps), Reflex (smart optics with onboard vision models), and Streamline (AI-enabled data collection with structured ontology write-back). Backed by General Catalyst; raised a $54M Series A led by Friends & Family Capital. Valinor publishes no public API or developer portal; its developer footprint is a GitHub organization and the @valinor-enterprises npm scope.

providers.name: Voltron Data
providers.description: Voltron Data is a Mountain View-based data infrastructure company (founded 2021) behind Theseus, a GPU-accelerated, composable distributed SQL query engine for petabyte-scale analytics and AI pipelines, distributed embedded through partners rather than as a self-serve public API. The company is a major steward of the open-source composable data stack — Apache Arrow, Ibis, Substrait, Arrow Flight SQL, and ADBC — acquired Claypot AI in January 2024, and is backed by Battery Ventures, GV, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and Walden Catalyst, with an Accenture investment in 2025. As of 2026-07-21 the company website (voltrondata.com) is unreachable — the domain is registered but its DNS zone is lame-delegated — leaving the GitHub organization as the live public surface; no public API, SDK packages, or developer portal are published.

providers.name: Omate
providers.description: Omate designs and manufactures Wearable-as-a-Service (WaaS) safety solutions built around cellular-connected smartwatches for people who need protection — seniors, children, and lone workers. Its devices (such as the O6L Pro line, marketed under the Omahome brand) combine GPS location tracking, SOS calling, fall detection, and two-way voice into a managed hardware-plus-service offering sold direct to consumers and through partners. Omate is a hardware and connected-device company; as of this profile it exposes no public developer program, API, or SDK. This entry was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio lead and enriched with an identity and domain-security pass.

providers.name: PowerLight Technologies
providers.description: PowerLight Technologies is an American engineering company headquartered in Kent, Washington that develops laser power beaming systems — wireless transmission of kilowatt-level electrical power over free space and over optical fiber. Founded as LaserMotive and renamed in 2017, the company builds power-over-fiber and free-space laser power links for defense unmanned aerial systems, telecom sites, temporary and disaster power, smart-grid applications, and lunar and satellite power distribution, including work under DARPA's LunA-10 program. Its products are hardware energy-transmission systems rather than software, and the company publishes no public developer program, API, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: 3com
providers.description: 3Com Corporation was a networking-technology pioneer founded in 1979 by Robert Metcalfe, the co-inventor of Ethernet, and colleagues; its name derived from "Computer, Communication, and Compatibility." 3Com built Ethernet network interface cards, switches, routers, and enterprise networking and security hardware, and at one point owned the Palm handheld computing business. An early Mayfield Fund portfolio investment (seed participation in 1981, alongside NEA, Venrock, and Sequoia), 3Com later operated the 3Com, H3C, and TippingPoint brands before being acquired by Hewlett-Packard in 2010 for roughly $2.7 billion, after which the standalone brand was wound down. This record is a historical company profile; 3Com no longer operates an independent developer portal, public API, or live product surface (the 3com.com domain now serves a placeholder page).

providers.name: 6thSense
providers.description: 6thSense is a physical-AI hardware company building the touch layer for dexterous robots. It designs and manufactures wearable tactile-sensing data gloves that capture how human hands interact with the world — pressure, contact, grip, and 3D hand pose — alongside custom tactile skin molded to robot hands. Its capture stack synchronizes eight aligned modalities (tactile and pressure proxies, egocentric video, depth/RGB-D, hand pose, motion and IMU dynamics, wrist and scene cameras, dense labels and commentary, and success/failure outcomes) into model-ready demonstration datasets used to train the next generation of dexterous, manipulation-capable robots. Founded in 2026 in San Francisco and backed by Y Combinator (S26).

providers.name: 9 Mothers Corporation
providers.description: 9 Mothers Corporation is a defense technology company founded in 2024 and based in Austin, Texas, building AI-powered counter-drone (C-sUAS) point defense systems for the FPV drone era.
