In 2017 Mentor Graphics was acquired by Siemens and its portfolio now ships as Siemens EDA (part of Siemens Digital Industries Software), including Calibre for physical verification and DFM, the Questa functional verification platform, and the Xpedition / PADS PCB design suites. The mentor.com domain now redirects to the Siemens EDA site. Siemens EDA delivers desktop and cloud-hosted engineering software and managed services; it does not publish a public developer REST API, OpenAPI definition, or self-serve developer portal, so there is no public API surface to enrich for this provider.

providers.name: Meridian Data
providers.description: Meridian Data, Inc. was a Battery Ventures-backed maker of network-attached storage (NAS) appliances, best known for the Snap! Server workgroup NAS line and one of the industry's first storage operating systems for entry- and workgroup-level appliances. Quantum Corporation acquired Meridian Data in a stock swap valued at roughly $85M, completed June 1, 1999, folding its technology into Quantum's storage systems strategy. The company has not operated independently since and publishes no current developer or API surface; this profile is retained for API Evangelist network completeness as a historical, acquired entity.

providers.name: Milliray
providers.description: Milliray is an airspace-security company building millimeter-wave radar technology to detect, track, and classify the small drones that conventional radar systems miss — from $50 quadcopters to autonomous swarms. Its DroneTector product fuses multiple sensor types into all-weather, 24/7 units that operate standalone or in networked mesh configurations, protecting airports, critical infrastructure (substations, refineries, water-treatment facilities), and forward-deployed defense operations. The company is backed by Y Combinator, NATO DIANA, the UK Defence and Security Accelerator, and the Royal Academy of Engineering. As of this enrichment pass Milliray publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation surface — it is a hardware/defense provider without a programmable interface.

providers.name: Muir Test Systems
providers.description: Muir Test Systems is a company in the Battery Ventures portfolio, operating in the test-and-measurement space. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. An enrichment pass on 2026-07-20 searched the web, npm/PyPI/Maven/other package registries, and probed for a developer/API surface and found no publicly discoverable developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDKs, or hosted MCP server. No production website domain for the company resolved during probing, so domain, well-known, and security probes could not be run. This profile remains a company-only lead with no API artifacts.

providers.name: Mutto Optronics
providers.description: Mutto Optronics (Mutto Inc) is a Taipei, Taiwan-based provider of resistive and capacitive touch panels for the mobile phone and tablet market. Formerly a Qiming Venture Partners portfolio company, it is now publicly held. It is a hardware/optronics manufacturer with no public API, developer program, or documented software surface. The registered domain (muttoinc.com) has lapsed and now resolves to a domain-parking and ad-monetization landing page across all hosts, so there is no first-party developer, docs, or API infrastructure to enrich.

providers.name: Mycotech
providers.description: MYCL (Mycotech Lab) is an Indonesian biomaterials company, founded in 2015 and based in Bandung, that cultivates mushroom mycelium on agricultural waste to produce sustainable, carbon-sequestering alternatives to animal leather, plastics, and construction materials. Its flagship product is Mylea, a mycelium-based leather-like material, alongside Biobo binder board, MYCL Composite for architecture and interior design, and Mylea Sea, a seaweed-based biopolymer. A certified B Corp and Good Design Award winner backed by 500 Global and the Unreasonable Group, MYCL sells physical materials and finished goods rather than software; it publishes no public API, developer portal, or developer documentation.

providers.name: Mycoworks
providers.description: MycoWorks is a San Francisco Bay Area biotechnology and advanced-materials company founded in 2013 by artist Philip Ross and Sophia Wang, headquartered in Emeryville, California. It engineers premium leather-alternative biomaterials from mycelium using its patented Fine Mycelium process, sold under the Reishi brand to luxury fashion, automotive, and design partners. The company was backed by DCVC and other investors; it entered insolvency and was wound down through an Assignment for the Benefit of Creditors in late 2025. MycoWorks operates as a physical-materials manufacturer and publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI definition, SDK, or developer portal, so this API Evangelist profile carries company identity only.

providers.name: Mythic
providers.description: Mythic is a high-performance analog computing company building Analog Processing Units (APUs) for energy-efficient AI inference. Its compute-in-memory architecture stores AI model parameters directly in the processor to eliminate the memory bottleneck of traditional digital designs, targeting data center, automotive, robotics, edge, and defense workloads with claims of dramatically lower energy use and cost versus GPUs. Surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC and Threshold Ventures. As of this enrichment pass Mythic publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Nanoconduction
providers.description: Nanoconduction, Inc. was a Sunnyvale, California hardware startup that developed carbon-nanotube-based thermal management (chip-cooling) solutions for the microprocessor industry. The company licensed NASA Ames-developed Nano Engineered Thermal Material — vertically aligned carbon nanotube array composites that act as a high-efficiency thermal interface at the junction where processors meet heat sinks. Backed by Battery Ventures, Jerusalem Venture Partners, Phoenix Venture Partners, Western Technology Investment, and Woodside Fund (roughly $23M raised), Nanoconduction was acquired by Unidym in July 2008 and is permanently closed. It was surfaced as a Battery Ventures portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; the enrichment pass found no public API, developer, or specification surface — a defunct materials-science hardware company with no digital API footprint.

providers.name: nasn-auto
providers.description: NASN Automotive Electronics Co., Ltd. is a Shanghai-based automotive chassis electronic-control manufacturer founded in 2016, developing brake-by-wire and steer-by-wire systems for smart and assisted driving. Its products include the NBooster intelligent braking system, brushless electric power steering (EPS) controllers, and motion-control solutions for autonomous vehicles. Backed by Qiming Venture Partners, Matrix Partners China, Hillhouse and CATL, NASN has raised roughly $231M and is a Tier-1 supplier pursuing a Hong Kong listing. Surfaced as a Qiming portfolio company; NASN is an automotive hardware manufacturer with no public developer API surface at nasn-auto.com.

providers.name: Natural Intelligence Systems
providers.description: Natural Intelligence Semiconductor (Natural Intelligence Systems) is a fabless semiconductor startup founded in 2016 and headquartered in Boise, Idaho, led by founder and CEO Paul Dlugosch. The company is developing the Natural Neural Processor (NNP), a novel processor architecture inspired by the human neocortex to deliver disruptive performance for artificial intelligence and big-data analytics workloads. Its roadmap spans the chips, system boards, and a software tool chain of compilers, drivers, and low-level APIs needed to bring the NNP into customer systems. It exposes no public web API today; the developer surface is chip- and driver-level tooling. Added to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio lead.

providers.name: Nervana Systems
providers.description: Nervana Systems was a deep-learning and AI-hardware startup founded in 2014 (founders Naveen Rao, Amir Khosrowshahi, and Arjun Bansal) that built the open-source "neon" deep-learning framework and a custom AI training ASIC (the Nervana Engine). Backed by DCVC (Data Collective) and others, the company was acquired by Intel in August 2016 and folded into Intel's AI effort, where its work became the Intel Nervana Neural Network Processor (NNP-T / NNP-I); Intel wound that product line down in early 2020 following its Habana Labs acquisition. Nervana Systems no longer exists as an independent entity and publishes no live developer surface: its primary domains (nervanasys.com, nervana.com, nervanasystems.com) no longer resolve, and it is not present in the APIs.io catalog. This profile is retained as a historical VC-portfolio lead.

providers.name: Network Engines
providers.description: Network Engines, Inc. was an early venture-backed (Canaan Partners) server and storage appliance maker that built application platforms and OEM appliance integration hardware for software vendors. The company was later acquired by UNICOM Global and rebranded UNICOM Engineering — its original networkengines.com domain now redirects to www.unicomengineering.com, where the business is positioned around Dell-based appliances and OEM engineering / build-to-order application platform integration. It is a hardware and manufacturing-services business, not an API producer: an enrichment probe on 2026-07-20 found no public developer program, no OpenAPI, no /api or /developers surface, and no /.well-known discovery documents on either host. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a Canaan Partners portfolio lead; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Noise & Vibration Technologies
providers.description: Noise & Vibration Technologies (NVT Group) is a Battery Ventures-backed platform of test-and-measurement companies that design, manufacture, and support equipment for measuring, simulating, and analyzing vibration, noise, shock, and other environmental variables. Its operating brands include Data Physics (SignalCalc dynamic signal analyzers and vibration controllers), Team Corporation (electrodynamic and hydraulic shakers), and Lansmont (package and product-testing systems), serving aerospace, defense, commercial space, automotive, and industrial customers worldwide. The company ships hardware and desktop analysis/control software rather than any public web API, REST service, SDK, or developer portal, so it has no programmable API surface for the API Evangelist network at this time.

providers.name: nomiku
providers.description: Nomiku (Y Combinator W15, backed by Slow Ventures) was a consumer-hardware startup that built an affordable WiFi-connected sous-vide immersion circulator and the companion Tender recipe app, later pivoting to the Nomiku Meals ready-to-cook subscription paired with the Nomiku Smart Cooker. The company emailed customers on December 13, 2019 that it was discontinuing the Smart Cooker and Meals and suspending operations. It exposed no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; the device was controlled through a private mobile app and cloud backend. Retained in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead identity record for historical and investor-graph completeness only.

providers.name: North
providers.description: North (formerly Thalmic Labs) was a wearable-computing hardware company founded in 2012 in Kitchener, Ontario by University of Waterloo graduates Stephen Lake, Matthew Bailey, and Aaron Grant. It first shipped the Myo gesture-control armband, which read electrical muscle activity to wirelessly control computers and other devices, and later pivoted to Focals, consumer smart glasses with a heads-up display. A Y Combinator Winter 2013 company that raised over $140M, North was acquired by Google in January 2020 and wound down; its products and consumer-facing website (bynorth.com) were discontinued. This profile is retained as a network record. North published no public API, developer portal, or SDKs, so there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Northstar Technology
providers.description: Northstar Technology (Northstar Technologies, Inc.) was a marine navigation electronics company and an exited Battery Ventures portfolio investment. It was a leader in premium marine GPS/chartplotter hardware and was acquired by Brunswick Corporation in December 2002 to form Brunswick New Technologies, and later sold to Navico in 2007. It is a defunct hardware company with no live website, developer portal, or public API surface; the enrichment pipeline found no API artifacts to harvest.

providers.name: Nova Instruments
providers.description: Nova Instruments is a test-and-measurement platform company that designs, develops, and manufactures instruments and systems for analyzing fluid and solid mechanics. It operates a family of established brands — Brookhaven Instruments, Dantec Dynamics, DegreeC, NDT Systems, Phoenix Inspection Systems, Technology Design, and Stresstech — spanning particle characterization, optical measurement, thermal management, and non-destructive testing. A portfolio company of Battery Ventures since 2010, it operates as part of the Nova Ventures Group. As a hardware-focused instruments manufacturer, Nova Instruments does not currently publish a public web API, developer portal, or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: Nubis
providers.description: Nubis Communications is a co-packaged optics (CPO) and silicon-photonics semiconductor startup building high-density, low-power optical interconnects for AI, machine-learning, and hyperscale data-center systems. Its technology places optics directly next to switch and accelerator ASICs to move data at very high bandwidth with dramatically lower energy per bit than pluggable optics. The company (originally at nubis-inc.com) has been absorbed into Ciena, whose optics-for-co-packaged-applications product line now carries the work; the former Nubis domain redirects to Ciena. As a fabless hardware / photonics-IP company it exposes no public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal, so no API artifacts apply to this record.

providers.name: Nuvia
providers.description: Nuvia was a semiconductor startup founded in 2019 to design high-performance, energy-efficient Arm-based CPU cores for data-center and client computing, backed by Mayfield among other investors. Qualcomm acquired Nuvia in 2021 and its core technology became the Qualcomm Oryon CPU. Nuvia has no independent developer, API, or product surface today; its former site nuviainc.com now redirects to qualcomm.com. Retained in the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio identity record rather than an active API provider.

providers.name: Olix
providers.description: Olix (OLIX Computing) is a stealth-stage hardware company building a new computing architecture that integrates SRAM with photonics to address the computational bottlenecks of large-scale AI deployment. The company positions its SRAM-plus-photonics design to surpass HBM-based architectures on throughput-per-megawatt and total cost of ownership while outperforming silicon-only alternatives on speed and latency as frontier-model demand compounds faster than today's infrastructure can scale. Backed by Creandum, Olix is currently pre-product and hiring across the US and UK; it publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or documentation at this time. This profile was surfaced as a Creandum portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead.

providers.name: oneNav
providers.description: oneNav is a fabless GNSS (Global Navigation Satellite System) semiconductor company building the next generation of mobile positioning. Its L5-direct receiver acquires and tracks on the modern L5 satellite band without legacy L1 aiding, delivering higher location accuracy in urban canyons and far greater resilience to GPS jamming and spoofing, in half the RF size, power and cost of hybrid L1+L5 solutions. Founded in 2019 (Steve Poizner, Paul McBurney) with offices in Sunnyvale, CA and Tampere, Finland, oneNav targets smartphones, wearables, IoT trackers, defense and emergency services. It is backed by GV, Norwest Venture Partners and GSR Ventures. oneNav is a hardware/silicon company and does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal.

providers.name: Oratomic
providers.description: Oratomic is a Pasadena, California quantum computing company where leading researchers from Caltech and Harvard are building utility-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computers with neutral atoms and optical systems. Launched from stealth in March 2026, the company advances quantum error correction with the aim of making practical, cryptographically relevant quantum computation possible with far fewer qubits than previously believed (on the order of ~10,000 reconfigurable atomic qubits rather than millions). Oratomic is a deep-tech hardware and research organization; at this time it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or programmatic access surface.

providers.name: Origami Robotics
providers.description: Origami Robotics is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) hardware startup based in Millbrae, California building advanced robotic hands designed specifically for machine learning and general-purpose robotic manipulation. The company designs a high-degrees-of-freedom hand with in-joint motors, co-designed with a matching data-collection glove that eliminates the embodiment gap between human and robot manipulation so that real-world training data transfers directly to deployed robots. Its focus areas include force transparency, avoiding the sim-to-real problems of high-ratio gearboxes, and scaling real-world manipulation data by deploying devices "in the wild." Origami Robotics targets industrial automation in manufacturing and logistics and has sold hands to Physical AI research labs including Amazon. Origami Robotics is a hardware and robotics company; as of this profile it publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or machine-readable interface.

providers.name: PCH International
providers.description: PCH International (pchintl.com) is a global supply chain solutions provider that helps brands bring innovative physical products to market across the entire product lifecycle. Its services span new product introduction (NPI) planning, design and development, validation and manufacturing (EVT/DVT/PVT), and post-production revenue optimization, plus global logistics, direct-to-consumer (D2C) transformation, supply-chain financing, and sustainability programs. PCH serves personal care and beauty, health and fitness, home and lifestyle, accessories, audio and entertainment, and smart retail sectors. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners, PCH is a B2B services provider with no public developer API or platform at this time.

providers.name: Peel
providers.description: Peel Technologies Inc (peel.com) is a Redpoint Ventures-backed consumer technology company known for the Peel Smart Remote mobile app, which turned smartphones into universal remote controls for TVs, set-top boxes, and home-entertainment devices with a TV guide and content discovery layer. As of this enrichment pass the peel.com website resolves over HTTPS but serves only a single-logo placeholder page (frameset redirecting to an S3-hosted logo), indicating the company is dormant. No public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI, SDKs, or /.well-known discovery surface was found; developer/api/docs subdomains do not resolve.

providers.name: Performance Drone Works
providers.description: Performance Drone Works is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of lux-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: defense. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Periodic Labs
providers.description: Periodic Labs builds AI scientists and autonomous laboratories to accelerate discovery in the physical sciences. Its systems formulate hypotheses, run real-world experiments in self-driving labs, and learn from the results, targeting materials design and the search for higher-temperature superconductors, and helping industrial partners such as semiconductor manufacturers analyze experimental data to iterate faster. The company is backed by Accel, Bain Capital Ventures, Lightspeed Venture Partners and SV Angel. As of this profile Periodic Labs publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation surface; this record captures its identity for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: petkit
providers.description: PetKit is a consumer smart pet-technology company that designs and sells connected pet-care hardware — automated feeders, smart water fountains, self-cleaning litter boxes, cameras, and health-monitoring accessories — paired with the PetKit mobile app that controls the devices over the cloud. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of the venture firm qiming and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass, PetKit publishes no dedicated first-party developer portal or public API; petkit.com is operated as a Shopify storefront, so the only machine discoverable surface on the domain is Shopify's Customer Account OAuth/OIDC discovery documents. Third-party (community, reverse-engineered) integrations exist for the mobile-app backend but there is no officially documented API.

providers.name: Piestro
providers.description: Piestro was a Los Angeles-area food-robotics company that built a fully enclosed, automated pizza-making vending machine — an unattended kiosk that pressed, sauced, topped, baked, cut and boxed an artisanal pizza in roughly three minutes, sold both as direct-to-consumer placements and as a white-label unit for existing pizza brands. Founded by Massimo Noja De Marco and incubated by Wavemaker Labs (since rebranded Vebu Labs), it raised roughly $11.7M from equity-crowdfunding investors, largely via StartEngine, and piloted units with partners including Capriotti's and 800 Degrees Go. Piestro shut down in January 2025 without shipping a production unit. It is a hardware and food-service company, not a software vendor: it never ran a developer program, and no public API, SDK, webhook, developer portal or machine-readable contract of any kind was ever published. This profile records that absence rather than inventing a surface.

providers.name: Pixelworks
providers.description: Pixelworks, Inc. (NASDAQ: PXLW) is a San Jose, California based semiconductor company founded in 1997 that designs video and pixel processing integrated circuits and software for digital video applications. Its technology spans digital displays, mobile devices, projection systems, digital signage, and video conferencing and surveillance, including the Iris visual processing line and TrueCut Motion cinematic-quality video platform. Pixelworks sells chips and IP to device makers rather than operating a public developer API platform; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company discovery and coverage tracking.

providers.name: Pliant Technology
providers.description: Pliant Technology, Inc. was a data-center storage company that pioneered the introduction of high-performance enterprise solid-state drives (SSDs) into mission-critical data-center environments. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, the company was acquired by SanDisk in 2011 and its product line was folded into SanDisk's enterprise storage solutions. The company operated as a hardware/semiconductor storage vendor and published no public developer API, SDK, or programmatic developer surface; its former domain now redirects to SanDisk. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead record with no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Porotech
providers.description: Porotech (Poro Technologies Ltd) is a Cambridge University deep-tech spinout, founded in 2018 by Dr. Tongtong Zhu, Dr. Yingjun Liu, and Professor Rachel Oliver, that develops gallium nitride (GaN) semiconductor materials and MicroLED display technology. Its proprietary PoroGaN porous-InGaN epitaxy enables full-color MicroLED production on 4-to-12-inch wafers using a single material system, and its Dynamic Pixel Tuning (DPT) technology generates any visible color from a single LED chip. Porotech supplies epitaxy, micro displays, and light-engine products for AR/VR/MR applications, and has established mass-production partnerships with Foxconn, PSMC (Powerchip), and GIS. The company is backed by Speedinvest. Porotech is a hardware and semiconductor manufacturer and publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or event/streaming surface; this record is maintained for company-level discovery within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: PriceBaba
providers.description: PriceBaba is an India-based consumer price-comparison and gadget research platform, founded in 2012 and headquartered in Mumbai. It helps shoppers compare mobile phones, consumer electronics and other gadgets by aggregating specifications, expert and user reviews, and prices across online and offline local retail stores, so buyers can find the best available deal near them. PriceBaba is backed by 500 Global (formerly 500 Startups). No public developer program or API surface was discoverable during this enrichment pass. The website is served behind Cloudflare and blocks automated access, and no api.pricebaba.com host resolves.

providers.name: prmeasure
providers.description: prmeasure (Precision Measurement & Control, 精实测控) is a Zhuhai, China based high-tech enterprise specializing in measurement, control, and artificial intelligence technologies for flexible manufacturing. The company builds industrial-grade testing and control equipment for the consumer electronics, automotive, and home-appliance industries, and offers consumer-level customized production through a C2M (customer-to-manufacturer) model. Its WowNow platform (iwownow.com) provides creative prototyping tools and flexible manufacturing equipment for individuals. prmeasure was surfaced as a portfolio company of the Qiming Venture Partners investment graph and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a corporate marketing website only, with no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Pure Watercraft
providers.description: Pure Watercraft was a Seattle, Washington electric marine propulsion company founded in 2011 by Andy Rebele. It built electric outboard motors marketed as drop-in replacements for 20 to 50 horsepower gas engines, along with lithium-ion battery packs, chargers and Wi-Fi throttle controls, plus a consumer companion mobile app that pulled trip history and telemetry off the outboard over Bluetooth and pushed firmware updates to it. General Motors took a reported 25 percent stake in 2021. The company wound down and sold its assets in 2024, with the outboard line acquired by Raider Outboards and other assets going to a Seattle electric boat club. purewatercraft.com and the former companion-app host app.purewatercraft.com both now 301 to www.pureoutboards.com, the Pure Electric Outboard storefront operated by the acquirer. Pure Watercraft never published a public developer program, API reference, SDK, or machine-readable API contract; its telemetry cloud was private to its own mobile app.

providers.name: Quantum Effect Dev
providers.description: Quantum Effect Devices (QED, originally Quantum Effect Design) was a fabless semiconductor company founded in 1991 by former MIPS Computer Systems managers Tom Riordan, Earl Killian, and Ray Kunita. QED designed MIPS-based 32- and 64-bit embedded RISC microprocessors (the RM5200 and RM7000 families) for networking and communications systems including routers, switches, and optical transport equipment. The company completed an IPO in 2000 and was acquired the same year by PMC-Sierra for approximately $2.3 billion. It has no independent operations, developer platform, or API surface today; the former corporate site (qedinc.com) is defunct. This record was surfaced as a Lightspeed Venture Partners portfolio company and is retained as a historical/no-API-surface entry.

providers.name: Quantum Motion
providers.description: Quantum Motion is a UK-based full-stack quantum computing company building scalable, fault-tolerant quantum computers using silicon (CMOS) technology, the same manufacturing process used for conventional microchips. Spun out of University College London and the University of Oxford, the company develops qubit control hardware, cryogenic electronics, and quantum architecture aimed at manufacturing quantum processors at scale. It is a research- and hardware-focused company rather than an API or developer-platform provider; this profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass no public developer API, documentation portal, or SDK surface could be verified (the corporate site sits behind bot-challenge protection and web search was unavailable), so the profile remains identity-only.

providers.name: Quirky
providers.description: Quirky was a crowdsourced consumer-product invention platform (founded by Ben Kaufman) that let inventors submit ideas the community helped design, manufacture and sell; it was backed by a16z among others. The company filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2015. As of this enrichment pass the quirky.com domain is a parked "domain name is for sale" page with no operating product, developer portal, or API surface. This profile is retained as a defunct a16z portfolio-company lead; no API artifacts exist to enrich.

providers.name: Remora
providers.description: Remora is a carbon-capture startup (legally Echeneidae Inc.) founded in 2020 and based in Wixom, Michigan, that retrofits semi-trucks and locomotives with zero-backpressure devices which extract and purify up to 90 percent of the CO2 from vehicle exhaust while cutting other pollutants. The company then sells the captured, purified carbon dioxide and shares the resulting revenue with the transportation operators it partners with. Remora is a hardware and climate-technology business with no public API or developer platform; this profile tracks it as an API Evangelist network company for portfolio and discovery purposes.

providers.name: Resonado Labs
providers.description: Resonado Labs is a high-velocity innovation and hardware development lab focused on improving the acoustic performance of the next generation of audio products through speaker hardware design and engineering. Backed by 500 Global, the company designs novel loudspeaker and transducer technology for consumer electronics and audio OEMs. Resonado Labs is a hardware and acoustics company; it publishes a marketing website but does not currently expose a public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Rev1
providers.description: Rev1 (REV1, Inc.) is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) startup building an AI-powered platform that automatically converts 3D CAD models into fully annotated, production-ready 2D manufacturing drawings in minutes instead of hours. The software applies ASME Y14.5-2018 geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T) standards, captures design intent, and lets mechanical engineers review the design rationale before sharing with manufacturers, reportedly recovering roughly 25% of engineering time at hardware companies across robotics, aerospace, automotive, medical devices, and consumer electronics. As of this enrichment pass the company exposes only a marketing site and a demo-request flow — there is no public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation surface to catalog.

providers.name: Reveal Imaging
providers.description: Reveal Imaging (Reveal Imaging Technologies) is a security-screening hardware company known for CT-based explosives-detection and checkpoint screening systems for aviation and critical infrastructure. Founded around 2002 and backed by General Catalyst since 2003, the company was acquired into SAIC and its detection business is now part of Leidos. It is a physical-security systems provider, not an API provider - enrichment found no public developer portal, API, developer documentation, or machine-readable specification hosted under its own name (its former revealimaging.com domain now serves Leidos, and the General Catalyst portfolio entry points to saic.com).

providers.name: Revolv
providers.description: Revolv was a smart-home company that built a connected home hub and mobile application to unify control of disparate smart-home devices and wireless protocols from a single app. The company was acquired by Nest (Google) and the Revolv hub and service were subsequently discontinued; owners of purchased Revolv hubs were directed to Nest support for refunds through a deadline of October 31, 2018. This API Evangelist profile is retained as a historical portfolio record. The company publishes no active API, developer portal, SDKs, or public developer surface, so this entry carries only a domain-security probe of its remaining web presence.

providers.name: Ricursive
providers.description: Ricursive (Ricursive Intelligence) is a frontier AI lab building self-improving systems, starting with chip design. The company combines modern AI methods with semiconductor and electronic design automation (EDA) workflows to create a feedback loop between AI systems and the hardware that runs them. It was founded by veterans from Google DeepMind, Anthropic, and NVIDIA (including researchers behind AlphaChip) and is backed by leading investors. As of this profile Ricursive publishes a public marketing and careers site but no public API, SDK, developer documentation, or developer product surface — so there is no API artifact to harvest. This company profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for discovery and monitoring.

providers.name: Ricursive Intelligence
providers.description: Ricursive Intelligence is a frontier AI laboratory building self-improving systems to reinvent chip design, closing the loop between artificial intelligence and the hardware that powers it. Founded by researchers behind work such as AlphaChip (Nature 2021), RL-CCD (DAC Best Paper 2023), Insta (DAC Best Paper 2025), and C3PO (ASP-DAC Best Paper 2026), and contributors to major AI models and accelerators (Gemini, Claude, Grok, TPUs), the company raised $335M from Sequoia, Lightspeed, DST Global, and NVentures. As of this profile the company operates as a research lab with a public marketing site and careers page but no publicly documented developer API, SDKs, or developer portal.

providers.name: Riide
providers.description: Riide manufactures connected electric bicycles combining a street-legal 500W ebike (the Riide 2) with built-in GPS tracking, 4G cellular connectivity, remote lock/disable theft prevention, and a removable battery with state-of-charge monitoring. The company pairs hardware with a mobile app and connected-vehicle services. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; as of this pass the public site is a consumer product/pre-order page ("coming soon") with no documented developer, API, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Rise Robotics
providers.description: RISE Robotics develops industrial linear-actuation technology designed to replace traditional hydraulic systems. Its flagship Beltdraulic Cylinder is a fluid-free hydraulic alternative delivering faster actuation, higher reliability, no fire hazard, and fuel-source flexibility for large-scale industrial applications. The company builds actuation products (Beltdraulic Cylinder, Railgate, SuperJammer, CLD) for Tier 1 suppliers, OEMs, and the US Department of Defense. RISE Robotics is a hardware and heavy-equipment company backed by Techstars; it publishes no developer API, SDK, or developer portal, so this API Evangelist profile captures identity and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Rohm and Haas
providers.description: Rohm and Haas Company was an American specialty chemicals manufacturer founded in 1909 and headquartered in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The company produced electronic materials, specialty polymers, adhesives, coatings, paints, and process chemicals. On April 1, 2009, Rohm and Haas was acquired by The Dow Chemical Company for approximately $18.8 billion in cash and stock. The Rohm and Haas brand has since been largely retired and its product lines, technologies, and businesses have been integrated into Dow (now Dow Inc., NYSE: DOW). Some legacy product brands persist under Dow but the standalone company no longer exists.

providers.name: S3 Graphics
providers.description: S3 Graphics, Inc. is a legacy graphics, video, and multimedia accelerator company known for its GPU architectures (Savage, Chrome and DeltaChrome, plus the earlier ViRGE and Trio chipsets) and its display drivers. Originally founded as S3 Incorporated in 1989, the graphics business later operated as S3 Graphics under VIA and HTC ownership. Its public web presence is a legacy marketing and driver-download site (still Flash/Ruffle based); it exposes no modern web API, SDK, or developer platform. The historical "Developers" area was a hardware developer-relations channel offering GPU sample cards during the DeltaChrome era, not a programmatic API.

providers.name: Sabi
providers.description: Sabi ("Just Think") presents itself at sabi.com as a consumer neural-interface company building a wearable (a beanie) that transforms a wearer's thoughts directly into text — "no typing, no voice, just think." As of this enrichment pass the company operates a single marketing landing page with no public developer portal, API, documentation, SDK, changelog, or status surface; the only outbound links are its social accounts on X and Instagram. Added to the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio stub lead; there is currently no API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Samsara Eco
providers.description: Samsara Eco is an Australian climate-technology company pioneering enzymatic recycling, a process that uses engineered enzymes to break plastics and synthetic textiles down into their molecular building blocks so they can be infinitely remade into new materials with no loss of quality. Spun out of the Australian National University, the company recovers nylon and polyester from mixed and coloured textile and plastic waste and partners with global brands to build a circular materials supply chain. It is a materials-science and biotech company rather than an API provider, and has no public developer, API, or technical integration surface at this time.

providers.name: Sandforce
providers.description: SandForce was a fabless semiconductor company (Canaan Partners-backed) that designed flash memory / SSD controller processors. It was acquired by LSI Corporation in 2012 and its flash-controller business was subsequently folded into Seagate; the sandforce.com domain now redirects to seagate.com. As a defunct, absorbed brand it operates no independent website, developer portal, API, SDK, or documentation, so there is no live API surface to enrich. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a canaan-partners portfolio lead; retained as a historical/company record.

providers.name: SGI (Silicon Graphics)
providers.description: SGI, or Silicon Graphics, was a workstation, server, supercomputing, and computer-graphics company founded in 1982 and one of Mayfield's landmark early portfolio companies. It pioneered high-performance 3D graphics hardware, the IRIX operating system, and the OpenGL API. The independent company was acquired by Rackable Systems in 2009 (which adopted the SGI name) and that business was in turn acquired by Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) in 2016. There is no longer an independent SGI developer program or public API surface; the historic sgi.com domain now redirects to HPE's high-performance-computing product line. This profile is retained as a historic Mayfield portfolio record; it is not an active API provider.

providers.name: Shellworks
providers.description: Shellworks is a materials-science company that produces VIVOMER, a home-compostable, biodegradable alternative to conventional plastic made through a natural fermentation process from agricultural waste. VIVOMER runs on standard plastic-manufacturing equipment, is certified for food contact (FDA and EU 10/2011), and biodegrades without leaving microplastics or toxic residue. Shellworks supplies these sustainable packaging materials to consumer brands across the UK, EU, and US. Backed by Version One Ventures, the company was surfaced as a portfolio lead and added to the API Evangelist network. It is a B2B climate / materials supplier with no public API, developer portal, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Sibeam
providers.description: SiBEAM, Inc. was a fabless semiconductor company that pioneered 60GHz millimeter-wave (mmWave) wireless technology and helped drive the WirelessHD standard for uncompressed wireless HD video and multi-gigabit data links. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lux Capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment (sector: semiconductors). The enrichment pass found no independent public surface: SiBEAM was acquired by Silicon Image in 2011, and Silicon Image was in turn acquired by Lattice Semiconductor in 2015, so there is no live SiBEAM website, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Silicon Clocks
providers.description: Silicon Clocks is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of lux-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: semiconductors. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Silicon Optix
providers.description: Silicon Optix Inc. was a fabless semiconductor company that designed image- and video-processing chips, best known for its Realta HQV (Hollywood Quality Video) processor for high-definition video scaling, de-interlacing, and noise reduction, and for the Teranex line of professional video processors. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners, it was acquired by Integrated Device Technology (IDT) in 2008 (IDT was subsequently acquired by Renesas). The company operated as a hardware/chip vendor and did not publish a public developer API; its historical primary domain (siliconoptix.com) no longer resolves. This profile is retained as a network stub with no live API surface.

providers.name: Singularity
providers.description: Singularity (Singularity Defense Corp) is a defense-technology company building low-cost, mass-producible air-defense and counter-weapon systems to protect warfighters and civilians from drones and cheap aerial munitions. Founded by engineers from SpaceX, Tesla, and Anduril alongside operators who have deployed air defenses in combat, the company emerged from stealth in July 2026 with an $80M Series A at a $400M valuation led by Khosla Ventures and Felicis, with Menlo Ventures, NEA, Y Combinator, Harpoon Ventures, and others participating. It emphasizes in-house manufacturing of major subsystems combined with commercial-volume components for rapid production and field deployment, including active conflict zones. Singularity is a hardware defense company and does not publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs. This profile was surfaced as a Menlo Ventures portfolio lead and enriched with verified company identity by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Singularity Defense
providers.description: Singularity Defense Corp (operating on singularityus.com) is a defense-technology company building affordable, scalable counter-weapon air defense systems that protect warfighters and civilians from drones and low-cost, mass-produced munitions. Led by CEO Jack Oswald with COO Shail Giroux, the company is backed by Khosla Ventures, New Enterprise Associates, Andreessen Horowitz, Y Combinator, Menlo Ventures, and Felicis. It ships physical air-defense hardware and publishes no public API, developer portal, or developer documentation. Added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead; this enrichment pass confirmed the company has no public API surface.

providers.name: SIQ Basketball
providers.description: SIQ Basketball is a Techstars-backed sports-technology company that builds a FIBA-approved, sensor-embedded smart basketball and companion mobile app that automatically tracks shooting mechanics, makes and misses, shot arc and other performance data to coach players. Its technology is now marketed under the Spalding brand as the Spalding TF DNA Smart Basketball, sold with an app subscription. The company operates as a direct-to-consumer product and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its network identity and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Snowcap Compute
providers.description: Snowcap Compute is building the world's first commercial superconducting computing platform, operating at 4.5 Kelvin to deliver breakthrough energy efficiency and performance for AI and data-center workloads. Launched in June 2025 with $23 million in seed funding led by Playground Global, the company is developing superconducting chips and systems aimed at the next era of AI and quantum-adjacent compute. As a hardware and deep-tech company it publishes a marketing and careers presence but no public API, developer portal, or SDK at this time.

providers.name: supermag
providers.description: Suzhou Supermag Intelligent Technology Co., Ltd. is a Chinese deep-tech manufacturer specializing in magnetic levitation (maglev) motion and fluid-handling systems. Its product lines include SCM maglev wafer turntables for ultra-clean semiconductor rotation, SCP maglev pumps for contamination-free fluid transport, MSS maglev stirring systems for low-shear mixing, and SCT maglev turbomolecular pumps for high-vacuum applications, serving the semiconductor, biopharmaceutical, chemical, and energy industries. Backed by Qiming Venture Partners, the company markets physical industrial hardware and publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface at this time.

providers.name: Syenta
providers.description: Syenta is an Australian deep-tech semiconductor company (founded 2022, spun out of the Australian National University, with teams across Australia, Europe and the United States) building manufacturing equipment for advanced chip packaging. Its proprietary Localized Electrochemical Manufacturing (LEM) technology combines material deposition and 3D patterning in a single step to produce sub-micron High-Resolution Interconnects on large (>1000 mm2) packages, targeting the chip-to-chip bandwidth bottleneck in AI computing; its Achyon production tool delivers wafer-level system integration at high density. Backed by Playground Global and Australia's National Reconstruction Fund (Series A), Syenta is a hardware / fabrication-equipment maker and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Symmorphix
providers.description: Symmorphix, Inc. was a materials-science company founded in 1998 and based in Sunnyvale, California, that developed and manufactured advanced amorphous dielectric and optical thin films for the optical-networking and communications industries. Its core technology was a proprietary wide-area physical vapor deposition (PVD) process performed at low temperatures, enabling deposition of a broad range of material compositions onto metal, ceramic, and polymer substrates for use as physical barriers, dielectric layers, and optical layers. The company was venture-backed by Battery Ventures and Crescendo Ventures and was acquired by Springworks on February 6, 2004. It is a defunct hardware/materials company with no public API, developer portal, or software developer surface, and is retained in the API Evangelist network only as a historical portfolio-lead record.

providers.name: Synplicity
providers.description: Synplicity, Inc. was a supplier of software for the design of programmable logic devices (FPGAs, PLDs and CPLDs) used in communications, military/aerospace, consumer, semiconductor and computer systems. Its tools provided logic synthesis, physical synthesis, ASIC prototyping and verification for FPGA and DSP designers (Synplify, Synplify Pro, Identify). Synplicity was acquired by Synopsys for approximately $227 million, with the transaction completed on 2008-05-15, and no longer operates as an independent company. The legacy domain synplicity.com now 301-redirects to synopsys.com. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners; it has no independent public API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Talking Computers
providers.description: Talking Computers is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) startup building Facility, described as "The Workplace for AI" and delivering autonomous organizations for enterprises. The company deploys fleets of AI Infrastructure Engineers that collaborate over week-long time horizons, run hundreds of experiments in parallel, and learn from them to optimize customers' training and inference infrastructure to their specific workloads. Talking Computers reports partnering with companies to speed up GPU kernels to 6x state-of-the-art and to cut the latency of voice models to roughly half that of competitors. As of enrichment, the company is an early-stage two-person team and publishes only a marketing presence at talkingcomputers.ai (a single-page application); it exposes no public API, OpenAPI definition, developer portal, documentation, or SDKs. This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio lead and enriched from verified public sources.

providers.name: Target Arm
providers.description: Target Arm is a robotics company building systems to autonomously launch and recover drones from moving vehicles without stopping. Its Ralar robotic arm captures drones mid-air, recharges them, and relaunches them, while TRACKR sensor-fusion, TurboFly autopilot, and Maestro mission-control software coordinate drone fleets across commercial delivery, first-responder, agriculture, energy-inspection, and defense/ISR use cases. A Techstars-backed hardware startup with no public API or developer program at this time; this network profile captures identity and infrastructure signals only.

providers.name: Tattvam
providers.description: Tattvam AI (Tattvam Labs) is an early-stage, Seedcamp-backed deep-tech startup building the intelligence layer of chip design, applying artificial intelligence to semiconductor and electronic design automation (EDA) workflows. As of this profile the company operates a single marketing landing page at tattvamlabs.ai (a Vercel-hosted React single-page app) with no public API, developer documentation, or SDKs; it is in a pre-product, team-building stage. Contact hello@tattvamlabs.ai.

providers.name: Tempo Automation
providers.description: Tempo Automation is a San Francisco-based software-automated printed circuit board assembly (PCBA) manufacturer, founded in 2013 and formerly publicly traded on Nasdaq as TMPO. Its software-driven manufacturing platform was built to take complex electronics from design to physical prototype and new product introduction in as little as a few days, serving customers in aerospace, medical technology, semiconductor, industrial, and automotive. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Lux Capital and Uncork Capital. The company does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; its current website is a single-page placeholder offering on-demand circuit board manufacturing through a contact form.

providers.name: Tenet Industries
providers.description: Tenet Industries is a Swedish defense-technology startup founded in 2026 by Hugo Frisk, Fabian Andersson, and Emil Falk (students from KTH Royal Institute of Technology and the Stockholm School of Economics) building low-cost, mass-producible defense systems. Applying design-for-manufacturing and first-principles engineering, the company starts with strike/attack drones — a kamikaze quadcopter that assembles in two minutes with roughly half the parts of comparable systems — and extends the same hardware/software platform to loitering munitions, jammers, radars, and missile systems. Backed by Y Combinator ($500K). As a defense hardware manufacturer, Tenet Industries currently publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or event surface; this profile is maintained as a company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Terra Industries
providers.description: Terra Industries is a Nigeria-based defense-technology company, positioning itself as Africa's first defense prime, that designs, manufactures, and deploys autonomous multi-domain security systems across air, land, and eventually sea. Founded in 2024 by Nathan Nwachuku and Maxwell Maduka, the company builds ArtemisOS (an AI-powered operating system for infrastructure security), the Archer long-range VTOL surveillance drone, the Iroko modular UAV, the Duma autonomous unmanned ground vehicle, and the Kallon solar-powered AI sentry tower to monitor, detect, and respond to threats such as terrorism, sabotage, and armed attacks on critical infrastructure including hydropower plants, mines, and power assets. Terra raised $11.75M led by 8VC in January 2026. As a hardware and defense-systems manufacturer it publishes no public API, developer portal, or technical documentation surface; this profile is maintained as a company/provider record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: TopXGun
providers.description: TopXGun (Nanjing TopXGun Robotics / 拓攻机器人) is a Chinese unmanned aerial vehicle manufacturer specializing in the research, development, and production of agricultural spray drones, heavy-lift delivery drones, industrial and cleaning drones, firefighting and emergency UAVs, tethered drones, eVTOL and large unmanned aircraft, and the professional flight-control and avionics hardware, payload equipment, and software systems that power them. Its whole-aircraft capability spans all airspace below 5,000 meters and payloads up to 1.5 tons across core industries, and it offers ODM/OEM customization and education support. Its overseas agricultural line is marketed as TopXGun Agriculture (topxgunag.com) with CE, FCC, RoHS, and KC certifications. Surfaced as a portfolio company of DCM Ventures. No public web API, SDK, or developer portal was found during enrichment; this is a hardware manufacturer.

providers.name: Trocafone
providers.description: Trocafone is a Brazilian e-commerce company specializing in refurbished and pre-owned smartphones and consumer electronics sold with warranty. Operating primarily in Brazil on the VTEX commerce platform, it runs a consumer marketplace for certified semi-new iPhones, Samsung, Motorola and other devices, a trade-in program ("Venda seu aparelho") that buys used devices from consumers, and a Reparofone device-repair service. Backed by 500 Global, the company is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: TruckLabs
providers.description: TruckLabs built TruckWings, an automated tractor-mounted aerodynamic device that closes the gap between the tractor and trailer to reduce aerodynamic drag, cutting fuel consumption by a proven 3-6% and eliminating roughly 7-10 metric tons of CO2 per truck each year with an 18-24 month payback. The device deploys automatically at highway speed and retracts below it, reduces buffeting and trailer sway in crosswinds, and installs on both new builds and retrofits in about two hours. TruckLabs was acquired by ConMet, and trucklabs.com now redirects to the ConMet TruckWings product line. As a hardware fuel-efficiency company, TruckLabs exposes no public developer API, SDK, or well-known discovery surface; this profile captures its identity and probed domain-security posture. Backed by Uncork Capital.

providers.name: uBEAM
providers.description: uBeam was an ultrasonic wireless power startup founded in 2011 by Meredith Perry and headquartered in Marina del Rey, California. It raised roughly $26 million from Andreessen Horowitz, Upfront Ventures, Founders Fund, Mark Cuban, and Marissa Mayer to charge devices over the air using 45-75 kHz phased-array ultrasound. The company rebranded as SonicEnergy in December 2018 and went defunct on February 5, 2024, without shipping a commercial product. It published no developer APIs, SDKs, or documentation, and both ubeam.com and sonicenergy.com are now parked domains.

providers.name: Vertical Circuits
providers.description: Vertical Circuits, Inc. (VCI) was a semiconductor company based in Scotts Valley, California, supplying high-density semiconductor memories and die-level vertical-interconnect packaging technology. Its patented ViP (vertical interconnect pillar) process stacked die to bridge wire-bond product solutions and through-silicon-via (TSV) technology, serving computer, telecom, consumer-electronics, aerospace, and military customers. The company's die-stacking IP and technology were acquired by Invensas/Tessera around 2013. Vertical Circuits is a hardware and semiconductor-IP company with no public web API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface; it was surfaced as a Battery Ventures portfolio lead and enriched to record that it has no API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Vexata
providers.description: Vexata was an all-flash, NVMe-based enterprise storage startup headquartered in Santa Clara, California, known for its Vexata Active Data Fabric software and VX-100 scale-out storage arrays aimed at high-performance database and analytics workloads. The company was backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and was acquired by StorCentric in 2019; StorCentric subsequently filed for bankruptcy in 2022. As of this enrichment pass the vexata.com domain no longer belongs to the company and redirects to an unrelated business (farmhousela.com), the api./developer./docs. subdomains do not resolve, and no developer portal, documentation, SDK, or API surface could be found. This profile is retained as a historical/defunct company record.

providers.name: Vue
providers.description: Vue (Vue Technology) was an item-level RFID hardware and software company based in Lake Forest, California, backed by Canaan Partners at Series A. Its product family combined RFID readpoints and networking devices with a software platform for real-time, item-level inventory monitoring and tracking, with notable retail rollouts including American Apparel. Tyco's Sensormatic Electronics acquired Vue Technology in October 2008 for approximately $43M, so the company no longer operates as an independent entity. It surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a Canaan Partners portfolio lead; enrichment finds no active developer portal, public API, or first-party artifacts to catalog.

providers.name: Weft
providers.description: Weft was a Burlington, Vermont based supply-chain logistics startup, founded by Marc Held around 2013-2014, that combined hardware sensors and software to track the shipping of physical goods worldwide in real time. It raised a seed round of under $1M led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Data Elite, with plans for a $5M Series A. The company was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the company appears defunct: no live corporate website, no developer portal, and no public API surface could be found. Candidate domains were probed and none host an active product (weft.com refused connection, weft.io does not resolve, weft.ai is a parked domain listed for sale).

providers.name: Yunyinggu (Viewtrix Technology)
providers.description: Yunyinggu Technology (云英谷科技), which rebranded as Viewtrix Technology, is a Shenzhen-based fabless semiconductor company founded in 2012 that designs AMOLED display driver integrated circuits (DDIC) and color-rendering display solutions for smartphones and other devices. By 2024 sales volume it was the largest AMOLED display driver chip supplier in mainland China and the fifth-largest globally, with R&D and operations across Shenzhen, Shanghai, Beijing, and Hong Kong. Backed by Qiming Venture Partners (Series C and extension), Huawei, and Xiaomi, the company completed a Hong Kong IPO. It is a hardware/semiconductor business and publishes no public developer API surface; this profile is retained as a network identity record. The original yunyinggu.com domain no longer resolves and viewtrix.com is a parked domain-for-sale listing.

providers.name: ZeroMark
providers.description: ZeroMark is a defense-technology company building an AI-powered targeting system for counter-drone (counter-UAS) defense. Its bolt-on hardware and software components attach to existing weapons, platforms, and sensing systems to detect, track, and neutralize small drone threats in milliseconds while minimizing collateral damage. The product line spans Apex (AI aim-assist for shoulder-mounted rifles), Vanguard (a precision system for turret-mounted and vehicle platforms effective against Group 1-3 drones), and Nexus (a command-and-control software layer that integrates deployments into shared targeting and battlespace-awareness environments). ZeroMark was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, SDK, developer documentation, or open-source presence; its Nexus C2 integration is delivered through defense procurement rather than a public developer program.

providers.name: Zibra Labs
providers.description: Zibra Labs is a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) startup building distributed compute infrastructure for AI workloads at scale. The platform gives teams access to the cheapest CPUs and GPUs across hyperscalers and neoclouds, orchestrating clusters of 100 to 50,000 mixed hardware nodes with sub-50ms task-dispatch overhead and millions of parallel tasks on spot instances across regions. Target workloads include quantitative-trading backtesting and parameter sweeps, AI post-training and reinforcement-learning pipelines, multi-modal data processing, batch and high-volume inference, and long-horizon agentic workflows. The founding team previously built three LinkedIn databases (Venice, Liquid, Espresso) and were tech leads on the open-source Ray compute framework. As of this profile Zibra Labs publishes only a corporate marketing site; no public API, developer documentation, or SDKs are available yet.

providers.name: Zymergen
providers.description: Zymergen was a synthetic-biology and bio-manufacturing company founded in 2013 in Emeryville, California, that used machine learning and automation to engineer microbes and discover novel bio-based materials and molecules. It went public on NASDAQ in 2021 and was acquired by Ginkgo Bioworks in October 2022; the zymergen.com domain now 301-redirects to Ginkgo Bioworks. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC, Kindred Ventures, and Obvious Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. Enrichment found no public developer portal, API, documentation, or event surface — the company has no independent API footprint following the acquisition. This profile is retained as a portfolio/history record.

providers.name: Unconventional AI
providers.description: Unconventional AI (unconv.ai) is rethinking the foundations of the computer to optimize energy efficiency for AI, working to bring biology-scale efficiency to artificial intelligence through analog, dynamical-system hardware co-evolved with neural software. Founded by experts in AI systems, analog circuits, computing theory, and neuroscience, and backed by Felicis, the company publishes research including the Un-0 image-generation model built on coupled Kuramoto oscillators and an instruction set architecture for dynamical-system hardware, but does not yet publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Entegris
providers.description: Entegris is a global supplier of advanced materials and process solutions for the semiconductor and other high-technology industries. The company develops and manufactures specialty chemicals, gases, filtration and purification systems, advanced materials handling, and process control products. No public developer API or developer portal has been identified at the corporate level; technical integration is typically supported through sales engineering, the supplier portal, and product documentation.

providers.name: Occamnetworks
providers.description: Occam Networks was a broadband access equipment vendor that developed and marketed systems enabling telecommunications carriers to profitably deliver emerging voice, video, and high-speed data (triple-play) services over copper and fiber, including its BLC 6000 access platform and ONT/ONU customer-premises hardware. The company was acquired by Calix in early 2011 and no longer operates independently. The occamnetworks.com domain currently serves an archived circa-2010 marketing site (products, solutions, support, news, whitepapers) with no developer program, API, SDK, or documentation surface. Enrichment found no API artifacts to harvest.

providers.name: Primesense
providers.description: PrimeSense was an Israeli fabless semiconductor and 3D-sensing company, best known for co-developing the depth-sensing technology behind Microsoft's Kinect and for sponsoring the open-source OpenNI (Open Natural Interaction) framework and its NiTE middleware for skeleton tracking and gesture recognition. The company shipped the PrimeSensor reference design and PS1080 system-on-chip for structured-light depth cameras. Apple acquired PrimeSense in November 2013 for roughly $360M; the OpenNI project and openni.org were subsequently wound down (openni.org now redirects to apple.com) and the company's developer program, website, and API/docs hosts are no longer online. Only legacy Apache-2.0 source repositories (the OpenNI sensor driver and NiTE controls) remain public on GitHub. There is no live web/REST API surface for PrimeSense.

providers.name: Astral Systems
providers.description: Astral Systems is a fusion-technology company based in Bristol, United Kingdom, developing Multi-State Fusion (MSF) reactors that produce high-flux neutron sources on demand. Co-founded by Talmon Firestone (CEO) and Dr. Tom Wallace-Smith (CTO), the company applies compact, modular fusion to near-term problems: large-scale medical isotope production to address the global isotope shortage affecting cancer diagnosis and treatment, spent fission fuel analysis, neutronics research, industrial neutron irradiation and accelerated lifetime testing, materials-damage testing, nuclear-waste burnup, and hybrid fission/fusion power. It is a Speedinvest deep-tech portfolio company. Astral Systems is a hardware/deep-tech provider and does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API specifications.

providers.name: Ateios
providers.description: Ateios Systems is an Indianapolis-based advanced battery manufacturer that produces high-energy, recyclable, PFA-free battery electrodes for global battery makers. Its proprietary RaiCure platform is a solvent-free, cure-on-command coating process using energy-curable polymers instead of solvent-based thermal drying, enabling thicker electrodes (>10 mAh/cm2), higher energy density, and roughly 5x faster coating throughput at lower cost and emissions. Ateios targets medical device, IoT, mobility, and defense markets. Founded in 2017 and backed by Techstars, TitletownTech, Good Growth Capital and others, the company is a materials/hardware manufacturer and publishes no developer API, SDK, or programmatic developer platform.

providers.name: finern
providers.description: Finern (Finern Automation) is a China-based industrial automation company that designs and builds fully automated production lines and intelligent measurement systems for manufacturing. It serves five sectors — automotive, electronics, new energy (battery/EV), healthcare/pharmaceutical equipment, and consumer goods — with automated assembly, testing, and inspection systems. The company reports 600+ personnel, 30,000+ square meters of facilities, 100+ global clients, 8 international sites, and 4 R&D centers. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Finern publishes a corporate marketing website but does not currently expose any public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable discovery surface (no /.well-known/*, llms.txt, or OpenAPI found on probe).

providers.name: Gokin
providers.description: Gokin Solar Co., Ltd. (高景太阳能股份有限公司) is a Chinese photovoltaic manufacturer founded in 2019 and headquartered in Jiangsu, China. The company produces monocrystalline silicon ingots and wafers (N-type and P-type) and high-efficiency solar modules (GOKIN BC and FLAMINGO series), operating four major production bases with roughly 100 GW of wafer and 16 GW of module annual capacity. Ranked among the top three global silicon-wafer shippers, Gokin employs 6,000+ people, holds 500+ patents, and serves utility, commercial, and residential solar projects across 30+ countries. Backed by IDG Capital, Gokin is a solar-hardware manufacturer with a corporate marketing website and no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: Green Revolution Cooling
providers.description: Green Revolution Cooling, which does business as GRC and brands itself "The Immersion Cooling Authority", is an Austin, Texas manufacturer of single-phase liquid immersion cooling systems for data centers. Founded in 2009, GRC builds the ICEraQ family of immersion-cooled racks (SX, Flex, Nano, Micro), the ICEtank containerized immersion data center, the ReliaSys IR500 coolant distribution unit, and ElectroSafe dielectric fluids, and sells them into AI/ML, HPC, edge, enterprise, cloud and hyperscale data centers in more than twenty countries. Its only software product is Systems Manager, an on-premises appliance that gives operators a single monitoring interface across connected ICEraQ and ICEtank systems over the customer's own secure network. GRC publishes no developer portal, no API reference, no SDKs and no machine-readable API description; its systems integrate with data center DCIM and BMS platforms through industrial protocols such as Modbus TCP, SNMP and BACnet rather than through a web API.

providers.name: Nurotron
providers.description: Nurotron (Zhejiang Nurotron Neural Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. / 诺尔康) is a Hangzhou, China-based medical device manufacturer specializing in neural electrical stimulation. Its self-developed neural-prosthesis and neuromodulation product lines span auditory reconstruction (cochlear implants and speech processors such as the CS-10A/CS-20A/CS-30A implant bodies and Airum/NSP processors), visual reconstruction, urological and pelvic-nerve disease treatment, and brain neuromodulation. The company runs a corporate marketing and patient-support website with product, technical-support, rehabilitation-community, and news sections. It is a hardware medical-device company and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or machine-readable API surface. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network for tracking.

providers.name: PicoJool
providers.description: PicoJool is an optical connectivity company building Vertical Cavity Surface Emitting Lasers (VCSELs) and optical engines for AI and cloud data-center infrastructure. Its 50G NRZ, 100G PAM4, and 200G PAM4 VCSEL arrays target 800G and 1.6T transceivers for PCIe, Ethernet, and InfiniBand, aiming to raise bandwidth density and cut the power cost of moving data across hyperscale AI clusters. Founded in 2024 and based in Palo Alto, California, PicoJool emerged from stealth in November 2025 with $12M led by Playground Global. It is a semiconductor/photonics hardware company with no public API or developer platform; this profile is maintained by the API Evangelist network for portfolio and market tracking.

providers.name: Solestial
providers.description: Solestial is a space solar energy company developing space-stable silicon photovoltaics — radiation-hardened, ultrathin flexible silicon heterojunction solar cells and modules for spacecraft. Its products are the only solar products on the market that self-cure radiation damage at operating temperatures, offering competitive performance at lower cost than III-V multijunction solar. Solestial has flight heritage across multiple spacecraft and works with customers including NASA, Boeing, and the U.S. Space Force. This is a hardware and manufacturing company with no public developer API surface.

providers.name: 83 Sciences
providers.description: 83 Sciences is an AI-native materials-discovery company (Y Combinator Summer 2026) that helps research labs unlock value from unpublished and discarded experimental data. Roughly 90% of experimental data never reaches publication; 83 Sciences works on-site with researchers to capture and structure that hidden data into a queryable database, then applies AI-powered analysis and generative models to learn from a lab's full experimental history — including failed experiments — to surface novel materials, co-authored manuscripts, and patents. Founded by researchers from MIT, Stanford, Harvard, and Columbia and based in San Francisco. The company currently ships no public API or developer surface; this profile tracks its identity for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Atomic Semi
providers.description: Atomic Semi is a semiconductor company founded in 2023 by Sam Zeloof and Jim Keller, now operating publicly as fab2 (atomicsemi.com redirects to fab2.com). It designs and manufactures semiconductor fabrication equipment and the fabs that house it — pumps, valves, sensors, actuators, chambers, heaters, gas lines and robots — with the stated goal of mass-producing small, software-defined chip fabs, a "fab fab". It runs a 120K sq ft chip fab in Austin TX (HQ), a 30K sq ft fab fab in Lockhart TX, and the original 25K sq ft garage fab in San Francisco. Its one software product, Studio (formerly Atomic Studio), is an in-browser collaborative EDA for schematic capture, layout and simulation, used internally rather than sold as a developer platform. The company publishes no API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Celero Communications
providers.description: Celero Communications is a fabless semiconductor company headquartered in Irvine, California, founded in 2024 by engineering leaders drawn from Marvell, Inphi, Broadcom and ClariPhy. The company designs coherent digital signal processing (DSP) silicon for high-bandwidth, low-power optical interconnect inside AI data centers, targeting the scale-up and scale-out optical links that connect large AI accelerator clusters, and it operates additional design centers in Canada and Argentina. Celero has raised approximately $140 million to date, including a $100 million Series B led by CapitalG, Alphabet's independent growth fund, following seed and Series A rounds led by Sutter Hill Ventures with participation from Valor Equity Partners, Atreides Management and Maverick Silicon. Celero sells hardware components rather than a developer-facing web service; its public web presence at celero.inc is served behind a Cloudflare managed bot challenge, so no developer, documentation, or API surface could be read during profiling.

providers.name: Celestial AI
providers.description: Celestial AI was a Santa Clara, California silicon-photonics company and the creator of the Photonic Fabric optical interconnect technology platform, which replaces electrical links between compute and memory with light in order to scale AI accelerators within a package, package-to-package, and across racks. The company raised more than $515 million across Series B and Series C rounds and introduced the Photonic Fabric Module, an SoC carrying optical interconnect in the middle of the silicon die. Marvell Technology completed its acquisition of Celestial AI on 2 February 2026 in a cash-and-stock deal reported at approximately $3.25 billion; the technology and team were folded into Marvell's Data Center Group and Celestial AI no longer operates as an independent entity. Its product was semiconductor hardware and IP sold to hyperscalers and accelerator vendors, not software, and it never published a developer program, public API, SDK, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Greyter
providers.description: Greyter Water Systems Inc. was an Ontario, Canada manufacturer of onsite greywater recycling and water reuse systems, founded in 2012 after acquiring the assets of the defunct Brac Systems. Its flagship Greyter HOME captured water from showers and bathtubs, treated it, and returned clear, odor-free water for toilet flushing, cutting a family home's indoor water consumption by up to 25 percent; it earned NSF/ANSI 350 Class R certification in early 2019 as the first compact residential greywater reuse system to hold that designation. A scaled commercial line served water harvesting and reuse for toilet flushing and cooling towers in multi-unit and institutional buildings, and the systems were installed in more than a dozen countries. The company raised roughly $13M through a Series B. Its only software was an end-user monitoring surface — the mygreyter.com portal and a consumer Greyter mobile app used by owners to watch water savings — and it never published a developer program, public API, SDK, webhooks, or any machine-readable specification. Greyter Water Systems Inc. filed for bankruptcy on January 8, 2026, with GlassRatner Restructuring Inc. appointed Trustee and its intellectual property, patents and customer lists placed into an asset sale process. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Nantero
providers.description: Nantero, Inc. was a Woburn, Massachusetts nanotechnology company founded in 2001 by Greg Schmergel, Thomas Rueckes and Brent Segal to commercialize NRAM, a high-density non-volatile random-access memory that stores bits in the physical position of carbon nanotubes deposited on a conventional CMOS substrate. Its business was semiconductor intellectual-property licensing, not software: it raised more than $40 million through a Schlumberger-backed Series D in 2013 and a further ~$31.5 million Series E in 2015 from investors including Charles River Ventures and Draper Fisher Jurvetson, licensed NRAM to Fujitsu Semiconductor in 2016, granted Lockheed Martin an exclusive government-applications license in 2008, and collaborated with imec and Nano-C, but shipped its technology to foundry partners as process IP and test wafers rather than as any product a developer could call. Nantero ceased operations in mid-to-late 2024; its assets were partially acquired by Micron Technology and the remainder sold at auction.
