It never published a developer portal, API, SDK, or machine-readable specification of any kind, and the nantero.com domain has since been re-registered by an unrelated party. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Nexa3D
providers.description: Nexa3D was a Ventura, California additive-manufacturing company that built ultrafast photopolymer 3D printers (NXE 400, XiP, XiP Pro) around its Lubricant Sublayer Photo-curing (LSPc) process, QLS selective-laser-sintering systems, and the NexaX print-preparation and print-management software. The company disclosed severe funding challenges in late 2024, withdrew from Formnext, scaled back operations, and in July 2025 sold select assets — intellectual property, inventory and equipment, but not personnel — to Stratasys, with customer support and materials continuity moving to Stratasys subsidiary iSQUARED. Nexa3D no longer operates as an independent company: nexa3d.com now 301-redirects to a third-party additive-manufacturing materials marketplace, and no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable specification (OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL SDL, MCP manifest, agent card) was found on any Nexa3D host, live or archived.

providers.name: Perfumeo
providers.description: Perfumeo (Perfumeo(R)) is a consumer-hardware startup that built an AI-driven smart-home fragrance diffuser — a connected device holding scent capsules that its companion mobile app uses to adapt diffusion to the user's mood. The company describes itself as combining AI, data science, "green mechatronics" and green chemistry, and states it was founded in Paris in July 2021 and relocated to Cupertino, California in April 2023. It is an end-user product company: no public API, SDK, developer portal, webhook surface or machine-readable contract has ever been published, and none was found in this pass. As of 2026-08-26 the domain the company itself lists as its website, www.perfumeo-ai.com, no longer belongs to it — WHOIS shows the domain was created 2026-06-12 under a Dynadot privacy proxy on domain-parking nameservers, and it now serves a bot-challenge interstitial followed by a "Coming Soon" holding page. The company's LinkedIn page remains up and lists a headcount of one.

providers.name: Qualtera
providers.description: Qualtera was a French software company, founded in 2010 and backed by Serena, that built high-volume big data analytics platforms for semiconductor test and manufacturing — giving IDMs, foundries and OSATs real-time observability, traceability and production control over test and assembly data across worldwide operations, processing the data of tens of millions of wafers and billions of parts a year. Its products included SiliconDash, an automated decision-support system for test, quality and yield analysis. Synopsys acquired Qualtera on June 10, 2020 and folded its analytics into Yield Explorer and TestMAX, which now ship as part of the Synopsys Silicon Lifecycle Management family. The Qualtera brand and any surface it once had are gone: qualtera.com now resolves to Synopsys nameservers and 301-redirects every path to the Synopsys Silicon Lifecycle Management marketing page, and the host refuses a TLS handshake on port 443 entirely. Qualtera never published a public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI definition, SDK or package on any registry, and no machine-readable contract survives under its own name. This profile is retained as a historical record; the live analytics API surface, where one exists, belongs to Synopsys and is profiled there rather than credited here.

providers.name: RSI Video Technologies
providers.description: RSI Video Technologies was a St. Paul, Minnesota maker of wireless, battery-powered intrusion detection devices with built-in cameras, sold worldwide under the Videofied brand, together with the Frontel receiver software that delivered alarm events and short video clips to professional central monitoring stations. Honeywell acquired the company for approximately USD 123 million in March 2016, and the Videofied product line moved to Resideo Technologies when Honeywell spun out its Homes business in 2018. RSI Video Technologies no longer operates as an independent company: its own domains either do not resolve or redirect into Resideo and Honeywell Home marketing pages, and it publishes no developer program, documentation or machine-readable API contract of its own. Any current developer surface for Videofied hardware belongs to Resideo and is profiled separately in the API Evangelist network as resideo-technologies.

providers.name: Tela Innovations
providers.description: Tela Innovations, Inc. is a semiconductor design-technology and intellectual-property company founded in 2005 and headquartered in Los Gatos, California. It developed gridded, straight-line, one-dimensional layout structures and the pre-defined physical topologies built on them, sold as standard-cell libraries and embedded-SRAM peripheral circuits intended to let logic, memory, analog and I/O blocks scale to advanced process nodes with improvements in variability, performance, leakage and area — without forcing customers to change their existing design methodology, equipment set or process technology. Alongside the libraries it sold physical IC design services and layout- and power-optimization software; in 2009 it acquired Blaze DFM, adding patented design-for-manufacturing and power-optimization capability for digital logic in SoCs and ASICs. It was backed by Intel Capital, Cadence Design Systems, Qualcomm, KT Venture Group, Malloy & Company and Black Diamond Ventures, and a substantial share of its later activity was patent licensing, including a portfolio licence taken by Samsung in 2016. Tela never operated a developer program, public API, SDK, webhook surface or machine-readable specification — its products were delivered as licensed cell libraries, EDA software and design services under commercial agreement, not as a callable service. Its corporate host, www.tela-inc.com, still resolves in DNS but no longer runs a web service (ports 80 and 443 both refuse connections) and has no Internet Archive capture with content after January 2022, so it is deliberately not wired as a Website pointer. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Helion Energy
providers.description: Helion Energy is an Everett, Washington fusion power company building commercial fusion electricity generators using a pulsed, magneto-inertial field-reversed configuration (FRC) approach burning deuterium and helium-3. Helion forms two FRC plasmas at opposite ends of its machine, accelerates them toward each other, merges them, and uses pulsed magnetic compression to drive them to fusion conditions; the expanding plasma pushes against the confining magnetic field and induces current directly back into the machine's capacitor bank via Faraday's Law, recapturing electricity without a steam cycle. Founded in 2013 by David Kirtley, John Slough, Chris Pihl, and George Votroubek, Helion is chaired by Sam Altman and has progressed through seven generations of prototypes (IPA, Venti, Trenta, and most recently Polaris) on its way to commercial generators. Polaris, brought online in late 2024, is the company's seventh-generation machine and the first privately developed fusion device to demonstrate measurable deuterium-tritium fusion, reaching 150 million degrees Celsius in February 2026. In May 2023, Helion signed the world's first commercial fusion power purchase agreement, committing to deliver 50 MWe to Microsoft starting in 2028, with the Orion plant planned for the Malaga, Washington area; a subsequent agreement with Nucor targets a 500-MWe facility. Helion is funded by Sam Altman, SoftBank Vision Fund 2, Nucor, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and others, with a reported $5.4B valuation as of early 2025. The company's revenue model is fusion electricity sales under long-term PPAs; Helion has no public developer API, SDK, or open-source software product, and its public GitHub organization (Helion-Energy) contains only forks of plasma-physics simulation tools (WarpX, FerroX, pyamrex, maestrowf).

providers.name: Jewelbots
providers.description: Jewelbots makes smart, codable friendship bracelets designed to teach kids (primarily tween girls) to code. The wearable is an Arduino-compatible, Bluetooth Low Energy device built on a Nordic nRF chipset that friends can program with an Arduino IDE library and firmware, with a companion iOS/Android app for pairing and messaging. The project is largely open source: the Jewelbots GitHub organization publishes the Arduino library, firmware, companion app, and hardware/toolchain repositories. Jewelbots was a 500 Global (500 Startups) portfolio company; jewelbots.com now runs as a Shopify storefront. It is a hardware/firmware and education company rather than a web API provider, and exposes no first-party public HTTP/OpenAPI API.

providers.name: Dow
providers.description: Dow Inc. is a global materials science company headquartered in Midland, Michigan. Dow combines science and technology to develop innovative products and solutions for packaging, infrastructure, mobility, and consumer applications. This entry is an alias of dow-chemical and covers the same parent company.

providers.name: Jabil Circuit
providers.description: Jabil (formerly Jabil Circuit) is a global manufacturing services and solutions company providing comprehensive electronics design, production, and product management services to electronics and technology companies in a broad range of industries.

providers.name: PEI-Genesis
providers.description: PEI-Genesis is a privately held, Philadelphia-headquartered global authorized distributor and value-added assembler of interconnect components (cable and circular connectors), founded in 1946. The company self-describes on LinkedIn as providing "Engineered Solutions for Connectors and Cables" in the Appliances, Electrical, and Electronics Manufacturing industry, with 501-1,000 employees. The public-facing peigenesis.com web property is a product catalog and quote-request portal protected by an interstitial JavaScript challenge; no public REST API, OpenAPI specification, developer portal, EDI integration documentation, PunchOut catalog, or GitHub organization could be located. Public API documentation has not yet been catalogued in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Vaire Computing
providers.description: Vaire Computing is a deep-tech semiconductor startup building reversible computing chips for near-zero energy computing. Its reversible logic gates recover and recycle the energy of computation instead of dissipating it as heat, aiming to decouple energy consumption from growth in computing power. The company was co-founded by Rodolfo Rosini (CEO) and Dr Hannah Earley (CTO), is backed by Seedcamp, 7percent Ventures, and Lifeline Ventures, and publishes technology and software whitepapers. Vaire currently publishes no public API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Apollo Atomics Inc
providers.description: Apollo Atomics is a Y Combinator-backed (Spring 2026 / P26) nuclear technology company building compact, power-dense pressurized water reactors for electricity generation, industrial process heat, and data-center power. Founded by Assil Halimi and Drew Walker and based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, the company modifies the steam generator of proven pressurized water reactor technology to shrink the plant by roughly an order of magnitude without sacrificing power output, turning a decade-long construction project into a factory-built machine that can ship on a truck. Apollo has announced a research collaboration with MIT's Department of Nuclear Science and Engineering to validate its reactor design and has submitted a regulatory engagement plan to the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission, targeting a construction permit application in 2028. This is a hardware/energy company with no public developer or API surface at this time.

providers.name: Cassie
providers.description: Cassie (Aircassie) develops advanced air filtration technology for healthcare and indoor environments. Its flagship CASSIE system uses patented filtration to eliminate mold, viruses, and bacteria with zero harmful emissions, contrasting with UV and ionizer systems that emit ozone. The company markets 99.9% effectiveness against viruses and bacteria, a 59-second disinfection cycle, and 24-hour air quality monitoring with real-time data. Cassie is a hardware and environmental-technology company backed by Techstars; it was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead. As of this enrichment pass it publishes a marketing website (Wix) with no public API, developer documentation, SDKs, or other machine-readable API artifacts.

providers.name: EnerVenue
providers.description: EnerVenue is a Fremont, California-based energy infrastructure company building long-duration stationary energy storage using a metal-hydrogen (nickel-hydrogen) battery chemistry derived from NASA-heritage technology that has powered the Hubble Space Telescope and the International Space Station since the 1980s. Co-founded by Stanford materials scientist Professor Yi Cui, EnerVenue refined the orbital nickel-hydrogen cell into a grid-scale "Energy Storage Vessel" (ESV) targeting a 30-year, 30,000+ cycle service life with 100% usable depth of discharge, ~90% round-trip efficiency, an operating range of -20 C to +60 C, no thermal runaway risk, and no active thermal management. The ESV's aqueous metal cell (AMC) uses a nickel hydroxide cathode, a nickel-alloy anode, an alkaline electrolyte, and hermetically sealed hydrogen gas storage built from steel, nickel, fiberglass, resin, and water — no lithium, cobalt, or rare earths. EnerVenue is scaling manufacturing through a one-million- square-foot gigafactory in Shelby County, Kentucky (1 GWh phase one, scaling toward 20 GWh per year with ~$1B of follow-on investment) plus a high-volume line in Changzhou, China (250 MWh by Q3 2026, 1 GWh in 2027). Customer commitments exceed 7 GWh and include Pine Gate Renewables (2.4 GWh, multi-year), Green Energy Renewable Solutions (Nicon Industries), Sonnell Power Solutions, and VedantaESS. The company closed a $300M Series B in 2026 to fund the gigafactory build-out. EnerVenue sells hardware, EPC-integrated storage systems, and long-duration service warranties — it does not publish a developer API, SDK, public OpenAPI specification, or open-source repository.

providers.name: Ideal Power Converters
providers.description: Ideal Power Inc. (NASDAQ: IPWR), formerly Ideal Power Converters, is an Austin, Texas power semiconductor company developing bidirectional bipolar junction transistor (B-TRAN) technology for ultra-low conduction losses, bidirectional current flow, and fast fault protection and switching. Its product portfolio includes B-TRAN power switches, SymCool power modules, and B-TRAN Known Good Die, targeting data centers, energy storage systems, power grids, solid-state circuit breakers, and EV charging infrastructure. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a Battery Ventures portfolio company; the company publishes a corporate and investor web presence but no public developer API or programmatic surface at this time.

providers.name: Rfmd
providers.description: RFMD (RF Micro Devices) was a semiconductor manufacturer of radio-frequency (RF) components for mobile, infrastructure, defense, and aerospace markets. In January 2015 RFMD merged with TriQuint Semiconductor to form Qorvo, and the rfmd.com domain now redirects to qorvo.com. Qorvo designs and manufactures RF and power solutions — amplifiers, filters, integrated circuits, wireless connectivity, and power management devices — spanning mobile, defense/aerospace, network infrastructure, IoT, automotive, and consumer electronics. As a hardware semiconductor company, RFMD/Qorvo publishes no public developer web API; its developer-facing resources are simulation models, QSPICE circuit-simulation software, datasheets, evaluation boards, and a technical support forum. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio lead of norwest-venture-partners and enriched to reflect the RFMD-to-Qorvo identity; there is no API surface to catalog.

providers.name: TeraWatt Technology
providers.description: TeraWatt Technology Inc. is a next-generation lithium-ion battery company founded in 2020 by Ken Ogata (CEO) and Yifan Tang, headquartered in California with an R&D center in Santa Clara and operations in Japan, including its first mass-production facility in Shizuoka. The company develops, manufactures and commercializes lithium-ion cells engineered for ultra-high energy density, high power output, improved safety and competitive cost, aimed at electric vehicles, drones, eVTOL aircraft and grid-scale energy-storage systems. It closed a Series C round with investors including Khosla Ventures, Temasek, JIC Venture Growth Investments, JBIC, JERA and ITOCHU Technology Ventures. TeraWatt Technology is a hardware manufacturer: it publishes no public API, developer portal, machine-readable contract or SDK, which was verified by probing its only public host rather than assumed.

providers.name: Arzeda
providers.description: Arzeda Corp is a Seattle, Washington protein design company — "The Protein Design Company" — founded in 2008 by David Baker (2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry), Alexandre Zanghellini and colleagues out of the University of Washington Institute for Protein Design. Its Intelligent Protein Design Technology combines physics-based computational protein design, generative AI and an agentic design-build-test-learn loop over fifteen years of proprietary in-house experimental data to create designer enzymes and proteins that do not exist in nature, then scale them to commercial production. Commercial programs span food and beverage (ViaLeaf Reb M / ProSweet Reb M stevia sweeteners with MANE), home and personal care enzymes (Unilever), advanced materials (W. L. Gore & Associates) and pharmaceutical biologics (Takeda), alongside DARPA and NSF funded work on AI-driven protein design and cell-free biomanufacturing. Arzeda co-founded the OpenFold consortium for open-source protein structure prediction. It sells designed molecules and joint development programs, not software, and publishes no public developer program, API or machine-readable interface.

providers.name: Dow Chemical
providers.description: Dow Chemical, now operating as Dow Inc., is a global materials science company headquartered in Midland, Michigan. Dow develops innovative products and solutions across three segments - Packaging and Specialty Plastics, Industrial Intermediates and Infrastructure, and Performance Materials and Coatings - serving packaging, infrastructure, mobility, and consumer applications.

providers.name: DuPont
providers.description: DuPont is a leading solutions provider for healthcare, water, and a broad range of industrial segments, powered by high-performance engineered products, leading-edge application development, and top-tier manufacturing. No public developer APIs or developer portal have been identified at this time; this index captures DuPont's web presence for monitoring future developer activity.

providers.name: hhgregg
providers.description: hhgregg is an electronics retailer offering products such as televisions, cameras, professional video equipment, laptops, headphones, drones, and more, with free shipping and installation services on many products.

providers.name: Modulus Video
providers.description: Modulus Video is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of trinity-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: hardware. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Northpoint Communications
providers.description: Northpoint Communications is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of accel and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: hardware. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: SiTera
providers.description: SiTera is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of matrix-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: semiconductors. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Kyten Technologies
providers.description: Kyten Technologies is a Seattle, Washington hardware manufacturing startup building a factory to produce custom aerospace-grade battery packs. The founders spent six years at Starlink, where they put more than 5,000 battery packs into space, and are now bringing rapid development and volume production of aerospace-grade battery packs to the wider industry. The company positions itself against a legacy supply chain that cannot keep up with the 100,000+ drones, submarines, and satellites being built in the United States. Kyten Technologies is a Y Combinator Winter 2026 company, classified under Industrials / Manufacturing and Robotics, and was an early-stage two-person team at the time of profiling. As a hardware manufacturer it publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API artifacts; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: Letel
providers.description: Shanghai Letel Communication Equipment (Group) Co., Ltd. (上海乐通通信设备（集团）股份有限公司) is a Chinese manufacturer of information and communication network infrastructure, founded in March 1992 and headquartered in Shanghai with over 1,500 employees and 20+ service locations nationwide. Letel builds data center physical infrastructure — cabinet micromodules, cold aisle micromodules, containerized micromodules, pallet IT cabins, and cabinets — alongside communication cabling equipment, optical communication devices, data communication equipment, broadband access equipment, and structural components for notebooks and servers. It operates through subsidiaries including Zhongle Communication Technology Co., Ltd. Letel publishes no public API, developer portal, or developer documentation; this is a company profile in the API Evangelist network, surfaced as a Qiming Venture Partners portfolio company.

providers.name: LiquidStack
providers.description: LiquidStack is a data center liquid cooling company that designs, manufactures and services direct-to-chip and immersion cooling systems for AI, hyperscale, high performance computing, edge/5G and cryptocurrency workloads. Its product line spans direct-to-chip coolant distribution units — the CDU-1MW at up to 1,350kW of cooling at N+1 and the modular GigaModular CDU-10MW platform — alongside single-phase and two-phase immersion DataTank systems rated to 252kW, plus full lifecycle services covering consulting, installation, training and maintenance. The company spun out of Bitfury in 2021, raised $20 million from Tiger Global, is headquartered in Carrollton, Texas with engineering, R&D and manufacturing operations in Texas and Hong Kong, and was acquired by Trane Technologies in a deal completed in March 2026. LiquidStack sells capital equipment and services rather than software: it operates no developer program and publishes no public API, specification, SDK or developer portal. The only machine interface it documents is embedded in the hardware — its CDUs ship with native MODBUS TCP/IP or a RESTful API, plus BACnet/IP and SNMP, for remote management from a customer's own building or data center management system.

providers.name: Misfit
providers.description: Misfit is a consumer wearables brand — fitness trackers and smartwatches such as the Misfit Shine, Flash, Ray and Vapor — founded in 2011 by Sonny Vu, John Sculley and Sridhar Iyengar and backed by Norwest Venture Partners, Khosla Ventures, Founders Fund, GGV Capital and Xiaomi before being acquired by Fossil Group in 2015. Misfit ran a developer program (the Misfit Cloud API, Device SDK and Scientific Library) at build.misfit.com with 30+ launch partners. Fossil discontinued the Misfit backend, Cloud API and companion app in spring 2023, so the hosted API and all misfit.com domains are now unreachable. The only surviving developer surface is the official Misfit-Developers GitHub organization and its unmaintained iOS SDKs on CocoaPods.

providers.name: Modern Electron
providers.description: Modern Electron is a Bothell, Washington energy-hardware company founded in 2015 by Tony Pan (CEO) and Max Mankin (CTO) as a spin-out of Intellectual Ventures. It was built to commercialize advanced thermionic energy converters — solid-state, direct heat-to-electricity devices intended to add on-site generation to combustion and thermal equipment. The company now operates publicly as Modern Hydrogen, applying methane pyrolysis behind the meter to crack natural gas into hydrogen and solid carbon before combustion, for industrial heat and steam, on-site power, data-center energy, asphalt products and heavy-duty fleet fueling. The product is physical equipment installed at customer sites; Modern Electron / Modern Hydrogen operates no developer program, publishes no public API, SDK or machine-readable specification, and its public GitHub organization holds only forks of open-source scientific-computing projects (WarpX, AMReX, PICMI, GPy) used in its own R&D.

providers.name: Transphorm
providers.description: Transphorm was a GaN (gallium nitride) power-semiconductor company based in Goleta, California, known for its GaN-on-Si cascode FET technology used in power supplies, fast chargers, motor drives, solar inverters, and EV charging. It was acquired by Renesas Electronics in June 2024, and transphormusa.com now redirects to the Renesas GaN power-discretes product line. Transphorm publishes no public web API surface.

providers.name: Unigrid
providers.description: UNIGRID Inc. is a San Diego-based sodium-ion battery company founded in 2021 out of UC San Diego Ph.D. research by Dr. Darren H. S. Tan and Dr. Erik A. Wu. Its sodium chromium oxide (NCO) chemistry and alloy anode technology deliver fire-safe, fully passive batteries rated for 30,000+ cycles and -40C to 60C operation, sold as 12V starter batteries (Na+ Fleet), BMS-less rack modules (Na+ Module), residential energy storage (Na+ Casa), and DC rack systems for commercial, industrial, and data center use (Na+ Cleo). Cells are UN38.3 and UL 9540A certified. Backed by Transition VC, Ritz Venture Capital, Union Square Ventures, and Foothill Ventures via an oversubscribed $12M Series A (2024); shipped its first sodium-ion residential batteries in July 2026. UNIGRID publishes no public API or developer program.

providers.name: Voxel Energy
providers.description: Voxel Energy is a Y Combinator Winter 2026 company building energy-independent, off-grid data centers powered by on-site solar generation and second-life EV batteries over a DC microgrid architecture. Founded in 2025 by ex-Tesla engineers Casey Spencer, Max Pfeiffer, and Evan Schmidt, the San Francisco company delivers modular, prefabricated data center power systems that bypass multi-year utility interconnection queues, taking facilities from site selection to commissioning in months. Voxel Energy is an infrastructure hardware company and does not currently publish a public API or developer program.

providers.name: XtalPi
providers.description: XtalPi is an AI-and-quantum-physics drug discovery and materials research platform company with headquarters in Cambridge, Massachusetts and major operations in Beijing, Shanghai, and Shenzhen, publicly listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange under stock code 2228.HK. The company combines a hybrid AI plus quantum mechanics (QM) discovery engine with large-scale robotic laboratory automation to accelerate molecular research and development for pharmaceutical, agrochemical, and materials customers, including engagements with Pfizer, Eli Lilly, and Novartis. XtalPi's offering spans proprietary software platforms — PatSight for patent extraction, XFEP for free-energy perturbation binding-affinity prediction, XMolGen for generative chemistry, and XtalGazer for solid-state research — and intelligent automation hardware including the XmartChem intelligent synthesis workstation and ChemPlus desktop solid dispenser. Its drug discovery services cover hit discovery, hit/lead optimization, biology capabilities, focused library synthesis, and the PepiX peptide platform, complemented by sister brands Ailux (biology) and AiFChem (chemistry). XtalPi's products are delivered as enterprise collaborations, licensed software, and CRO-style services; there is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release.

providers.name: AMD
providers.description: A multinational semiconductor company designing high-performance processors, graphics cards, and adaptive computing solutions. Competes in data center, gaming, and embedded markets with its Ryzen, EPYC, and Radeon product lines.

providers.name: Epirus
providers.description: Epirus is a Torrance, California-based defense technology company building solid-state, software-defined high-power microwave (HPM) directed-energy systems for counter-electronics and counter-unmanned-aerial-systems (cUAS) missions. Its flagship product is Leonidas, a non-kinetic HPM weapon system designed to defeat single drones and large drone swarms by disabling their onboard electronics, with a growing product family that includes Leonidas IFPC-HPM (Indirect Fire Protection Capability — High-Power Microwave) for the U.S. Army, Leonidas Expeditionary (ExDECS) for the U.S. Marine Corps, Leonidas H2O for maritime interdiction, the portable Leonidas Pod, and Stryker Leonidas (with General Dynamics Land Systems). Epirus also collaborates with Anduril, Northrop Grumman, L3Harris, Kodiak AI, Peraton, and Palantir, and has received contracts from the U.S. Army, U.S. Air Force, U.S. Navy, DARPA, ONR, and Singapore's DSTA. The company is privately held, has raised more than $550M across Series B/C/D, and operates under CMMC Level 2 certification. Its product surface is classified defense hardware and embedded firmware — there is no public developer portal, REST API, SDK, or open-source software offering.

providers.name: Peloton Interactive
providers.description: Peloton Interactive is a connected fitness company that produces interactive exercise equipment and a streaming subscription service. The company sells connected stationary bikes, treadmills, rowers, and a digital app offering live and on-demand fitness classes. Peloton has built a large community of members who participate in instructor-led workouts and track performance metrics through its platform.

providers.name: Alsym Energy
providers.description: Alsym Energy is a Malden, Massachusetts battery technology company founded in 2015 by Mukesh Chatter, Rahul Mukherjee, and Kripa Varanasi to develop low-cost, high-performance rechargeable batteries that are free of lithium and cobalt. Its Na-Series is a line of non-flammable, non-toxic sodium-ion batteries aimed at grid and utility-scale energy storage, data-center backup, and industrial applications where safety and supply-chain resilience matter. The company uses a proprietary AI/computational-materials platform to accelerate battery chemistry development, and has raised roughly $111M+ including a $78M round in 2024 led by Tata Limited and General Catalyst. Alsym is a hardware/energy-infrastructure manufacturer and does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures its identity and public web surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Amprius Technologies
providers.description: Amprius Technologies is a Fremont, California-based developer and manufacturer of high-energy density lithium-ion batteries built on a proprietary 100% silicon anode platform. Its flagship SiCore and SiMaxx cell families are marketed as among the industry's highest gravimetric and volumetric energy density rechargeable cells, enabling longer endurance, faster charging, and higher payload capacity than conventional graphite-anode chemistries. Amprius targets aviation and aerospace (high-altitude pseudo-satellites, unmanned aerial systems, electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft), defense (US Army soldier-worn power, BAE Systems), light electric vehicles, robotics, and AI hardware. Public references include AALTO's Airbus-derived Zephyr HAPS programs, Prismatic's PHASA-35 stratospheric aircraft, Nokia Drone Networks, and Matternet drone delivery. The company runs pilot manufacturing and R&D in Fremont and is scaling a GWh-scale Brighton, Colorado plant alongside contract manufacturing partnerships in Asia. Amprius is publicly traded on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker AMPX. It is certified to ISO 9001:2015 and AS9100:2016. Amprius sells cells, modules, and engineering services to OEMs and defense primes; it does not publish a developer API, SDK, or open-source battery telemetry interface, and has no public GitHub organization.

providers.name: Nabhdrishti Aerospace
providers.description: Nabhdrishti Aerospace is a Bangalore-based deep-tech startup building India's first fuel-flex micro gas turbine for aviation and power generation. Its ND 400 engine is a 400 N single-core micro gas turbine designed for UAVs, hybrid-electric aircraft, and small aircraft as well as oil & gas, manufacturing, and vehicle range-extender power generation, running on conventional fuels, biofuels, and hydrogen with an innovative recuperator design that targets greater than 15% efficiency at under half the cost of competing turbines. Backed by Accel, the company raised USD 3M and operates from the IISc Bangalore IHUB. As a hardware manufacturer it publishes no public API, SDK, or developer platform; this profile tracks its public web presence.

providers.name: NuScale Power
providers.description: NuScale Power is a Portland, Oregon-based small modular reactor (SMR) company developing the NuScale Power Module (NPM), a 77 MWe pressurized light-water reactor that is the first — and to date one of only two — SMR designs to receive design approval from the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission. Originally certified in 2020 at 50 MWe and uprated to 77 MWe under the US460 Standard Design Approval issued by the NRC on May 29, 2025, the NPM is delivered as a factory-fabricated, rail-shippable cylindrical containment vessel using passive natural-circulation safety features. Its commercial offering, the VOYGR SMR power plant, is sold in 4-, 6-, and 12-module configurations (308, 462, and 924 MWe respectively) and is targeted at utilities, data centers, hydrogen production, district heating, desalination, and industrial process heat. NuScale traces its origins to Oregon State University research begun in 2000 and was formally founded in 2007; Fluor Corporation became majority investor in 2011. The company went public on the NYSE in 2022 (ticker SMR) through a SPAC merger with Spring Valley Acquisition Corp., becoming the first publicly traded pure-play SMR vendor. NuScale partners exclusively with ENTRA1 Energy for global commercialization and operates Energy Exploration (E2) Centers — full control-room simulators hosted at Oregon State University, Texas A&M, the University of Idaho, and SNU in South Korea — for operator and regulator training. The high-profile Utah Associated Municipal Power Systems (UAMPS) Carbon Free Power Project at Idaho National Laboratory was terminated in November 2023 after costs rose from $58 to $89/MWh and subscription targets fell short, leaving NuScale without a first-of-a-kind US deployment and prompting a focus on data-center, industrial, and international (Romania RoPower, Poland KGHM, Ghana, Standard Power) opportunities. NuScale's revenue model is power-module sales/leasing, EPC services, and plant lifecycle services — there is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release. NPM design data, topical reports, and safety analysis are conveyed through NRC docket filings and topical reports rather than a developer portal.

providers.name: Pacific Fusion
providers.description: Pacific Fusion is a fusion energy company based in Fremont, California developing commercial fusion power using pulsed magnetic inertial fusion. Its modular system pairs a fast electric pulser, a meter-scale fusion chamber, and centimeter-scale fuel targets to pursue net facility gain with practical, affordable manufacturing. Building on breakthroughs from US National Laboratories (Lawrence Livermore, Sandia) and partners such as General Atomics, the company aims to deliver limitless, clean, on-demand power. Surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC, General Catalyst, and Lightspeed Venture Partners, this profile has been enriched through the API Evangelist network. Pacific Fusion is a hardware and energy company and publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK surface at this time.

providers.name: Plexus
providers.description: Plexus is a global manufacturing and product development company that helps customers in highly regulated industries (Aerospace/Defense, Healthcare/Life Sciences, Industrial, and Semiconductor Capital Equipment) design, manufacture, and service their products. Plexus does not currently publish a public developer API; this index tracks customer/supplier portals and corporate web properties.

providers.name: TAE Technologies
providers.description: TAE Technologies (formerly Tri Alpha Energy) is a Foothill Ranch, California fusion energy company founded in 1998, pursuing commercial fusion power using aneutronic hydrogen-boron (p-B11) fuel in an advanced beam-driven field-reversed configuration (FRC). Because the p-B11 reaction is aneutronic, TAE's approach produces virtually no neutron flux or on-site radioactive waste compared with conventional deuterium-tritium concepts. The company has built a progression of plasma machines — Sewer Pipe, CBFR-SPS, C-2, C-2U, and C-2W ("Norman") — and is constructing Copernicus in Irvine, California to demonstrate net energy gain, with Da Vinci planned as the grid-connected power-plant demonstration. TAE has raised more than USD 1.2 billion from investors including Google, Chevron, NEA, Goldman Sachs, Vulcan, Venrock, Wellcome Trust, and the Kuwait Investment Authority, and runs research collaborations with Japan's National Institute for Fusion Science (NIFS). Two operating subsidiaries commercialize spin-off technology: TAE Life Sciences develops accelerator-based Boron Neutron Capture Therapy (BNCT) systems for cancer treatment, and TAE Power Solutions builds modular, software-controlled power-management systems for e-mobility and battery applications. TAE is a private hardware and deep-science company; it does not publish a developer API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, or public open-source code repository.

providers.name: Volt14
providers.description: Volt14 Solutions Pte Ltd is a Singapore-based deep-tech startup developing silicon-majority anode materials for lithium-ion batteries. Its fully integrated, tunable, and ready-to-use anodes replace conventional graphite to deliver large gains in energy density and lower normalized cell cost, while remaining compatible with existing battery cell manufacturing infrastructure. Target application markets include electric vehicles, consumer electronics, appliances, and power tools. The company is a materials-science and battery-technology producer; it publishes a corporate and careers website but exposes no public developer or API product surface. Backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: SOURCE Global
providers.description: SOURCE Global, PBC (founded as Zero Mass Water) is a Scottsdale, Arizona public benefit corporation started in 2014 by Arizona State University materials scientist Cody Friesen to make drinking water out of sunlight and air. Its SOURCE Hydropanel is an off-grid solar-thermal device that pulls water vapor from the atmosphere, condenses and mineralizes it, and delivers roughly five liters of drinking water a day; the panels were deployed in residential, commercial, community and humanitarian projects across more than 50 countries, and the company later moved into bottled water, acquiring Proud Source Water in 2023. It raised approximately USD 270 million in total, including a USD 50 million Series C led by BlackRock in 2020 and a USD 130 million Series D in 2022 co-led by Breakthrough Energy Ventures and the Drawdown Fund with Microsoft Climate Innovation Fund and Fifth Wall participating. SOURCE was a hardware and consumer-products business rather than a software vendor: it never published a developer portal, API reference, SDK or any machine-readable API contract, and the only machine-readable surface its site ever exposed was the Shopify platform behind its direct-to-consumer storefront. The company went quiet during 2025 — an April 2025 SEC filing showed a USD 75 million raise that closed at USD 19.3 million, and founder Cody Friesen announced his departure in June 2025 — and as of August 2026 source.co answers HTTP 402 "Store unavailable" on every path while the legacy zeromasswater.com domain resolves to a parked GoDaddy builder page.

providers.name: Allevi
providers.description: Allevi is a bioprinting company that designs and manufactures 3D bioprinters, bioinks, and accompanying software for tissue engineering, regenerative medicine, and life-sciences research. Its desktop bioprinters and biomaterials let researchers fabricate living tissue constructs for drug discovery, disease modeling, and organ-on-chip work. Allevi was acquired by 3D Systems and operates as part of its regenerative medicine portfolio. The company publishes bioprinting protocols, application notes, webinars, and white papers, but exposes no public web API, developer portal, or SDK at this time.

providers.name: Lam Research
providers.description: Lam Research is a global supplier of innovative wafer fabrication equipment and services to the semiconductor industry, providing systems used in the production of integrated circuits.

providers.name: onsemi
providers.description: ON Semiconductor (now branded as onsemi) is a global supplier of semiconductor-based solutions for power efficiency, image sensing, and signal processing in automotive, industrial, and other applications. No public APIs are documented at this time.

providers.name: Nlight
providers.description: nLIGHT, Inc. (NASDAQ: LASR) is a US-based designer and manufacturer of high-power semiconductor and fiber lasers, optical fibers, and beam-control systems. For more than 25 years the company has served mission-critical directed-energy and defense, sensing, and advanced-manufacturing markets (cutting, welding, additive, medical, and battery production) from a vertically integrated stack spanning semiconductor chips to complete laser systems, with a portfolio of over 450 patents and design and manufacturing based in Camas, Washington. nLIGHT is a hardware and photonics company and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Reach Labs
providers.description: Reach Labs (operating as Reach Power Inc.) is a wireless power transmission company that delivers electrical energy through the air without physical connections, describing its mission as "doing for power what Wi-Fi did for data." Its patented approach combines energy-transmission hardware, a custom delivery algorithm, and adaptive software controls to beam power to devices across varying distances and conditions. The company targets three primary sectors: defense and intelligence (powering sensors, autonomous vehicles, and drones in remote environments), manufacturing and logistics (energizing robotics and IoT devices in industrial settings), and public safety (enabling continuous drone operations for first responders). Reach was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or machine-readable metadata surface.

providers.name: TSMC
providers.description: The world's largest dedicated semiconductor foundry manufacturing chips for leading technology companies. Produces the most advanced processor chips used in smartphones, data centers, and AI applications for clients including Apple, NVIDIA, and AMD.

providers.name: Anki
providers.description: Anki, Inc. was a consumer robotics and artificial-intelligence company based in San Francisco, founded in 2010 and backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Index Ventures, and J.P. Morgan. It was known for the Cozmo and Vector companion robots and the Anki Drive / Overdrive robotic racing system, which combined computer vision, on-device AI, and mapping/navigation. Anki debuted at Apple's WWDC in 2013, shipped Cozmo in 2016 and Vector in 2018, and published first-party Python and C# SDKs so developers could program the robots over a local connection. Anki ceased operations in May 2019 and its assets were later acquired by Digital Dream Labs. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; the robot SDKs remain the company's public developer surface.

providers.name: Alpha Technologies
providers.description: Alpha Technologies is a power-systems manufacturer providing AC, DC, and renewable powering solutions for the telecom, cable-broadband, traffic, security, industrial, and alternative-energy industries. Its product line spans uninterruptible power supplies (UPS), standby and non-standby power systems, batteries, enclosures, network/fiber powering gear, and renewable-energy products. Founded in the 1980s and now part of EnerSys, Alpha operates as a hardware and stored-energy solutions provider rather than a public API platform; it was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as an Accel-associated portfolio lead and carries no public developer or API surface at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Amphiform
providers.description: Amphiform is an energy technology company redefining the future of energy by developing new materials and manufacturing processes that create clean, abundant, and dense energy sources. Rather than scaling existing technologies, Amphiform engineers entirely new materials using precise manufacturing tools to address energy demands for decarbonization, computing, and space exploration. A General Catalyst portfolio company in the energy-infrastructure sector, it is pre-product and does not currently publish any public API, developer documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Arcturus
providers.description: Arcturus (Arcturus Technologies) is a Los Angeles advanced-materials company founded by Amir Mashal that infuses carbon nanomaterials into metals to create a new class of conductors, using lasers to embed carbon into copper and dramatically improve its electrical, thermal, and mechanical performance. Positioned in frontier climate/energy tech, its drop-in materials target motor windings, bus bars, heat sinks, data-center infrastructure, electric motors, drones, robotics, and — over time — transmission lines and grid infrastructure. The company emerged from stealth in June 2026 with an $8M seed round led by Initialized Capital, with 1517, Breakthrough Energy Discovery, Toyota Ventures, and Wireframe Ventures participating. This is a deep-tech hardware/materials company with no public API or developer program; the profile is maintained as an API Evangelist network company record.

providers.name: atantares
providers.description: Atantares (芯宿科技) is a Chinese synthetic-biology company based in Suzhou Industrial Park that builds "silicon-based biology" — semiconductor-driven biotechnology. Its chip-based, high-throughput platform (the EcoSyn synthesizer and ECHOS MicroArray, using electrochemical oligonucleotide synthesis on CMOS/MEMS microelectrode arrays) drives low-cost, high-fidelity DNA synthesis and is expanding into RNA and protein synthesis and detection. Research-service offerings include primer/oligo synthesis, gene synthesis, gene sequencing, cloning and mutagenesis, strain-library preparation, and gene editing, built on an in-house full-workflow automation, sequence-analysis, and order-management platform. Backed by Qiming Venture Partners. The company operates a marketing website only and publishes no public developer program, API, or documentation at the time of this profile.

providers.name: Bellabeat
providers.description: Bellabeat is a femtech and women's wellness technology company founded in 2014 by Urska Srsen and Sandro Mur, headquartered in San Francisco, California. It designs health-tracking wearables and connected devices aimed at women, including the Leaf and Ivy wellness jewelry trackers, the Time hybrid smartwatch, and the Spring smart water bottle, paired with the Bellabeat mobile app that tracks activity, sleep, stress, meditation, menstrual cycle, and overall wellness. Bellabeat operates as a direct-to-consumer wellness brand; it does not currently publish a public developer API, so this profile captures company identity and network provenance rather than API artifacts. Added to the API Evangelist network as a Y Combinator portfolio lead and enriched here.

providers.name: Beyond Reach Labs
providers.description: Beyond Reach Labs is a Brooklyn, New York aerospace company building deployable solar arrays and thermal radiators for spacecraft that expand from compact launch sizes to enormous structures in orbit. Its patented geometry-changing panels grow from the size of a dining table to a football field once deployed, giving satellites, orbital data centers, commercial space stations, and lunar outposts up to 10x more usable power without adding launch mass or volume. Founded by two aerospace engineers, the company is targeting its first in-space demonstration in Q2 2027 and is a Y Combinator portfolio company. Beyond Reach Labs is a hardware manufacturer and does not currently publish a public API or developer program.

providers.name: Cencorp
providers.description: Cencorp (Zhuhai) Industrial Technology Co., Ltd. is a process-automation equipment manufacturer that designs and builds high-end laser processing, dispensing, automated optical inspection (AOI), and system-integration & automation systems for the consumer electronics, automotive electronics, semiconductor, and new-energy industries. Formed in 2020 and combining the acquired Finland-based Cencorp automation business with operations headquartered in Zhuhai, China, the company runs 12 offices worldwide with 400+ R&D engineers and 300+ patents, and is a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. It exposes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal — this is a physical automation-equipment business.

providers.name: Chariot Defense
providers.description: Chariot Defense is a San Francisco-area defense technology company building high-voltage, hybrid-electric power systems for the modern battlefield. Its AMPHORA family (the 24 VDC / 5 kW A24 and the 400 VDC / 35 kW A400) and the upcoming VANGUARD platform deliver quiet, high-density, transportable power that replaces loud, fuel-hungry diesel generators, cutting energy signature and fuel use while powering distributed systems such as drones, sensors, electronic warfare, command and control, additive manufacturing, and directed-energy weapons. Founded in 2022 by Adam Warmoth, the company has raised $41M (a $34M Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz plus an $8M seed) and its systems are fielded by the U.S. Army and the Defense Innovation Unit. This is a hardware/defense company profiled in the API Evangelist network; it publishes no public developer API, portal, or documentation.

providers.name: Circularity Fuels
providers.description: Circularity Fuels builds AI-controlled, mass-manufacturable reactors that turn waste carbon and cheap renewable power into drop-in hydrocarbons, starting with affordable sustainable aviation fuel (SAF). Its Ouro Reactor reforms waste carbon (methane and CO2 off-gassed by dairy farms, agricultural plants, and industrial facilities) into clean syngas, and its Aion Reactor uses next-generation Fischer-Tropsch synthesis to assemble that syngas into liquid fuels. The company is a portfolio company of DCVC and was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile. It is a hardware and process company with no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Eltek
providers.description: Eltek is a Norwegian power-electronics and telecom power-systems manufacturer (DC power rectifiers, industrial and telecom energy systems, the Flatpack product family) now operating as part of Delta Electronics. Its primary domain eltek.com 301-redirects to Delta's standard telecom power solutions catalog (www.delta-emea.com). This is a physical-hardware brand: no independent developer portal, public API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or well-known discovery surface was found. Surfaced as a portfolio-lead stub via the sierra-ventures VC pipeline; profile retained for domain-security signal and future re-check.

providers.name: Evonetix
providers.description: Evonetix is a Cambridge, UK deep-technology company developing a benchtop DNA synthesis platform built on semiconductor technology. Its core innovation is a silicon chip carrying thousands of independently thermally-controlled reaction sites, allowing many DNA strands to be synthesised in parallel with per-site temperature control, in-process error detection and correction, and assembly of high-fidelity genes at the desktop. The company's goal is to give synthetic biology, life-science, and drug-discovery researchers accurate, on-demand access to synthetic DNA without relying on centralised outsourced gene foundries. Evonetix was surfaced as a portfolio company of the deep-tech venture firm DCVC and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK, and its primary web domain (evonetix.com) resolves to a suspended-account placeholder page.

providers.name: FangTek
providers.description: FangTek (Shanghai Fangtek Electronics Co., Ltd.) is a Chinese fabless semiconductor company headquartered in Shanghai. It designs highly integrated analog and mixed-signal integrated circuits for mobile phones, portable devices and consumer electronics, with a product line spanning audio power amplifiers, voice and audio processing, image processing, LED drivers, power management ICs, analog switches and DC boost converters. Qiming Venture Partners lists FangTek in its portfolio as "a leading provider of highly integrated circuit solutions for cell phone, portable device, voice processing, audio processing and image processing." FangTek is a silicon component vendor that reaches customers through electronics distributors; it publishes no public developer platform, web API, SDK or machine-readable API surface, so this profile carries identity and domain-security data only.

providers.name: Fujian Deer Technology
providers.description: Fujian Deer Technology (福建德尔科技股份有限公司) is a Chinese specialty-chemicals manufacturer founded in June 2014 and headquartered in the Jiaoyang Industrial Concentration Zone, Shanghang County, Longyan City, Fujian Province. The company pursues a full fluorine-chemistry industry-chain strategy, researching, producing and selling basic chemical materials, fluorine-containing electronic gases, high-purity semiconductor wet electronic chemicals, new-energy (lithium battery) materials and other fluorinated advanced materials. Its electronic-grade gases include trifluoromethane, carbon tetrafluoride, sulfur hexafluoride, hexafluoroethane, chlorine trifluoride and octafluorocyclobutane, supplied into semiconductor chips, LED chips, flat-panel displays, communications optical fibre, power and energy-storage batteries, ultra-high-voltage transmission and transformation, and photovoltaic power generation. It is a designated national high-tech enterprise and is privately held; its shares appear on secondary-market venues. It manufactures physical materials and publishes no public API, developer program or machine-readable interface.

providers.name: Happiest Baby
providers.description: Happiest Baby is a consumer sleep-technology company founded by pediatrician Dr. Harvey Karp, best known for the SNOO Smart Sleeper - an FDA-authorized responsive bassinet that uses sensor-driven motion and white noise to soothe infants and improve sleep. The company also sells the Sleepea swaddle and sleep sacks, runs a companion mobile app with parenting guidance, and operates a healthcare/hospital program. Its connected SNOO hardware communicates in real time over PubNub; Happiest Baby publishes no official public developer API, and the only programmatic access is via community-built wrappers around the undocumented mobile-app API. Backed by GV and Obvious Ventures.

providers.name: Hydro Wind Energy
providers.description: Hydro Wind Energy develops offshore renewable energy infrastructure at the convergence of dispatchable clean power, grid-scale energy storage, and freshwater production. Its OceanHydro Omni deep-sea offshore wind platform converts wind into mechanical lift with built-in storage; SubSea RO Wind couples wind energy directly to subsea reverse-osmosis desalination; and the Offshore AI Power Plant integrates both with floating data centres for off-grid AI infrastructure. The company also ships QuenchSea, a portable hand-powered desalination device deployed across 60+ countries. Backed by Techstars, Republic, and Shell StartUp Engine. The company publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Instabeat
providers.description: Instabeat is a San Francisco based swimming technology company that builds a heart-rate monitoring device integrated directly into swim goggles, giving swimmers real-time, color-coded effort feedback (heart-rate zones), automatic stroke detection, lap counting, pace, distance and rest-interval tracking without a chest strap or wrist watch. Paired with the Instabeat mobile app and myinstabeat.com, it delivers data-driven training insights so swimmers can adjust workouts in the water rather than after the session. The company sells the device through a Shopify storefront and has tested the product with 250+ swimmers across 56 countries. Added to the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio company; no public developer or API surface has been identified.

providers.name: Linear Labs
providers.description: Linear Labs is an industrial motor technology company headquartered in Fort Worth, Texas, building high-torque motor systems for wind, nuclear, pumps, actuators, mining, and defense applications. Its patented Hunstable Electric Turbine (HET) permanent-magnet architecture uses a circumferential flux design the company states delivers 2x torque density, 97% peak efficiency, and 50% weight reduction versus conventional motors, scaling from 10 kW to 2.2 MW. Its PitchPro 2000 is a complete pitch-system replacement for aging GE 1.5 wind turbines, pairing the HET motor with KEBA drive electronics, a Bachmann PLC controller, and ultracapacitor backup power. Linear Labs is a hardware manufacturer and publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable technical surface; this profile is maintained for network coverage and identity only.

providers.name: Linear Technology
providers.description: Linear Technology Corporation was an American semiconductor company founded in 1981 by Robert H. Swanson Jr. and Robert C. Dobkin and headquartered in Milpitas, California. It designed and manufactured high-performance analog integrated circuits across data conversion (ADCs and DACs), signal conditioning (operational amplifiers, comparators, voltage references), power management (switching and linear regulators, battery management, LED drivers), interface (RS232, RS485), radio frequency, oscillators, and space and military ICs, shipping a catalog of more than 7,500 products. Analog Devices agreed to acquire Linear Technology in July 2016 in a cash-and-stock deal valued at approximately $14.8 billion, and the acquisition closed on March 10, 2017. Linear Technology no longer operates as an independent company: the linear.com domain permanently redirects to Analog Devices, and the Linear name survives only as the "Power by Linear" product brand. Linear Technology publishes no independent developer portal, documentation, or API surface of its own; its developer-facing successor in this network is analog-devices.

providers.name: Linear Technology Corporation
providers.description: Linear Technology Corporation (listed as "Linear Technologies" in the Mayfield portfolio harvest) was an American analog semiconductor company founded in 1981 and headquartered in Milpitas, California, designing and manufacturing high-performance analog integrated circuits — power management, data converters, amplifiers, voltage references, interface and RF products — for industrial, automotive, communications, computing, and military/aerospace markets. Backed early by Mayfield and Kleiner Perkins, it went public on NASDAQ in 1986 under the ticker LLTC and was acquired by Analog Devices in March 2017. The company no longer operates independently: its linear.com domain 301-redirects to www.analog.com, and its product lines, datasheets, and design tools (including LTspice) are now distributed through Analog Devices. As an analog component manufacturer it never operated a web/developer API program, and no public API surface exists to enrich. This profile is retained as an acquired-company lead; the successor developer surface is catalogued in the API Evangelist network under analog-devices.

providers.name: Mogassam
providers.description: Mogassam is a digital dentistry company building all-in-one dental 3D printing hardware and software for chairside, single-visit treatment. Its products include the DentCase automated all-in-one 3D printer with integrated CAM, automatic washing, and post-curing, the Microdent 1 Pro printer, and the DentPrint dental 3D printing software, used to produce dentures, dental models, surgical guides, and provisional and permanent restorations. The company was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. No public API, SDK, or developer documentation was found at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Natron Energy
providers.description: Natron Energy was a Santa Clara, California sodium-ion battery company spun out of Stanford University in 2012 by Colin Wessells, building cells based on a Prussian blue analog (PBA) chemistry that promised long cycle life, fast charge and discharge, non-flammability, and a domestic supply chain free of lithium, cobalt, and nickel. Natron's product line was aimed at critical power and industrial backup applications, including the BlueTray 4000 — a 48 VDC, 4 kW (6 kW peak), 50 V rack-mounted sodium-ion battery tray — and the BlueRack 250 / 500 kW battery cabinets targeted at data center UPS, peak shaving, and EV fast-charging support. The company stood up the first U.S. sodium-ion mass-production line in Holland, Michigan in 2024 (a converted Clarios facility, ~600 MW/yr nameplate) and announced a planned $1.4 billion factory in Kingsboro (Rocky Mount), North Carolina that was expected to create more than 1,000 jobs. Investors included Khosla Ventures, Chevron Technology Ventures, United Airlines Ventures, Aramco Ventures, and Sherwood Partners. After ~$373M raised, on August 27, 2025 Natron's board determined that ongoing fundraising and order-pipeline efforts were unsuccessful; the company filed a WARN notice and permanently ceased operations on September 3, 2025, terminating staff at both the Holland, MI and Santa Clara, CA sites and cancelling the North Carolina factory. Sherwood Partners, the largest shareholder, took over wind-down and asset disposition. Natron was a battery hardware OEM with no public developer API, SDK, GitHub organization, or programmable cloud surface.

providers.name: NVision Imaging Technologies
providers.description: NVision Imaging Technologies (now operating as NVision Quantum Technologies) is a deep-tech healthcare company that engineers quantum technology at the molecular level. Its flagship POLARIS platform delivers quantum-enhanced MRI, boosting the magnetic signal of engineered sugar molecules by over 10,000x to image disease metabolism in real time, and its PIQC platform is a quantum-computing architecture built on molecular quantum nodes native to photonic chips. The company is backed by Playground Global. It publishes no public developer API, SDK, or technical integration surface; this profile carries identity and domain-security signals only.

providers.name: Oklo
providers.description: Oklo Inc. is a Santa Clara, California advanced fission company designing and deploying small modular reactors under the Aurora powerhouse brand. The Aurora is a liquid-metal (sodium) cooled, metal-fueled fast reactor derived from the Experimental Breeder Reactor-II (EBR-II) lineage, engineered as a "walk-away safe" passively cooled system that is self-stabilizing and self-controlling under loss-of-coolant and loss-of-shutdown conditions. Oklo's reactors are intended to run on recycled high-assay low-enriched uranium (HALEU) fuel, including legacy EBR-II material, with the company building out three vertically integrated fast-reactor businesses: clean power generation, advanced nuclear fuel fabrication and recycling, and medical radioisotope production. The first commercial Aurora is targeted for operation at Idaho National Laboratory (INL) in late 2027 to early 2028, supported by selection into the DOE Reactor Pilot Program and Fuel Line Pilot Projects, and the company has completed an NRC Phase 1 pre-application assessment. Oklo went public in May 2024 via merger with AltC Acquisition Corp (a SPAC co-founded by Sam Altman, who serves as chairman) and trades on the NYSE under ticker OKLO. Oklo's commercial posture is utility-scale and industrial — selling power, fuel cycle services, and isotopes to data center operators, defense customers, and industrial offtakers — and the company exposes no public developer API, SDK, or open source software.

providers.name: Orthocon
providers.description: Orthocon, now operating as Abyrx, is a surgical-therapeutics medical device company that has built a materials-science platform focused on therapeutic devices used during surgical procedures. Its portfolio centers on resorbable and hemostatic bone putties for orthopedic, trauma, spine, sports medicine, cranial, maxillofacial, and cardiothoracic applications, including AHBP (water-soluble hemostatic bone putty), the HemaSorb family (HemaSorb, HemaSorb Apply, HemaSorb Plus with HA/beta-TCP), and MONTAGE settable resorbable bone putty. The company sells directly to surgeons, hospitals, and distributors and does not operate a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or programmatic developer surface. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and enriched via the API Evangelist pipeline; the honest result is that there is no API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Panthalassa
providers.description: Panthalassa is a Portland, Oregon public-benefit corporation founded in 2016 that builds ocean wave-energy "nodes" — a buoyant sphere and central tube that convert deep-water wave motion into electricity in the open ocean. Rather than transmitting power to shore, the company pairs each node with sealed, seawater-cooled compute containers so the electrons power AI and data-center workloads at sea, backhauled over satellite link. It has run the Ocean-2 Pacific pilot and markets no public API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable contract; this profile records that absence and the company's public web surface.

providers.name: Petcube
providers.description: Petcube is a pet-technology company (a Y Combinator alum) that makes interactive Wi-Fi pet cameras and a companion mobile app for remote pet care. Its consumer hardware line includes the Petcube Cam, Bites treat-dispensing camera, and Play laser camera, offering HD video, night vision, two-way audio, motion and sound alerts, and app-controlled treat tossing and play. Petcube also sells the Care subscription (cloud video history, extended alerts) and Online Vet / Emergency Fund telehealth services. As of this enrichment pass Petcube exposes no public developer API, developer portal, or documented integration surface — the primary interface is the consumer iOS/Android app tied to its private cloud backend. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: Power Lattice
providers.description: Power Lattice (Powerlattice) is a semiconductor and power-management startup building power delivery solutions for AI accelerators and GPUs. Its core product is an industry-first power delivery chiplet that integrates voltage regulation directly into the processor package, addressing the data-center "power wall" as AI chips push past 2,000 watts. The Rainier micro-IVR architecture combines miniaturized on-die magnetic inductors, advanced control-circuit innovations, a vertical design, and a programmable software layer to deliver 50%+ power reduction, 2-3X performance-per-watt gains, and extended system lifetime. Backed by Playground Global, the company raised $25M to break the AI power wall. This is a hardware company with no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Prismlab
providers.description: Prismlab (Shanghai Prismlab Technology / 上海普利生) is an industrial-grade 3D printing equipment provider founded in Shanghai, China, and a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. The company develops high-precision additive manufacturing systems built on its proprietary SMS (Scan-Mode Slicing / sub-pixel micro-scanning) photocuring technology, including the Rapid 600 and Rapid 400 industrial printer series, the SP high-accuracy series, and MP micro-nano printers for research. Its systems serve dental and orthodontics (clear aligners, dentures), precision medical devices, jewelry, education and research, electronics, and mold/prototype manufacturing. As a B2B hardware manufacturer, Prismlab publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures identity and a live domain-security probe.

providers.name: Pseudolithic
providers.description: PseudolithIC is a semiconductor company specializing in heterogeneous integration technology for cost-effective, high-performance silicon RFICs (radio frequency integrated circuits). The company combines compound semiconductor chiplets with large-diameter, low-cost silicon wafers to deliver mm-wave power amplifiers, low-noise amplifiers, and transmit/receive (T/R) front-end modules for RF and wireless applications. PseudolithIC is a hardware/chipset manufacturer targeting the RF and semiconductor industries; it publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or programmatic surface. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Uncork Capital and profiled in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Pulse Space
providers.description: Pulse (Pulse - Space Power Solutions) is a Techstars-backed space technology company building power solutions for spacecraft and satellites. The company operates a WebGL marketing site at pulsespace.com and, as of this enrichment pass, publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API specifications. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; enrichment probing confirmed a marketing-only web presence (TLS 1.3 with HSTS) and no developer or API surface to harvest.

providers.name: Radiant
providers.description: Radiant is a nuclear technology company developing portable, transportable microreactors designed to deliver clean, reliable power to remote sites, military installations, disaster-relief operations, and industrial locations that today depend on diesel generators. Its flagship Kaleidos reactor is a factory-built, containerized ~1 MW microreactor intended to ship by truck, plane, or ship and be operational quickly on-site. Founded by former SpaceX engineers and headquartered in El Segundo, California, Radiant is backed by DCVC and Union Square Ventures. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a corporate and careers web presence but no public developer program, API, SDK, or technical documentation surface.
